cards.enTarget: When people who tried a new study method are asked for their impressions, many answer that their mood lifted before any results appeared.

words.defJa: 得することと損することの計算

cards.ja: 言葉を選ぶとき、私たちはしばしば損得勘定で動いている。「結構です」の一言が断りにも承諾にも聞こえるのは、相手との関係を壊さずに自分の立場を守るためだ。日本語の曖昧さは、そうした計算の積み重ねから生まれたとも言えよう。しかしこの曖昧さに安易に頼りすぎれば、肝心の本心が伝わらない恐れもある。だからこそ、打算を離れて本音を語る場面には、普段は隠れている言葉の本当の力が現れるのである。
cards.en: When choosing words, we often act on calculations of profit and loss. The reason a single remark like that's fine can sound like either refusal or acceptance is to protect one's position without damaging the relationship. One could say the ambiguity of Japanese was born from an accumulation of such calculations. But if we rely too easily on this ambiguity, there is a risk that our real feelings, the very point, will not get across. That is exactly why, in moments of speaking one's true mind apart from calculation, the real power of words that usually stays hidden appears.

cards.tipJa: 「損得勘定」「損得抜きで」。利害を計算する場面に使う。
cards.enTarget: When choosing words, we often act on calculations of profit and loss.

words.defJa: 筋道が合わないこと

cards.ja: 『韓非子』には、楚の商人が「どんな盾も突き通す矛」と「どんな矛も防ぐ盾」を同時に売り歩いたという話がある。客に「ではその矛でその盾を突いたらどうなる」と尋ねられ、商人は答えに詰まった。この故事から、つじつまの合わない状態を矛盾と呼ぶようになり、今では政治の議論から日常の口論に至るまで広く使われている。矛と盾という具体的な道具が、抽象的な論理の言葉に化けた例である。
cards.en: The Han Feizi tells of a merchant of Chu who went around selling both a spear that could pierce any shield and a shield that could stop any spear. When a customer asked what would happen if that spear struck that shield, the merchant was left without an answer. From this tale, a state where things do not add up came to be called mujun, and today it is widely used from political debate to everyday quarrels. It is an example of concrete tools, a spear and a shield, turning into a word of abstract logic.

cards.enTarget: From this tale, a state where things do not add up came to be called mujun, and today it is widely used from political debate to everyday quarrels.

words.defJa: 舞台や物語に姿を現すこと

cards.ja: 新しい習慣が生活に登場すれば、古い習慣は席を譲らざるを得ない。だが、相手は黙って去ってくれるわけではない。早起きを始めようと決意すると、夜更かしという悪癖が、あれこれと理由をつけて反撃してくる。習慣とは、意志の弱さの問題である以前に、脳が省エネのために選んできた回路なのである。だからこそ、新しい行動は、古い行動の置き換えとして、前もって丁寧に設計する必要がある。
cards.en: When a new habit enters your life, an old habit has no choice but to give up its seat. But the other does not go quietly. When you try to start rising early, the bad habit of staying up late counterattacks with one excuse after another. A habit is, before it is a matter of weak will, a circuit the brain has chosen to save energy. That is exactly why a new behavior must be carefully designed in advance as a replacement for an old one.

cards.enTarget: When a new habit enters your life, an old habit has no choice but to give up its seat.

words.defJa: 活気にあふれて元気なさま

cards.ja: 退職をきっかけに畑を借りて野菜を育て始めた人たちが、現役のころより生き生きしていると、地域の高齢者支援の担当者は話す。毎朝決まった時刻に畑へ出る習慣が、生活のリズムを整えているのだという。借り賃が手頃で、収穫物を近所に配る楽しみもあり、会話の相手が増えたことが気持ちの張りにつながっているようだ。心理学では、役割と日課を持つことが、心の健康を保つ大きな支えになると考えられている。
cards.en: People who rented a plot and began growing vegetables after retirement are livelier than when they were working, says a local official in charge of supporting the elderly. The habit of going out to the field at a set time each morning is said to be setting the rhythm of daily life. The rent is affordable, there is the pleasure of handing out the harvest to neighbors, and having more people to talk to seems to be linked to a sense of vigor. In psychology, having a role and a routine is considered a major support for keeping mental health.

words.defJa: 注意や関心の集まる中心

cards.ja: 話が散らかる原因の多くは、焦点が決まっていないことにある。話し始める前に、聞き手に持ち帰ってほしい一点を決めておくに越したことはない。その一点は、箇条書きにせず、一文で言えるかどうか試してみるとよい。言えないなら、材料がどれほど面白くても、聞き手の頭には何も残らない。写真を撮る前にレンズのピントを合わせるのと同じで、順序を間違えると、あとの努力が報われにくい。
cards.en: Much of what makes a talk scattered is that its focus has not been decided. Before you begin, it never hurts to decide the one point you want your listeners to take home. Try seeing whether you can state that one point in a single sentence rather than as a bulleted list. If you cannot, however interesting your material, nothing will remain in the listener's head. Just as you set the focus before taking a photograph, if you get the order wrong, the effort that follows is hard to reward.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: まっていないことにある。
cards.tipJa: 「焦点を絞る」「焦点が定まる」。話や議論の中心を写真のピントにたとえる。
cards.enTarget: Much of what makes a talk scattered is that its focus has not been decided.

words.defJa: 地位や年齢が自分より下の人

cards.ja: 話し方に人柄が出るのは、目下の人に向かって話すときである。上役には誰もが丁寧に話すが、立場の弱い相手にも率直で礼儀正しい調子を保てる人は、案外少ない。『論語』には、孔子がある重臣を評して、下の者に教えを請うことを恥じない人だと述べた箇所がある。言葉づかいは、相手を映す鏡である以前に、自分の器を映す鏡なのだ。下の者への一言には、その人の日ごろの心がけが、隠しようもなく表れる。
cards.en: A person's character shows in how they speak to those beneath them. Everyone speaks politely to a superior, but few people can keep a frank and courteous tone even with someone in a weaker position. In the Analects, there is a passage where Confucius, assessing a certain high official, says he was a man who was not ashamed to seek instruction from those below him. Your choice of words is a mirror of your own caliber before it is a mirror of the other person. A single remark to someone below reveals, unmistakably, the speaker's everyday attitude.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 対義語は「目上」。ここでは「もっか（今のところ）」ではなく「めした」と読む。
cards.sense: 地位や年齢が下の人（目上の対）
cards.enTarget: A person's character shows in how they speak to those beneath them.

words.defJa: 程度がいっそう深くなる

cards.ja: 訪日客の増加とともに、日本語を学ぶ外国人が各地の教室に集まるようになった。授業を重ねるうちに敬語の使い分けへの関心が深まり、「なぜ同じ『食べる』に三つの言い方があるのか」と率直に尋ねる受講生が増えたという。教える側も、文法の説明だけでは足りないと感じ、場面ごとの会話練習を取り入れつつある。言葉への理解は、辞書の中ではなく、使う場面を知ってはじめて確かなものになる。
cards.en: As visitors to Japan increase, more foreigners studying Japanese are filling classrooms in various places. As lessons accumulate, interest in using honorifics correctly has deepened, and more students are reportedly asking frankly, "Why are there three ways to say 'eat'?" Teachers, too, feel that explaining grammar alone is not enough and are bringing in conversation practice for each setting. Understanding of a language becomes solid not in the dictionary but only when you know the situations in which it is used.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「関心・理解・対立・秋」が深まる。自然に程度が増す変化を表す自動詞。
cards.enTarget: As lessons accumulate, interest in using honorifics correctly has deepened, and more students are reportedly asking frankly, "Why are there three ways to say 'eat'?"

words.defJa: 色や行動が目立って華やかなこと

cards.ja: 新しいチップの発表会って、毎回やたら派手じゃないですか。照明を落としたステージに経営者が革ジャンで登場して、棒グラフがどーんと映る。でも本当に見るべきなのは演出じゃなくて、電力あたりの性能なんですよね。華やかな売り文句に釣られて買ったら、速いどころか、前の機種とほとんど変わらなかったって話も聞きますよ。宣伝の上手さと製品の出来は、案外まったく別のものだったりします。
cards.en: Chip launch events are always weirdly flashy, aren't they? An executive walks onto a darkened stage in a leather jacket and a huge bar chart flashes up. But what you should really look at isn't the show, it's the performance per watt. I've even heard of people who fell for the glossy sales pitch, bought one, and found it was hardly different from the previous model, let alone faster. Skill at promotion and the quality of the product can turn out to be quite separate things.

ruby: のものだったりします。
cards.tipJa: 演出や見た目が目立つさま。「派手な〜」「派手に〜する」の形でよく使う。
cards.enTarget: Chip launch events are always weirdly flashy, aren't they?

words.defJa: 食事に出す料理の組み合わせ

cards.ja: 歴史の年号を覚えるとき、献立にたとえる人がいます。主菜は大きな出来事、副菜は人物、汁物は背景というように、食卓に並べて整理するのです。実際、江戸時代の武家の宴席に出された本膳料理は、飯と汁と菜を決まった位置に置く厳格な配置でした。位置が決まっていればこそ、並べ方そのものが記憶の手がかりになります。バラバラの知識も、置き場所を与えれば取り出しやすくなるんです。
cards.en: Some people compare memorizing historical dates to a menu. Main dish for the big event, side dish for the person, soup for the background; you arrange them on the table to organize them. Indeed, the honzen cuisine served at samurai banquets in the Edo period had a strict layout, with rice, soup and side dishes in fixed positions. Precisely because the positions are fixed, the arrangement itself becomes a clue for memory. Even scattered knowledge becomes easier to retrieve once you give it a place to sit.

ruby: がかりになります。バラバラの
cards.tipJa: 「今日の献立」「献立を立てる」。食事の料理の組み合わせや予定を指す。
cards.enTarget: Some people compare memorizing historical dates to a menu.

words.defJa: かざらず正直なさま

cards.ja: ラマナ・マハルシは、弟子の質問に驚くほど率直に答えた人でした。弟子たちが懸命に修行法を尋ねても、彼の答えはいつも同じで、「私とは誰か」と自分自身に問いなさい、というものです。難しい理論を並べるかわりに、問いそのものを差し出したのです。答えは外の本ではなく、問いを向けた先の自分の内側にある、というのが彼の立場でした。知識を積むより、問う人自身を見つめよという教えは、アドヴァイタの伝統にも深く根ざしています。
cards.en: Ramana Maharshi was a man who answered his disciples' questions with striking frankness. However earnestly they asked about methods of practice, his answer was always the same: ask yourself, "Who am I?" Instead of laying out difficult theory, he handed over the question itself. His position was that the answer lies not in outside books but within oneself, where the question is directed. A teaching that says to look at the one who asks rather than pile up knowledge is also deeply rooted in the Advaita tradition.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: いなさい、というものです。
cards.tipJa: 「率直に言う」「率直な意見」。遠回しにせず正直に伝える態度。
cards.enTarget: Ramana Maharshi was a man who answered his disciples' questions with striking frankness.

words.defJa: 体の表面をおおう組織

cards.ja: インドの伝統医学アーユルヴェーダには、ウコンやニームを使った皮膚の手入れの知恵が数多く伝わっている。近年は、こうした素材を使った化粧品や石けんが、国内市場に加えて海外でも売り上げを伸ばしている。ただし、伝統的な使い方がすべて科学的に裏づけられているわけではなく、成分の濃度や安全性の測定は、依然として課題とされる。消費者に求められるのは、歴史の長さを根拠に過信せず、表示を確かめる冷静さである。
cards.en: Ayurveda, India's traditional medicine, passes down a great deal of knowledge about skin care using turmeric and neem. In recent years cosmetics and soaps using such ingredients have been increasing sales abroad in addition to the domestic market. However, not every traditional use is scientifically backed, and the concentration of ingredients and the measurement of safety remain issues. What is asked of consumers is the calm to check the labels rather than overtrust a product on the length of its history.

づけられているわけではなく、
cards.tipJa: 「皮膚炎」「皮膚科」「皮膚感覚」。医学や化粧品の文脈で使う硬めの語。
cards.enTarget: Ayurveda, India's traditional medicine, passes down a great deal of knowledge about skin care using turmeric and neem.

words.defJa: 新聞や雑誌を初めて出すこと

cards.ja: 新聞や雑誌の発刊は、世界史の資料問題でよく問われます。たとえば日本では、一八七二年に東京日日新聞が創刊されたのをはじめ、各地で新聞が相次いで生まれ、文明開化の空気の中で新しいメディアが広がりました。覚えるときは、年号だけを暗記するのではなく、なぜその時期に出されたのかを短く一言添えておくのがコツです。背景とセットにした知識は、問われ方が変わっても応用が利きます。
cards.en: The launch of newspapers and magazines is often asked about in source questions on world history. In Japan, for example, starting with the Tokyo Nichinichi Shimbun in 1872, newspapers appeared one after another in various places, and a new medium spread in the atmosphere of civilization and enlightenment. When memorizing, the trick is not just to cram the year but to add a phrase on why it was launched at that time. Knowledge paired with its background can be applied even if the question is worded differently.

ruby: するのではなく、なぜその
えておくのがコツです。
cards.tipJa: 「創刊」とほぼ同じ。「月刊誌を発刊する」「発刊の辞」など出版で使う。
cards.enTarget: The launch of newspapers and magazines is often asked about in source questions on world history.

words.defJa: 県の行政を行う役所

cards.ja: 一八七一年の廃藩置県によって、それまでの藩は県に置き換えられ、各地に県庁が置かれた。中央政府が任命した官吏が派遣され、行政の中央集権化に伴って、地方の統治は一気に国の管理下に入った。その所在地には、旧藩の城下町がそのまま選ばれた例が多く、今日の県都の多くにその名残が見られる。のちに役所が別の都市へ移転した例もあるが、全体としては、旧藩の骨格が現在の地図に生きている。その後の統廃合を経て、県の数と区域は現在の四十七都道府県に落ち着いた。
cards.en: With the abolition of the domains and establishment of prefectures in 1871, the former domains were replaced by prefectures and prefectural offices were set up across the land. Officials appointed by the central government were dispatched, and with the centralization of administration, local governance came under national control all at once. In many cases the old castle town of a domain was chosen as the seat, and traces of this remain in many of today's prefectural capitals. There are cases where the office later moved to another city, but overall the skeleton of the old domains lives on in today's map. Through later mergers and reorganizations, the number and areas of prefectures settled at today's forty-seven.

cards.tipJa: 「県庁所在地」「県庁職員」。県の行政の中心となる役所とその建物。
cards.enTarget: With the abolition of the domains and establishment of prefectures in 1871, the former domains were replaced by prefectures and prefectural offices were set up across the land.

words.meaning: to float; to be left over
words.defJa: 水面や空中にとどまる。余りが出る

cards.ja: 生成AIが議事録や下書きを肩代わりしてくれるようになり、一日に浮く時間は確実に増えた。ところが、その時間で人は本当に考えているだろうか。空いた余白をすぐ別の作業で埋めてしまうなら、効率化は深い思索をもたらすどころか、忙しさを増すだけに終わる。節約された時間は、使い道を問われてはじめて意義を持つのである。少し立ち止まって何もしない時間を持てるかどうかが、これからの知的な贅沢を分けるだろう。
cards.en: Generative AI now takes over the minutes and the first drafts, and the time freed up each day has certainly grown. But are people really using that time to think? If the spare room is immediately filled with other tasks, efficiency brings not deep reflection but only more busyness. Saved time takes on meaning only once we are asked what it is for. Whether one can pause and keep some time to do nothing may well separate the intellectual luxuries of the years ahead.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: わりしてくれるようになり、
てるかどうかが、これからの
cards.tipJa: 「時間・お金・費用が浮く」は余りが出る意味。水に浮く意味とは別の用法。
cards.sense: 余りが出る（時間・お金が浮く）
cards.enTarget: Generative AI now takes over the minutes and the first drafts, and the time freed up each day has certainly grown.

words.defJa: 目当て。ねらった目的

cards.ja: 文章を書くとき、最初に問うべきなのは、何を書くかではなく、何のために書くかである。その狙いがはっきりしない文章は、どれほど美しい言葉を並べても、読み終えたあとに何も残らない。逆に、目的が一つに絞られていれば、控え目な表現や多少ぎこちない言い回しでも、読者は最後まで運ばれていく。名文の技巧とは、その目的に仕えているにすぎない。書き手が磨くべきは、飾りより先に、この一点なのである。
cards.en: When you write, the first thing to ask is not what to write but what you are writing for. A piece whose aim is unclear leaves nothing behind once it has been read, however beautiful the words lined up. Conversely, if the purpose is narrowed to one thing, readers are carried to the end even by modest phrasing or somewhat awkward turns. The craft of fine prose is nothing more than serving that purpose. What a writer should polish, before any ornament, is this one point.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「狙いは〜にある」「狙いを定める」。もともとは的に向ける意味から。
cards.enTarget: A piece whose aim is unclear leaves nothing behind once it has been read, however beautiful the words lined up.

words.defJa: 役所などに願い出ること

cards.ja: 制度を覚えるのが苦手な人は、「誰が、誰に、何を申請するのか」という形に直しておくと、制度を整理する上で役に立ちます。たとえば江戸初期の朱印船貿易は、商人が幕府に願い出て朱印状を受け取らなければ、海外へ渡れない仕組みでした。この場合、願い出る側は商人、許可を出す側は幕府です。登場人物と動作を決めてしまえば、制度は一つの小さな物語になります。年号の暗記より先に、こうした骨組みを押さえておくと、応用も利きます。
cards.en: If you find institutions hard to memorize, recasting them as "who applies to whom for what" helps you organize them. For example, early Edo red-seal ship trade was a system in which merchants could not go abroad unless they petitioned the shogunate and received a red-seal permit. In this case the petitioner is the merchant and the one who grants permission is the shogunate. Once you fix the characters and the action, an institution becomes one small story. Grasping this framework before cramming years makes it easier to apply.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「申請書」「ビザを申請する」。役所への正式な願い出を表す。
cards.enTarget: If you find institutions hard to memorize, recasting them as "who applies to whom for what" helps you organize them.

words.defJa: 水中や物の下に入る。人目を避けて隠れる

cards.ja: 江戸幕府が禁教令を出したあと、日本の信者たちは、表向きは仏教徒を装いながら信仰を守り続けました。彼らは社会の表から姿を消し、人目につかない暮らしの底に潜る道を選んだのです。家の納戸には聖母に見立てた観音像を祀り、祈りの言葉は口伝えで残しました。約二百五十年を経た一八六五年、長崎の大浦天主堂で、その子孫たちが神父に信仰を打ち明けました。外から見えない信仰が世代を超えて受け継がれた例として、世界史上の意義が大きい出来事です。
cards.en: After the shogunate issued its ban on Christianity, believers in Japan kept their faith while outwardly posing as Buddhists. They vanished from the surface of society and chose to sink into a life that drew no attention. In the storerooms of their homes they enshrined Kannon figures made to stand for the Virgin, and kept their prayers alive by word of mouth. After about 250 years, in 1865, their descendants confessed their faith to a priest at Oura Church in Nagasaki. It is an event of great significance in world history as an example of a faith invisible from outside being handed down across generations.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「地下に潜る」「人混みに潜る」。水中以外に、人目を避けて隠れる意味も持つ。
cards.sense: 人目を避けて隠れる
cards.enTarget: They vanished from the surface of society and chose to sink into a life that drew no attention.

words.defJa: 物質の含まれる割合

cards.ja: 半導体の工場では、空気中の微粒子の濃度が厳しく管理されている。最先端のチップを作るクリーンルームでは、一立方メートルあたりの粒子の数を測定し、基準を外れれば工程を見直す。髪の毛の太さの千分の一にも満たない塵が、回路の線を断ち切ってしまうからだ。作業服から清掃の手順に至るまで、細かな決まりが定められている。製品の品質は、目に見えない空気の質に静かに支えられている。
cards.en: In semiconductor plants, the concentration of fine particles in the air is tightly controlled. In the clean rooms where cutting-edge chips are made, the number of particles per cubic meter is measured and the process is reviewed if it falls outside the standard. This is because dust less than a thousandth of the thickness of a hair can sever the lines of a circuit. Detailed rules are set from work garments all the way to cleaning procedures. The quality of the product rests on the quality of air that cannot be seen.

cards.tipJa: 「濃度が高い／低い」「二酸化炭素濃度」。溶けているものや含まれる量の割合。
cards.enTarget: In semiconductor plants, the concentration of fine particles in the air is tightly controlled.

words.defJa: 夏に着る木綿の和服

cards.ja: 夏祭りの夜、浴衣姿の人々が提灯の灯る川沿いをそぞろ歩く光景は、いまや日本の風物詩である。もともとは貴族が蒸し風呂に入るときに着た湯帷子が起源とされ、江戸時代に銭湯が広まるのに伴って、風呂上がりの普段着として庶民に定着した。花火大会に着ていくようになったのはさらに後のことで、今では手頃な値段で揃える人も多い。衣服の意味は、着る場所や季節を移りながら、静かに変わってゆくものである。
cards.en: On a summer festival night, the sight of people strolling along the lantern-lit river in yukata has become a seasonal fixture of Japan. It is said to originate in the bath garment that nobles wore in steam baths, and as public baths spread in the Edo period it took hold among ordinary people as casual wear after a bath. Wearing it to fireworks displays came much later, and today many people buy a set at a reasonable price. The meaning of a garment shifts quietly as it moves through the places and seasons in which it is worn.

ruby: ていくようになったのはさらに
わってゆくものである。
cards.tipJa: 風呂上がりの普段着から夏祭りの装いへ。起源と用途の変化がこの語の背景。
cards.enTarget: On a summer festival night, the sight of people strolling along the lantern-lit river in yukata has become a seasonal fixture of Japan.

words.defJa: 場所や所有を移すこと

cards.ja: 歴史の年表には、「遷都」と単なる引っ越しとが、ごちゃ混ぜになって出てくることがあります。たとえば七九四年に桓武天皇が都を平安京に移した出来事は、一般に遷都と呼ばれます。一方、現代のニュースで首都機能の移転が議論されるとき、それは建物や省庁の引っ越しを指すことが多いです。文脈に応じて、政治的な意義を帯びた語なのか、物理的な移動を指す語なのかを見分けると、用語が整理されます。
cards.en: In historical chronologies, the relocation of a capital and a mere move sometimes appear jumbled together. For example, Emperor Kanmu's moving the capital to Heian-kyo in 794 is generally called a transfer of the capital. By contrast, when the relocation of capital functions is debated in today's news, it often means moving buildings and ministries. Depending on context, if you distinguish whether a word carries political significance or refers to physical movement, the terms fall into order.

cards.enTarget: By contrast, when the relocation of capital functions is debated in today's news, it often means moving buildings and ministries.

words.defJa: 折り重ねて小さくする。店などを閉じる

cards.ja: 商店街の八百屋が、長年の営業を終えて店を畳むことになった。この動詞はもともと衣類を折りたたむ動作を指すが、広げていたものを小さくして片づける、という意味が転じて、廃業や会議の終結にも使われるようになった。傘や布団の扱いに加えて、商売の幕引きまで一語で言い表せるのは、日本語の比喩の力といえる。店主は最終日に、店への愛着を語る常連客一人ひとりに頭を下げて見送った。
cards.en: A greengrocer on the shopping street has decided to close its shop after long years in business. This verb originally refers to folding clothes, but its sense of making something that was spread out small and tidying it away has extended to closing a business or ending a meeting. That one word can express both handling an umbrella or futon and the end of a business is a sign of the power of Japanese metaphor. On the last day, the owner bowed to each regular customer who spoke of their attachment to the shop and saw them off.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 衣類・傘を畳むのほか、「店を畳む」は廃業の意味。広げたものを小さくする核。
cards.sense: 店などを閉じる（廃業する）
cards.enTarget: A greengrocer on the shopping street has decided to close its shop after long years in business.

words.meaning: to run into; to hit a wall
words.defJa: 進んでいって行き止まりにぶつかる

cards.ja: 日本の新幹線方式を採用するインドの高速鉄道計画は、ムンバイとアーメダバードを結ぶ路線で建設が段階的に進められている。しかし、用地の取得や住民の移転をめぐる地元との交渉に突き当たり、工期は当初の予定から大きく遅れることになった。インド政府は理解を求めてきたが、対立が完全に解けたとは言いがたい。巨大な計画ほど、技術の問題より、人の暮らしとの折り合いに思わぬ壁が現れやすい。
cards.en: India’s high-speed rail project, which adopts the Japanese Shinkansen system, is being constructed in stages on a line linking Mumbai and Ahmedabad. But it ran into negotiations with locals over land acquisition and resettlement, and the schedule slipped well behind the original plan. The Indian government has sought understanding, but it can hardly be said that the dispute has been completely resolved. The bigger the project, the more readily unexpected walls appear not in technology but in the need to reconcile with people’s lives.

れることになった。インド

cards.enTarget: But it ran into negotiations with locals over land acquisition and resettlement, and the schedule slipped well behind the original plan.

words.defJa: 魚や貝をとる産業

cards.ja: 衛星画像と機械学習を使えば、海の上で何が起きているかを、人間の目よりも広く見張ることができる。たとえば違法な漁業は、船が位置信号を切って闇に紛れても、動きのパターンから見破られるようになってきた。技術は、海の監視という長年の難題に、ようやく手が届く形を与えたのである。とはいえ、監視できることと、取り締まれることは別の問題だ。指定された海域で何が見えたとしても、それにどう応えるかは、最後まで人間の判断にかかっている。
cards.en: With satellite imagery and machine learning, what is happening on the sea can be watched over a wider area than human eyes could cover. Illegal fishing, for example, has come to be detected from movement patterns even when a vessel switches off its position signal and slips into the dark. Technology has finally given the long-standing problem of monitoring the ocean a shape within reach. That said, being able to monitor and being able to enforce are separate matters. Even when something is seen in a designated sea area, how to respond rests with human judgment to the end.

words.meaning: to glare at; to keep an eye on
words.defJa: 鋭く見る。警戒して見張る

cards.ja: インドは、隣国の軍事的な動きを睨む形で、国境地帯の道路や空港の整備を急いでいる。ヒマラヤの標高の高い地域でも、年間を通じて物資を運べる道が増えれば、兵站の負担は大きく変わると、政府筋はみる。一方で、こうした整備は周辺の自然環境に影響を及ぼす恐れがあり、地元住民からは懸念の声も上がっている。安全保障と環境の両立は、今後も長く、難しい課題であり続けるだろう。計画の是非は、地図の上ではなく、現地の暮らしの中で問われることになる。
cards.en: India is rushing to build up roads and airports in border areas with an eye on a neighbor's military movements. Even in high Himalayan regions, if more roads can carry supplies all year round, the burden of logistics would change greatly, government sources believe. On the other hand, such development risks affecting the surrounding natural environment, and local residents have raised concerns. Balancing security and the environment will remain a difficult issue for a long time. The merits of a plan will be tested not on the map but in the daily lives of the places concerned.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.enTarget: India is rushing to build up roads and airports in border areas with an eye on a neighbor's military movements.

words.defJa: 力を加えて細かくする

cards.ja: 半導体の材料になる高純度のシリコンは、棒状に育てた塊を砕いて小さな破片にしてから、るつぼで溶かされる。原料のほんのわずかな汚れが、のちの回路の性能を左右するため、濃度のごく低い不純物さえ許されない。そこから作られた円柱状の巨大な結晶を薄く切り出したものが、いわゆるウェハーである。原料はもちろん、作業に使う道具に至るまで、工程のはじめから細心の注意が払われている。
cards.en: High-purity silicon, the material of semiconductors, is smashed from rods grown as blocks into small fragments before being melted in a crucible. Because a slight contamination of the raw material affects the performance of the circuits later, even impurities at very low concentration are not tolerated. The enormous cylindrical crystal made from it, sliced thin, is what is called a wafer. From the raw material to the tools used in the work, the utmost care is taken from the very start of the process.

words.defJa: 器具で長さや量を測ること

cards.ja: 日本語の話す速さを測定するときは、文字数ではなく、拍の数で数えるのが一般的である。拍とは、「きって」が「き」「っ」「て」の三つに数えられるような、一定の長さの音の単位をいう。この方法を通して、同じ人でも朗読と雑談では速さが変わることが、数字で確かめられる。速さの数字は有力な手がかりだが、それだけでは、聞き手が聞き取りやすいと感じるかどうかまでは分からない。間の取り方も、同じくらい重要な要素である。
cards.en: When measuring how fast Japanese is spoken, it is usual to count morae rather than characters. A mora is a unit of sound of fixed length, as when kitte is counted as three: ki, small tsu and te. Through this method it can be confirmed in numbers that even the same person speaks at different speeds when reading aloud and when chatting. The speed figure is a strong clue, but by itself it cannot tell us whether listeners find the speech easy to follow. How pauses are placed is an element just as important.

words.defJa: ごみやよごれを取り除くこと

cards.ja: ガンディーは、自分の使う便所の清掃を、他人任せにしなかったことで知られています。話し方を磨きたい人にも、この逸話から学べることがあります。人に何かを呼びかけるとき、言葉の説得力を決めるのは、声の大きさというより、語る本人が何を実践しているかです。どれほど見事な話を披露しても、行いが伴わなければ、聞き手はすぐに見抜きます。便所掃除のような地味な行いこそ、言葉に重みを与える土台になるのです。
cards.en: Gandhi is known for not leaving the cleaning of the latrine he used to others. Those who want to polish their way of speaking can also learn something from this anecdote. When you appeal to people, what decides the persuasiveness of your words is not the volume of your voice but what the speaker is practicing. However brilliant a speech you give, if your conduct does not match, listeners see through it at once. Plain deeds like cleaning a toilet are the very foundation that gives words weight.

cards.enTarget: Gandhi is known for not leaving the cleaning of the latrine he used to others.

words.defJa: 謝る気持ちを表す。言いわけが立たない

cards.ja: 誤回答で利用者に損害が出たとき、「申し訳ない」と頭を下げるだけでは、企業の説明責任は果たせない。「システムの不具合により」という主語のない言い方は、人間の判断の誤りを機械の問題にすり替えてしまう。二〇二四年には、カナダの航空会社がチャットボットの誤案内をめぐって、賠償を命じられた。故意ではなくとも、AIを導入する以上、その発言が生む信頼の損失は企業が負うほかない。
cards.en: When a wrong answer causes a user harm, bowing and saying "I'm sorry" is not enough to discharge a company's accountability. The subjectless phrasing "due to a system malfunction" swaps a human error of judgment for a problem of the machine. In 2024, a Canadian airline was ordered to pay damages over incorrect guidance from its chatbot. Even if it was not intentional, once a company adopts AI, it has no choice but to bear the loss of trust that AI's statements create.

words.defJa: 進んで働きかけないさま

cards.ja: インド哲学の「無執着」という教えは、消極的な生き方だと誤解されがちです。ところがヨーガの教えでは、損得の計算や結果への執着を手放すことこそが、行動を最も力強くするとされます。『バガヴァッド・ギーター』で、戦士アルジュナは戦うことをためらいますが、クリシュナは行為そのものを捧げ物として果たせと説きます。何もしないのではなく、実りを求めずにやり抜く、これが彼の言う道です。
cards.en: The Indian teaching of non-attachment tends to be misread as a passive way of life. Yet in yoga, letting go of calculations of gain and loss and of attachment to results is said to make action most powerful. In the Bhagavad Gita, the warrior Arjuna hesitates to fight, but Krishna tells him to carry out the act itself as an offering. It is not doing nothing but seeing it through without seeking the fruit, and that is the path he describes.

cards.enTarget: The Indian teaching of non-attachment tends to be misread as a passive way of life.

words.defJa: たがいに働きかけ合うこと

cards.ja: 心と体は、どちらか一方が他方を動かす主従の関係ではなく、相互に影響を及ぼし合っている。緊張すれば胃を痛め、胃を痛めれば気分が沈む。この循環は、心と体をあたかも別々のものであるかのように扱ってきた近代の見方に、静かな疑問を投げかける。仏教が古くから心身を一つの流れとして捉えてきたのは、こうした実感に根ざしていたからであろう。身体の感覚を整える修行が心を静めるのも、この循環を逆向きに使っているからだ。
cards.en: Mind and body are not in a master-and-servant relation where one moves the other; they influence each other mutually. Tension upsets the stomach, and an upset stomach sinks the mood. This cycle quietly questions the modern view that has treated mind and body as if they were separate things. That Buddhism has long grasped mind and body as one flow was probably rooted in just this kind of felt reality. That practices which regulate bodily sensation calm the mind is because they use this cycle in reverse.

cards.enTarget: Mind and body are not in a master-and-servant relation where one moves the other; they influence each other mutually.

words.defJa: 座敷の広さを数える単位

cards.ja: 受験勉強をするなら、広い部屋より狭い部屋のほうが集中できる、という人は少なくありません。たとえば六畳ほどの部屋に机と本棚だけを揃えれば、視界に入る誘惑がぐっと減ります。環境を絞り込むと、意志の力に頼らなくても、やるべきことに自然と目が向くようになるのです。勉強の質は、時間の長さに限らず、場の設計によっても決まります。机の上に何も置かないという小さな工夫も、同じ発想です。
cards.en: Some people say that for exam study a small room helps concentration more than a big one. For example, if you furnish a room of about six tatami with only a desk and a bookshelf, the temptations in your field of view drop sharply. When you narrow down the environment, your eyes turn naturally to what you must do, even without relying on willpower. The quality of study is decided not only by how long you work but also by how the place is designed. The small trick of putting nothing on the desk comes from the same idea.

cards.enTarget: For example, if you furnish a room of about six tatami with only a desk and a bookshelf, the temptations in your field of view drop sharply.

words.defJa: 持つ力を十分に表に出すこと

cards.ja: 『バガヴァッド・ギーター』は、戦場で迷うアルジュナに、結果への執着を手放して行為そのものに集中せよ、と教えます。この態度は、現代の私たちが仕事で実力を発揮する場面にも、そのまま通じます。結果ばかり気にすると、体が固まって本来の力は出ません。損得に気を取られることなく目の前の動作に没頭したときにこそ、人は最もよく働くのです。二千年ほど前に成立した教えが、集中状態の研究と重なると指摘されることもあります。
cards.en: The Bhagavad Gita teaches Arjuna, wavering on the battlefield, to let go of attachment to results and concentrate on the act itself. This attitude applies directly to those of us who need to bring out our abilities at work today. If you fixate only on results, your body stiffens and your real strength does not come out. It is when we are absorbed in the movement in front of us, without being distracted by gain and loss, that we work best. It is sometimes pointed out that a teaching composed roughly two thousand years ago overlaps with research on states of deep focus.

cards.enTarget: This attitude applies directly to those of us who need to bring out our abilities at work today.

words.defJa: 普通と違って特別なさま

cards.ja: 勉強が得意な人って、生まれつきの、何か特殊な才能があるように見えますよね。でも学習科学の研究では、成績を分けるのは、才能というより、思い出す練習を何回したかだと言われています。教科書を読み返すだけでは、わかった気になるだけで、記憶には定着しにくいんです。問題を解いて、間違えて、また解き直す。この一見地味なくり返しこそが、本番で力を発揮する確かな近道になります。
cards.en: People who are good at studying seem to have some special innate talent, don’t they? But learning-science research says what separates grades is less talent than how many times you practiced recalling. Just rereading the textbook only makes you feel you understand, and it hardly sticks in memory. You solve problems, get them wrong, and solve them again. It is precisely this seemingly plain repetition that becomes a reliable shortcut to showing your strength on the day.

cards.enTarget: People who are good at studying seem to have some special innate talent, don’t they?

words.meaning: to be blocked, to be packed
words.defJa: すきまがふさがって通らなくなる。

cards.ja: 考えがなかなか先に進まなくなるとき、私たちはたいてい、目の前の問題にさらに力を込めて向かおうとする。しかし、排水管に限らず、詰まった場所を押し続けても水は流れない。清掃の基本は、まず原因を見極めることである。一度手を止め、散歩に出るなどして問題から離れると、あとから不意に答えが浮かぶことがある。頭の中の流れを取り戻すのは、集中の量ではなく、視点を変える勇気なのだ。
cards.en: When our thinking stops moving forward, we usually try to face the problem in front of us with even more force. But this is not limited to drainpipes: continuing to push on a blocked spot does not make the water flow. The basic of cleaning is to first work out the cause. If you stop for a moment and step away from the problem, say by going for a walk, an answer sometimes pops up out of nowhere later. What restores the flow in the head is not the amount of concentration but the courage to change perspective.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「排水管が詰まる」「言葉に詰まる」のように、流れが止まる意。
cards.enTarget: But this is not limited to drainpipes: continuing to push on a blocked spot does not make the water flow.

words.defJa: ずっとやまずに続けて。

cards.ja: 対話型の人工知能の答えが毎回少し違うのは、故障ではなく仕組みのせいだ。モデルは次に来る言葉の確率を絶えず計算し、その中から一つを選んで文章をつないでいく。選び方に乱数が混ざるからこそ、同じ質問をしても答えが揺れるのである。逆に言えば、調節さえすれば、毎回ほぼ同じ答えを引き出すことも不可能ではない。研究者はこの揺れの幅を、アイデア出しの場面ではあえて武器として使うこともある。
cards.en: That a conversational AI's answers differ slightly every time is due to its mechanism, not a malfunction. The model constantly calculates the probability of the next word, picks one from among them, and links the text together. It is precisely because randomness enters the way it chooses that the answer wavers even for the same question. Conversely, with the right adjustment it is not impossible to draw out nearly the same answer every time. Researchers sometimes deliberately use the range of this wobble as a weapon when brainstorming.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「絶えず変化する」のように、途切れず続く動作や状態に添える副詞。
cards.enTarget: The model constantly calculates the probability of the next word, picks one from among them, and links the text together.

words.defJa: そのとおりだと認めること。

cards.ja: 日本語の会話では、断るときに「いいえ」とは言わず、「ちょっと難しいですね」の一言で済ませることが多い。反対に、はっきりした肯定の返事ですら、「そうですね」と曖昧にぼかしてしまう場面がある。率直さを美徳とする文化から来た人は、ここで戸惑いがちだ。しかし、この曖昧さは相手への配慮にほかならず、言葉の裏にある距離感を読み取る力が求められる。日本語の学習者にとって、最後の関門はこの辺りかもしれない。
cards.en: In Japanese conversation, people often decline not by saying no but by settling for a single remark that it is a little difficult. Conversely, even a clear affirmative reply is sometimes blurred into a vague that's right. People from cultures that treat frankness as a virtue tend to be bewildered here. But this vagueness is nothing other than consideration for the other person, and it calls for the ability to read the sense of distance behind the words. For learners of Japanese, this may be where the final barrier lies.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「肯定的」「肯定する」のように、「否定」の反対。承認や賛成の意。
cards.enTarget: Conversely, even a clear affirmative reply is sometimes blurred into a vague that's right.

words.defJa: 他人にたのまず、自分で。

cards.ja: 日本語には、同じ「自分で」という意味でも、響きや重みの違う言い方がある。たとえば社長が自ら工場の現場に足を運んだと言えば、立場のある人が率先して動いたという含みが生まれる。一方、「自分で行った」では、単に誰の足で行ったかを述べているにすぎず、そこに立場の重みはない。語源は「身」に由来すると考えられており、動作の主体が体ごと関わるという感じが、いまも残っているのだろう。
cards.en: Even among expressions meaning by oneself, Japanese has ones that sound different. For example, if you say the company president went to the factory floor personally, it carries the implication that a person of standing took the initiative. By contrast, saying that he went by himself merely states whose feet carried him, and there is no weight of position in it. The word is thought to derive from the word for body, and perhaps the feeling that the agent is involved with his whole self remains.

ruby: べているにすぎず、そこに
cards.tipJa: 「自ら進んで」「自ら命を絶つ」など、自分の意志で行う含みがある。
cards.enTarget: For example, if you say the company president went to the factory floor personally, it carries the implication that a person of standing took the initiative.

words.defJa: 結んだものや絡んだものをゆるめて離す。

cards.ja: 支援にあたって、心理士はすぐに悩みを聞き出そうとはしない。災害の被災者の固く結ばれた心の結び目を解くには、まず温かい飲み物を渡し、体のこわばりが取れるのを待つところから始めるのだという。話すかどうかの選択を相手に残すこの姿勢は、一見消極的に見えて、実は最も効くとされる。靴ひもは、力任せに引っ張るほど締まっていく。同じように、急かされた心は、かえって固く閉じてしまうものだ。
cards.en: In providing support, psychologists do not try to draw out people's troubles right away. To undo the tightly tied knot in the hearts of disaster victims, they first hand over a warm drink and wait for the stiffness in the body to go away. This posture, which leaves the choice of whether to speak to the other person, looks passive at a glance but is said to work best. A shoelace only gets tighter the harder you pull it. In the same way, a hurried heart tends to close even more tightly.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「結び目を解く」「帯を解く」のように、結んだものをほぐして離す。
cards.sense: ほどく意
cards.enTarget: To undo the tightly tied knot in the hearts of disaster victims, they first hand over a warm drink and wait for the stiffness in the body to go away.

words.defJa: ちょうどよい具合に整えること。

cards.ja: 昔の人は時計がなかったから、日の出と日没に合わせて生活を調節してたんですよね。日の出とともに起床して、日が暮れたら休む。江戸時代の日本には「不定時法」があって、昼と夜をそれぞれ六等分するから、季節によって一刻の長さが変わるんです。夏の昼の一刻は長くて、冬は短い。だから、季節ごとに文字盤の間隔をずらせる和時計まで作られたわけで、あれは職人技としか言いようがないですよ。
cards.en: People in the old days had no clocks, so they adjusted their lives to sunrise and sunset, didn't they? They rose with the sun and rested when it got dark. Edo-period Japan had a system of variable hours, which divided day and night into six equal parts each, so the length of an hour changed with the season. A daytime hour in summer is long and in winter short. So they even made Japanese clocks whose dial intervals could be shifted for each season, and that can only be called masterly craftsmanship.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「温度を調節する」「音量の調節」のように、程度をちょうどよく合わせる意。
cards.enTarget: People in the old days had no clocks, so they adjusted their lives to sunrise and sunset, didn't they?

words.defJa: 道が交わる所。町の通りのすみ。

cards.ja: 街角の看板に目を向けると、日本語の文字の使い分けがよく見える。たとえば、美容院の看板にカタカナの店名が目立つのは、洗練された印象を出すためだ。ひらがなだけの「ひとやすみ」のような言葉は、親しみやすさを演出する。業種に応じて文字が選ばれており、同じ内容でも、表記ひとつで受け手に与える印象は大きく変わる。街を歩くことは、そのまま表記の見本帳を眺めることでもある。
cards.en: If you look at the signs on a street corner, you can clearly see how Japanese uses its scripts differently. For example, katakana shop names stand out on hair salon signs in order to give a refined impression. Words written only in hiragana, like a rest-a-while, create an approachable feel. Characters are chosen according to the type of business, and even with the same content, the impression given to the viewer changes greatly with the notation alone. Walking around town is, as it is, like leafing through a swatch book of orthography.

words.defJa: 決まった数や量をこえること。

cards.ja: 国家も家計と同じで、無計画に支出が収入を超過し続ければ、いつか行き詰まります。十八世紀のフランスはまさにその状態でした。アメリカ独立戦争への支援などで戦費がふくらんだあげく、財政は大幅な赤字に陥っていたのです。国王ルイ十六世は課税の拡大を図りましたが、そのために三部会を招集することになり、これがフランス革命の引き金の一つとなりました。革命の背景には、思想の変化だけでなく、こうした台所事情があったのです。
cards.en: A state is like a household: if spending keeps exceeding income with no plan, it will one day reach a dead end. Eighteenth-century France was in exactly that condition. After war costs swelled with its support for the American War of Independence and the like, its finances had fallen into a huge deficit. King Louis XVI tried to expand taxation, but this meant convening the Estates General, which became one of the triggers of the French Revolution. Behind the revolution lay not only a change in ideas but also this state of the kitchen accounts.

words.defJa: 仕事をする場所。

cards.ja: 職場の敬語って、難しいですよね。「ご苦労さま」は目上の人に言っちゃだめで、「お疲れさまです」にしなきゃいけないって習ったじゃないですか。でも、新人のころ、あまりに緊張したものだから、うっかり部長に「ご苦労さまです」って言って、空気が凍ったことがあるんですよ。それ以来、挨拶ひとつにも気を遣うようになりました。ただ、構えすぎると、かえって謙遜が過ぎて不自然になるんですよね。
cards.en: Honorific language in the workplace is hard, isn't it? We were taught that you must not say gokurōsama to a superior and have to say otsukaresama desu instead. But back when I was a new hire, I was so nervous that I carelessly said gokurōsama desu to my department head, and the atmosphere froze. Ever since then, I've become careful even about a single greeting. Still, if you brace yourself too much, you end up so modest that it comes across as unnatural.

words.defJa: 歌や踊りや演技などの、人に見せる芸。

cards.ja: 最近、有名人そっくりの声を人工知能でつくれるようになったじゃないですか。あれ、本人の知らないうちに広告やゲームに使われたりしたら、たまったもんじゃないですよね。だから芸能事務所は、声や顔の権利をめぐって頭を抱えてるらしいです。もちろん、本人の許可があれば、亡くなった俳優の演技をよみがえらせる使い方だって出てくるでしょう。率直に言って、技術のほうがルールづくりより先に走っちゃってて、線引きが難しいところですよね。
cards.en: Lately it's become possible to make voices that sound just like famous people with AI, hasn't it? If one were used in an ad or a game without the person knowing, that would be unbearable. So talent agencies are apparently agonizing over the rights to voices and faces. Of course, with the person's permission, there may even be uses that bring a deceased actor's performance back to life. Frankly, the technology has run ahead of rule-making, so where to draw the line is a hard question.

words.defJa: 部品や要素を合わせて形にする。

cards.ja: 記憶とは、倉庫にしまった品物をそのまま取り出す作業ではない。思い出すたびに、私たちは自ら断片を拾い集め、ひとつの物語として組み立てているのである。だからこそ、同じ出来事でも語るたびに少しずつ形が変わってしまう。はっきり覚えていると信じ込んでいるものですら、その例外ではない。確かだという感覚と正確さは別物であり、前者の強さが後者を保証してくれることはないのだ。
cards.en: Memory is not the act of taking goods out of a warehouse exactly as they were stored. Each time we remember, we gather fragments on our own and put them together into a single story. That is exactly why even the same event changes its shape a little every time we tell it. Even the things we firmly believe we remember clearly are no exception. The feeling of certainty and actual accuracy are different things, and the strength of the former never guarantees the latter.

cards.enTarget: Each time we remember, we gather fragments on our own and put them together into a single story.

words.defJa: 小さくなる。短くなる。

cards.ja: 十四世紀半ば、黒死病はヨーロッパの人口を三分の一ほど奪ったと言われています。人口が縮むと同時に労働力も不足し、生き残った農民は自ら賃金の引き上げを求めて、領主との交渉に出ました。賃金が上がり、土地を離れる者も増えていきました。領主は農奴をこれまでのように縛りつけておけなくなり、荘園の仕組みは根元から揺らぎ始めます。惨禍が古い秩序を壊すきっかけになったとしたら、歴史とはなんと皮肉なものでしょう。
cards.en: In the mid-fourteenth century, the Black Death is said to have taken away about a third of Europe's population. As the population shrank, labor also ran short, and the surviving peasants went into negotiations with their lords on their own, demanding higher wages. Wages rose, and more people left the land. Lords could no longer keep serfs bound to the land as before, and the manorial system began to shake at its roots. If a catastrophe became the occasion for breaking up an old order, how ironic history is.

cards.enTarget: As the population shrank, labor also ran short, and the surviving peasants went into negotiations with their lords on their own, demanding higher wages.

words.defJa: 不満や困っていることを訴える言葉。

cards.ja: カスタマーセンターの電話対応を人工知能に任せる会社が、最近すごく増えてますよね。苦情の電話って、対応というより我慢くらべに近くて、職場の担当者にはかなりの負担だったんですよ。そこで機械が一次対応をすれば、疲れ切って辞めていく人も減るだろう、という狙いがあるそうです。でも、怒ってる人は「人間を出せ」って言うことが多いんで、結局、最後は人の出番になっちゃうんですけどね。
cards.en: Lately a lot more companies are leaving phone support at call centers to AI, aren’t they? A call with a complaint is closer to a contest of endurance than to handling, and it was quite a burden on the staff at the workplace. So, reportedly, the idea is that if a machine handles the first response, fewer people will burn out and quit. But angry people often demand a human, so in the end it’s still the humans’ turn to step in.

words.defJa: こわがらせて、思いどおりにしようとする。

cards.ja: 恐怖で人を動かす方法は、一時的には、確かによく効く。「早く寝ないとお化けが来るよ」と子どもを脅かして従わせれば、その夜はおとなしく布団に入るだろう。しかし、恐れから従った者は、見ていない所では平気で約束を破るものだ。しかも、脅しに慣れてしまえば、同じ手はやがて通じなくなり、さらに強い脅しが必要になる。行動を本当に変えたいなら、自ら納得して動く力を育てるほかはない。
cards.en: Moving people through fear certainly works for a while. If you scare a child into obeying by saying that a ghost will come unless he goes to sleep soon, he will probably go quietly to bed that night. But those who obey out of fear will break their promises without a second thought where no one is watching. Moreover, once they get used to threats, the same trick eventually stops working, and an even stronger threat becomes necessary. If you truly want to change behavior, there is no choice but to cultivate the ability to act on one's own conviction.

words.meaning: to compensate for, to make up
words.defJa: 足りない部分を満たす。

cards.ja: 加齢に伴って、新しいことを覚える力が落ちるのは避けられない。しかし、経験を積んだ人は、蓄えた知識や勘によって、その衰えを補っていることが多い。知識の使い方の巧みさは、年齢を重ねるほど増す場合もあるという。将棋の棋士が、読みの速さを失いながらも、大局観で戦い続けるのは、その好例だろう。弱点を隠すのではなく、強みを生かす道を選ぶことが、長く現役でいる秘訣といえる。
cards.en: With aging, it is unavoidable that the ability to learn new things declines. However, people who have accumulated experience often make up for that decline with the knowledge and intuition they have stored. It is said that skill in using knowledge sometimes grows the older one gets. Shogi players who keep competing on their grasp of the whole board, even while losing speed of reading, are a good example. Choosing to use one's strengths rather than hide one's weaknesses is the secret of staying active for a long time.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「不足を補う」「欠点を補う」のように、足りない部分を別のもので満たす。
cards.enTarget: However, people who have accumulated experience often make up for that decline with the knowledge and intuition they have stored.

words.defJa: あやまりの気持ちを相手に伝える。

cards.ja: 人工知能に間違いを指摘すると、すぐに「申し訳ありません」って詫びてくれるじゃないですか。表向きは反省してるように見えるけど、そういう返答が自然だと学習しているにすぎないんですよね。人間だと、言葉で謝るだけじゃ足りなくて、態度とか次の行動で示さないと許してもらえない。そう考えると、謝るってけっこう身体的な行為だなって思います。言葉より先に、頭が下がったり、手が動いたりするものなんですよね。
cards.en: When you point out a mistake to an AI, it apologizes right away with a line about being very sorry, doesn't it? Outwardly it looks as if it is remorseful, but it is only learning that such a reply is natural. With humans, apologizing in words is not enough, and you aren't forgiven unless you show it through attitude and your next actions. When I think about it like that, saying sorry is quite a physical act. Before the words, the head bows or the hands start moving, don't they?

words.defJa: 文章や映像を集めて整え、まとめること。

cards.ja: 江戸時代後期の学者、塙保己一は、古文書をはじめ各地に散らばる記録を集めて『群書類従』にまとめた。全六百六十六冊に及ぶこの叢書の編集は、およそ四十年をかけた事業である。保己一は七歳で失明したが、目の不自由さを耳と記憶で補うことで、人に読んでもらった内容を頭に刻んだと伝えられる。散逸しかけた史料の多くが今日まで残ったのは、この執念の仕事のおかげだと評価されている。
cards.en: Hanawa Hokiichi, a scholar of the late Edo period, collected records scattered across the country, starting with old manuscripts, and compiled them into the Gunsho Ruijū. The editing of this series, which runs to 666 volumes in all, was an undertaking of roughly forty years. Hokiichi went blind at the age of seven, yet he is said to have made up for his lack of sight with his ears and memory, etching into his mind what others read aloud to him. The fact that many historical sources that were close to being lost survive to this day is credited to this work of sheer determination.

cards.tipJa: 「編集作業」「編集者」のように、集めた素材を整えて一つにまとめる意。

words.defJa: 朝、ねどこから起きること。

cards.ja: 起床時刻は平日と休日を問わずそろえるだけで、睡眠の質が改善するという報告がある。体内時計は、朝に浴びる淡い光を手がかりに、二十四時間の周期へと調整されるためだ。休日に昼まで寝ている習慣は、平日の眠気を招く「社会的時差ぼけ」の原因になりうるとされる。就寝時刻を厳密に決めるより、まず起きる時刻を固定するほうが取り組みやすく、効果には個人差があるため二週間ほど続けて様子を見るのがよい、と専門家は助言している。
cards.en: There are reports that sleep quality improves just by keeping your wake-up time the same on weekdays and holidays alike. This is because the body clock is adjusted to a twenty-four-hour cycle using the faint light you take in in the morning as a cue. The habit of sleeping until noon on holidays is said to be able to cause social jet lag, which brings on sleepiness on weekdays. Experts advise that fixing the time you get up first is easier to take on than strictly deciding your bedtime, and that since effects vary from person to person, it is best to keep at it for about two weeks and see.

cards.tipJa: 「起床時刻」「六時に起床する」のように、朝おきる意を改まって言う。
cards.enTarget: There are reports that sleep quality improves just by keeping your wake-up time the same on weekdays and holidays alike.

words.defJa: 集まりや組織をやめて、ばらばらになること。

cards.ja: 一九四〇年、日本では主要な政党が相次いで解散し、大政翼賛会に合流した。近衛文麿を中心とする新体制運動が、挙国一致の名のもとに、政党政治の幕を引いたのである。戦時色が深まるなか、議会は残ったものの、政府を批判する力はほとんど失われた。民主的な制度は、一度に壊れるのではなく、「合理的な理由」を重ねながら静かに空洞化していく。その過程を、当時の人々はどこまで自覚していたのだろうか。
cards.en: In 1940, Japan's major political parties dissolved one after another and merged into the Imperial Rule Assistance Association. The new-order movement centered on Konoe Fumimaro drew the curtain on party politics in the name of national unity. As the wartime mood deepened, the Diet remained, but its power to criticize the government was almost entirely lost. Democratic institutions do not collapse all at once but are quietly hollowed out while piling up rational reasons. How far were people at the time aware of that process?

cards.enTarget: In 1940, Japan's major political parties dissolved one after another and merged into the Imperial Rule Assistance Association.

words.defJa: 紙でつくられたお金。

cards.ja: 二〇一六年十一月、インド政府は高額の紙幣を、予告なしに使えなくすると発表しました。手持ちの現金が一夜にして紙くずになりかねないとあって、銀行の前には夜明け前から長い列ができたのです。政府の狙いは不正な蓄財をあぶり出すことでしたが、現金で暮らす庶民ほど深刻な打撃を受けました。統計の上では、その後の経済の減速も指摘されています。それでも、この賭けが成功だったかどうか、評価はいまも割れているのです。
cards.en: In November 2016, the Indian government announced that it would make high-value banknotes unusable, with no advance warning. Because the cash in people's hands could turn into scrap paper overnight, long lines formed in front of the banks before dawn. The government's aim was to flush out illicit hoards, but the people hit hardest were ordinary citizens who live on cash. The statistics also point to a slowdown in the economy afterward. Even so, whether this gamble succeeded is still judged very differently today.

words.defJa: きつくない。厳しくない。

cards.ja: スピーチの冒頭で、あえて緩い空気をつくる人がいる。小さな失敗談をひとつ語るだけで、聞き手の肩の力がふっと抜け、その後の話がすっと耳に入るようになるからだ。とはいえ、話の骨組みまでたるんではならない。緊張をほぐす部分と、きちんと締めるべき部分を切り分けて組み立てる、その設計こそが話し手の腕の見せどころである。聴衆は、笑いの量ではなく、話の筋の確かさで話し手を評価するものだ。
cards.en: Some speakers deliberately create a relaxed atmosphere at the start of a speech. Just telling one small story about a failure makes the listeners' shoulders loosen all at once, so that the rest of the talk goes smoothly into their ears. That said, the framework of the talk must not go slack as well. The design that separates the parts that ease tension from the parts that must be properly tightened, and puts them together, is exactly where a speaker's skill shows. Audiences judge a speaker not by the amount of laughter but by how sound the thread of the talk is.

cards.enTarget: Some speakers deliberately create a relaxed atmosphere at the start of a speech.

words.defJa: 自分を低く見せて、ひかえめにふるまうこと。

cards.ja: 「つまらないものですが」と手土産を差し出す習慣は、日本人の謙遜の表れとしてしばしば外国人に紹介される。研究者の間では、これを単なる遠慮ではなく、相手との関係を円滑に保つための戦略とみる向きがある。一方で、過度にへりくだってばかりいると、自分の成果を正当に評価してもらう機会を逃す原因にもなりうる。職場では、特に国際的な場面で、率直に成果を伝える技術が求められつつある。
cards.en: The custom of offering a gift while saying that it is a trifle is often introduced to foreigners as an expression of Japanese modesty. Some researchers see this not as mere reserve but as a strategy for keeping relations with the other person smooth. On the other hand, always being excessively self-effacing can also cause you to miss the chance to have your results fairly evaluated. In the workplace, especially in international settings, the skill of conveying results frankly is increasingly in demand.

words.defJa: 行った先。ものごとの成り行き。

cards.ja: 昔、財布をなくしたことがあるんですけど、行方がわからなくなったものって、とっくにあきらめたはずなのに、頭の片隅にずっと残るじゃないですか。あれ、心理学で「ツァイガルニク効果」っていって、未完了のことのほうが覚えやすいらしいんですよ。だから、気になって眠れなかったりするんですね。結局、財布は交番に届いてたんですけど、それがわかった途端に、モヤモヤが嘘であったかのように解消しました。
cards.en: I once lost my wallet, but things whose whereabouts you don't know stay in a corner of your mind for ages even though you had long since given up on them, don't they? That's called the Zeigarnik effect in psychology, and apparently unfinished things are easier to remember. So you can end up unable to sleep because it nags at you. In the end the wallet had been turned in at a police box, but the moment I found that out, the nagging feeling cleared up as if it had never been there.

cards.ja: ああいう勉強法の解説動画って、見てるときは「なるほど」ってなるじゃないですか。でも、見終わって一週間もたつと、中身がほとんど出てこないんですよ。あれは、わかった気になっているにすぎなくて、自分では何も組み立ててないからなんですよね。大事なのは、動画のあとに、何も見ずに自分の言葉で説明してみること。試行錯誤の途中で詰まったところにこそ、本当の学びがあるんです。
cards.en: Those explanation videos about study methods make you go I see while you're watching them, don't they? But a week after you finish, almost none of the content comes back. That's because you only feel you've understood, and you haven't built anything yourself. What matters is trying to explain it in your own words, without looking at anything, after the video. Real learning is exactly in the spots where you got stuck in the middle of trial and error.

So in the end it's the cars that wait. In Hinduism the cow is regarded as sacred, so if you drove them off, it could turn into a very serious matter. By Japanese standards it's unbelievable, but in its own way I felt deeply that it works as a way of keeping a distance between people and animals.

cards.ja: 新聞の文章を一文字ずつ数えて統計で調べると、いちばん多いのはひらがなで、漢字は意外なほど少ない。ところが、漢字をすべて仮名に直してみると、文は一気に読みにくくなってしまう。語と語の距離が見えなくなり、どこで切れるのか見当がつかないからだ。少数派だけに、漢字の一字一字は、意味を運ぶという重い役目を一手に負っている。日本語の表記が三種類もあるのには、それなりの理由があるのだ。
cards.en: When you count newspaper prose character by character and examine it statistically, hiragana turns out to be the most common, and kanji is surprisingly scarce. Yet if you rewrite all the kanji in kana, the text suddenly becomes hard to read. The distance between words disappears, and you cannot tell where one ends. Precisely because they are a minority, each kanji character single-handedly carries the heavy duty of conveying meaning. There is good reason, in its own way, that written Japanese has three kinds of script.

words.defJa: 程度が限度を超えること。動詞の後ろにつく

cards.ja: 完璧を目指して頑張り過ぎる人ほど、三日もたたないうちに息切れしてしまいます。これは意志が弱いからではなく、脳が急な生活の変化を危険と見なして、元の習慣へ引き戻そうとするからだと言われます。ですから、最初は物足りないと感じるほど小さく始めてこそ、挫折することなく無理なく続けられます。腕立て伏せなら一回だけ、読書なら一ページだけ。そのくらいの小ささなら、疲れた夜でも、つい手が出ます。
cards.en: People who try too hard to be perfect run out of steam in three days. This is said to be not because their willpower is weak but because the brain sees sudden change as a danger and tries to pull you back to the old habit. So it is only by starting small enough to feel unsatisfying that you can keep going without giving up. One push-up, or one page of reading. At that level, your hand reaches out even on a tired night.

words.defJa: 多く見つもっても、それ以上にはならない

cards.ja: 産業革命の初期、蒸気機関の熱効率はせいぜい数パーセントにすぎなかったとされる。そのうえ、石炭の消費量は大変なもので、燃料代が事業を圧迫することも多かった。それでも石炭と鉄を原料とする工場は急速に増え、街は煤にまみれ、労働者は長時間労働を強いられた。後世から見れば、効率の低い機械が社会を一変させたのは皮肉というほかない。技術の価値は、性能の数字ではなく、使い道の広がりで決まることを歴史は示している。
cards.en: In the early Industrial Revolution, the thermal efficiency of steam engines is said to have been no more than a few percent at most. On top of that, coal consumption was enormous, and fuel costs often squeezed businesses. Even so, factories using coal and iron multiplied rapidly, towns were covered in soot, and workers were forced into long hours. Looking back, it can only be called ironic that low-efficiency machines transformed society. History shows that a technology's value is decided not by performance figures but by the breadth of its uses.

cards.ja: 「しかたがない」と口にした瞬間、人は考えるのをやめます。日本語のこの言葉は、あきらめと受け入れの両方を含み、使いどころによっては心を守る盾にもなります。たとえば、天気や他人の気分のように、自分では動かせないものには、この言葉が効きます。ただ、何度も使えば、自ら状況を変える力まで手放しかねません。変えられることとそうでないことを分け、前者にだけ力を注ぐのが賢いやり方でしょう。
cards.en: The moment you utter “it can't be helped,” you stop thinking. This Japanese phrase contains both resignation and acceptance, and depending on where it is used it can also be a shield protecting the heart. For example, with things you cannot move yourself, such as the weather or other people's moods, this phrase works. But use it over and over and you might even let go of your power to change the situation yourself. Separating what can be changed from what cannot, and putting effort only into the former, is probably the wise way.

cards.ja: 世界史の論述で減点されやすいのは、「全て」「必ず」のような言い切りの言葉です。たとえば「ローマの住民はすべて市民だった」と書けば、奴隷の存在を無視した誤りになります。歴史は例外とのせめぎ合いなので、「多くは」「おおむね」と一歩引いて書くほうが、精度は上がります。あいまいにしすぎると主張が弱まるため、根拠として、統計や具体的な事例に基づいて一つは添えましょう。
cards.en: What tends to lose marks in world-history essays are absolute words like “all” and “always.” For example, writing “all residents of Rome were citizens” makes an error that ignores the existence of slaves. History is a tug-of-war with exceptions, so stepping back and writing “many” or “on the whole” raises precision. Being too vague weakens your claim, so attach at least one piece of evidence based on statistics or concrete cases.

words.defJa: どんなときも変わらず、いつでも

cards.ja: 仏教の出発点にあるのは、諸行無常という見方です。この世のものはつねに移り変わり、同じ姿のままとどまるものはない、という教えです。草花が咲いては散るように、体の細胞も気づかないうちに入れ替わっていきます。変わりゆくものに執着するから苦しみが生まれる、と釈迦は説いたとされます。この考えは二千五百年にわたって、東アジアの人々の死生観や、日々の暮らしの感覚にも影響を与えてきました。
cards.en: At the starting point of Buddhism is the view of impermanence. It teaches that the things of this world are always changing, and nothing stays in the same form. Just as flowers and grasses bloom and scatter, the cells of the body are also replaced without our noticing. It is said the Buddha taught that suffering arises because we cling to what is changing. For twenty-five hundred years this idea has also influenced how people in East Asia view life and death and their sensibilities about everyday life.

words.defJa: それほど時間がたたないうちに

cards.ja: 米国の規制当局は、先端半導体の輸出管理を強化する方針を示し、業界に緊張が走った。間もなく詳細な規則が公表される見通しで、各社は在庫の確保を急いでいる。とりわけ、チップの設計を請け負う企業や製造装置のメーカーは、取引先との契約内容の確認に追われている。中国向けの売上に頼ってきた企業ほど、事業の見直しを余儀なくされるだろう。規制の行方次第で、世界の供給網は大きく組み替えられる恐れがある。
cards.en: American regulators signaled a stronger export-control policy on advanced semiconductors, and tension ran through the industry. Detailed rules are expected to be published shortly, and companies are rushing to secure inventory. In particular, companies that take on chip design and makers of manufacturing equipment are busy checking the terms of their contracts with customers. The more a company has relied on sales to China, the more it will likely be forced to reconsider its business. Depending on where regulation heads, the global supply chain could be substantially reorganized.

Even in this nearly flat stretch, the model is learning fine quirks little by little. In fact, small improvements in this period often decide the final accuracy. That said, if you continue too long, there is a risk of overfitting, memorizing the training data wholesale. While keeping an eye on the budget, you decide whether to stop by constantly checking the shape of the curve.

The river surface running beneath it sparkles, and just seeing that every morning perks me up a bit. Apparently research is advancing on measuring a bridge's vibrations with sensors and having AI diagnose its condition. Since it is hard for people to inspect every time, it is probably best to leave to machines whatever can be left to them. Still, I would like to keep for humans that sense of noticing the change in sound and thinking “huh.”

cards.ja: 面接で面接官に「お茶をどうぞ」と勧められたら、「お構いなく」と返す人が多いでしょう。ところが英語の面接練習でAIに添削させると、それを直訳した文は、冷たく聞こえると指摘されました。日本語の遠慮には、相手の厚意を肯定したうえで負担を下げる働きがあり、直訳ではその気配りが消えてしまいます。語学の試験でも、言葉だけでなく、背後にある文化の働きまで訳す意識がとても大切です。
cards.en: If an interviewer offers you tea at an interview, many people would reply “Please don't trouble yourself.” But when I had an AI correct my English interview practice, I was told that a sentence translating it literally sounds cold. Japanese reserve works to lighten the burden while affirming the other person's kindness, and a literal translation loses that consideration. In language exams too, an awareness of translating the workings of the culture behind the words, not just the words, is important.

cards.ja: 紀元前四世紀、アレクサンドロス大王の軍はヒンドゥークシュ山脈を越えてインドへ向かいました。険しい峠を抜けて山の麓に降りた兵士たちを待っていたのは、象を連れたインドの軍勢でした。ギリシャ人にとってインドは、神話に近い遠い世界だったはずです。異国の景色は、兵士たちの目にどれほど鮮やかに映ったことでしょう。この遠征をきっかけに、のちにガンダーラ地方でギリシャ風の仏像が生まれていきます。
cards.en: In the fourth century BCE, Alexander the Great's army crossed the Hindu Kush and headed for India. What awaited the soldiers who came down through the rugged pass to the foot of the mountains was an Indian force with elephants. For the Greeks, India must have been a distant world close to myth. How vividly the foreign landscape must have appeared to the soldiers' eyes. Taking this expedition as a spark, Greek-style Buddha images came to be born later in the Gandhara region.

cards.ja: デリーの遺跡には、およそ千六百年前の鉄柱が立っていて、ほとんど腐食しないことで知られています。普通の鉄なら赤くさびるはずの、風雨に絶えずさらされる屋外で、いまも立ち続けているのです。しかも、長い雨季と厳しい暑さを何度も経てきたのですから、驚くほかありません。成分にリンが多く含まれ、表面に薄い保護の膜ができたことが一因だと考えられています。昔の職人の技は、現代の研究者の関心を引かずにはおかないのです。
cards.en: At a site in Delhi stands an iron pillar roughly 1,600 years old, known for hardly corroding. Outdoors, constantly exposed to wind and rain, where ordinary iron would turn red and rust, it still stands today. And having been through long rainy seasons and fierce heat many times, one cannot but be amazed. A high phosphorus content in the metal and a thin protective film forming on the surface are thought to be one factor. The skill of ancient craftsmen cannot fail to draw the interest of today's researchers.

cards.ja: 「おとなしい子」は、教室で手のかからない存在として扱われがちだ。しかし心理学者の間では、内向的な子どもが、じっくり考えるぶん深い理解にたどり着く例が知られている。たとえば、先生に当てられるずっと前から、心の中で答えを何度も検討し直している子もいるのだ。発言の回数だけで評価する授業では、そうした力は見落とされかねない。静かな子の長所を引き出す工夫が、学校に求められている。
cards.en: A “quiet child” tends to be treated in class as one who needs no looking after. Among psychologists, however, there are known cases of introverted children reaching deeper understanding because they think things through carefully. Some children, for example, have been reconsidering their answers over and over in their minds long before the teacher calls on them. In classes that evaluate only by the number of times students speak, such strengths could be overlooked. Schools are being asked to find ways to draw out the strengths of quiet children.

cards.ja: 昼休みが終わるころ、職場の机にぐったりと突っ伏してしまう人は多いと思います。意志が弱いからだと思われがちですが、実は体内のリズムのせいで午後の早い時間に眠気が来ることが知られています。夜の睡眠が足りない日は、とくにその傾向が強くなります。短い仮眠をとると、午後の集中がずっと楽になると言われます。ですから、眠いのを我慢しつつ仕事を続けるより、二十分だけ目を閉じるほうが結局は得なのです。
cards.en: I think many people end up slumped limply over their desks at work around the end of the lunch break. It tends to be blamed on weak willpower, but it is known that sleepiness actually comes in the early afternoon because of the body's internal rhythm. On days when you did not get enough sleep at night, the tendency is especially strong. A short nap is said to make afternoon concentration much easier. So rather than carrying on working while fighting off sleep, closing your eyes for just twenty minutes is the better deal in the end.

words.defJa: すでにあるものにさらに加えること

cards.ja: 日本史の授業で、江戸幕府の鎖国は「完全に国を閉ざした」と習った人が多いでしょう。ところが長崎の出島を通じて、オランダや中国との貿易は続き、情報は絶えず入ってきていました。実際、幕府は海外の情勢を報告書にまとめさせ、かなり正確に把握していたのです。教科書の記述に一行を追加するなら、「閉じていたのは門ではなく、窓口の数だった」でしょうか。一つの言葉を疑うだけで、歴史の見え方はずいぶん変わります。
cards.en: Many people probably learned in Japanese history class that the Edo shogunate's policy of national isolation meant "completely closing the country." Yet trade with the Netherlands and China continued through Dejima in Nagasaki, and information kept flowing in. In fact, the shogunate had reports on overseas affairs compiled and maintained a fairly accurate understanding of the situation abroad. If we were to add a line to the textbook account, perhaps it would be, "The gates were not shut; the number of points of contact was limited." Questioning just one expression can greatly change the way we see history.

words.defJa: 動きや進み方がおそい。てきぱきしていない

cards.en: Many people lament “I am slow at memorizing,” but memory research holds that speed of learning and resistance to forgetting are separate matters. Content crammed in all at once soon drops from memory, whereas content recalled many times at intervals stays for long. So rather than competing on speed, gradually widening your review intervals turns out to be the shortcut. Please don't blame your impatience on your memory ability.

Apparently some recent service robots even change their pitch and speaking speed to match the customer's mood. But funnily enough, just because the voice is bright, I end up replying “thank you” with a smile myself. It feels less like saying it and more like my mouth moving on its own.

cards.en: Semiconductor miniaturization has become a rugged road as it approaches the limits of physics. When circuit line widths approach just a few atoms, a slight amount of heat or leakage current decides performance. Moreover, the finer the circuits, the larger the manufacturing variation, and the harder it is to raise yields. Even so, companies are aiming for the summit from other trailheads, such as technologies that assemble tiny parts into three dimensions and new materials. Many voices say it is still too early to declare Moore's law over.

In film subtitles there are even scenes where the same English sounds like a different language. Even so, the two countries across the sea have constantly taken in each other's words through films and music. While distance divides language, media are stitching it back together.

India’s meditation traditions also have a practice of repeating short phrases to settle the mind, of which the mantra is representative. It is easy to laugh it off as mere placebo, but if it can prevent your voice from trembling even a little when it matters, it is well worth trying.

Convenient as that is, you still have to edit and choose on your own, don't you. Even if the machine polishes the wording, it does not take over the responsibility of apologizing for you.

cards.en: When you want to add a condition or exception mid-talk, the trick is to state the claim fully first and add to it afterward. If you say “This method is highly effective, however, only for those who can keep it up every day,” the claim and the limit separate cleanly. Conversely, lining up conditions before the claim is finished leaves listeners unsure what the conclusion is. A talk stays in the ear only when you place it in the order of conclusion, conditions, reasons. Try rearranging the order as if you were editing a manuscript.

But that very mismatch is the outline of the sensibility its speakers have cherished. Therein lives the everyday life of that word. When you meet an untranslatable word, close the dictionary and observe the situations in which it is used.

Thinking that way, even the distant past seems continuous with today's fiscal news, doesn't it.

cards.en: The strength of generative AI is that it never tires and will put up with the same question any number of times. For example, laying out dozens of ways of phrasing honorifics is finished far faster than a human could. On the other hand, it may state plausible errors with confidence, so the user's own eye is indispensable. In corporate workplaces, a division of labor is spreading in which AI handles drafts and summaries and humans make the final judgment. Knowing a tool's characteristics and weaknesses is itself the first step to using it well.

An error obvious in hindsight looks to the person in the thick of it like nothing but an extension of success. Napoleon's Russian campaign is often told as the classic case. Though that is not the only cause, the human habit of complacency is something that does not change even after a thousand years.

The idea is that if water is returned to paddies, the soil stores it and the groundwater is replenished again. Interests surrounding water are coming to tie the whole community's livelihood together.

words.defJa: 文書や表を内容ごとに分けた一つ一つ

cards.ja: 十九世紀の万国博覧会では、各国が出品した機械や織物が、細かな項目に分けて審査された。たとえば英国のロンドンで開かれた一八五一年の博覧会は、会場の水晶宮とともに広く知られる。受賞の一覧は新聞に載り、国の威信を示す数字として受け止められた。日本も明治期に参加して、陶磁器や漆器を通じて欧州に自国の工芸を知らせている。展示の評価が外交の一部になるという構図は、現在の国際的なランキング競争にも通じる。
cards.en: At nineteenth-century world's fairs, the machines and textiles that countries exhibited were judged by being divided into detailed categories. The 1851 exhibition held in London, for instance, is widely known together with its venue, the Crystal Palace. Lists of prizes appeared in newspapers and were taken as figures showing a nation's prestige. Japan also took part in the Meiji era, introducing its crafts to Europe through ceramics and lacquerware. The pattern in which the evaluation of exhibits became part of diplomacy resonates with today's international ranking competitions.

words.defJa: にごりがなく、向こう側まで澄んで見えること

cards.ja: ねえ、ヨーガの先生が言ってたんだけど、心って濁った水みたいなものなんだって。かき回してるうちは何も見えないけど、じっと置いておくとだんだん透明になるらしいよ。沈んだ泥が底に落ち着けば、石の形まで見えてくるのと同じ理屈だよね。古いインドの教えは、結局「放っておく勇気」を説いてるんじゃないかな。私なんかスマホをいじってるうちにいつの間にか夜中の二時で、静かになるどころか波立つ一方なんだけどね。
cards.en: Hey, my yoga teacher said the mind is like muddy water. While you keep stirring it you can't see anything, but if you leave it still, it apparently gradually turns clear. It's the same logic as how, once the sunken mud settles at the bottom, you can see even the shapes of the stones. Ancient Indian teachings are probably about “the courage to leave things alone” in the end. Me, I fiddle with my phone and before I know it it is two in the morning, and instead of calming down I just get more and more stirred up.

words.defJa: 表面が平らでなく、高い所と低い所があるようす

cards.ja: ローマの街道は、遠くから見ればまっすぐで整っている。しかし実際に歩いてみると、石畳は場所によってでこぼこで、何百年もの長い年月に車輪が刻んだ溝が残っている。歴史もまた、整った物語の下に無数の凹凸を抱えているものである。年表の直線は、後の世の人々の編集によって引かれた線にすぎない。その線だけを眺めて過去を知った気になるのは、地図だけで山を登った気になるのと同じだ。
cards.en: Roman roads look straight and orderly from afar. But walking them in reality, the paving stones are bumpy in places and grooves carved by wheels over hundreds of years remain. History too holds countless irregularities beneath its tidy narrative. The straight lines of a chronology are merely lines drawn by later generations through editing. To feel you know the past by looking only at those lines is the same as feeling you have climbed a mountain from a map alone.

words.defJa: 音がひろがる。また、心や物事に強く伝わる

cards.ja: 職場の会議でも、同じ内容を話して心に響く人と、右から左へ抜けていく人がいる。差を生むのは、声の高さではなく、話す前に相手の顔を思い浮かべたかどうかだと私は考えている。聞き手の顔が浮かんでいれば、言葉の選び方も間の取り方も、自然とその人に合っていく。一人に向けて書いた言葉は、結果として多くの人に届くことが多い。だからこそ、原稿の最初の一行は、聞き手の悩みから始めるに越したことはない。
cards.en: Even in workplace meetings, there are people whose words stay with you and people whose words go in one ear and out the other, though they say the same content. What makes the difference, I think, is not the pitch of the voice but whether you pictured the listener's face before speaking. When the listener's face is in mind, both the choice of words and the timing of pauses naturally come to suit that person. Words written for one person often end up reaching many people. That is why it is best to begin the first line of a script with the listener's worry.

words.defJa: わかして熱くした水

cards.ja: 日本語には、温かい水を指すための専用の言葉があります。英語圏では、どちらも同じ語で、温度を言いたいときは「熱い」を表す語を足すだけです。ところが日本語では、やかんの音がしただけで「そろそろお湯が沸いたかな」と、水とは別のものとして受け止めます。湯気の立つ茶碗を両手で包む感覚には、温度以上の安心がある。この種の区別は水に限らず、米や魚にも見られ、その文化が大切にしてきたものを映しています。
cards.en: Japanese has a dedicated word for warm water. In the English-speaking world both are the same word, and to indicate temperature you just add a word meaning “hot.” In Japanese, however, the moment a kettle makes its sound you think “the hot water must be boiling by now,” taking it as something distinct from water. There is more than temperature in the comfort of cupping a steaming bowl in both hands. This kind of distinction is seen not only with water but with rice and fish, reflecting what the culture has valued.

words.defJa: ある数量に同じ量を足した大きさ

cards.ja: チェスの原型は古代インドで生まれたとされ、その誕生をめぐる有名な伝説があります。盤を発明した家臣は、王から褒美を聞かれて、一マス目に米一粒、次のマスにはその倍、またその倍と置いてほしいと願い出ました。王は安い願いだと笑いましたが、六十四マス目に着くころには、国中の米倉を空にしても足りなかったのです。何となく小さく見える数字ほど、二倍を重ねると途方もない大きさになるという話です。
cards.en: The prototype of chess is said to have originated in ancient India, and there is a famous legend about its birth. The retainer who invented the board, asked by the king what reward he wanted, asked for one grain of rice on the first square, double that on the next, and double that again. The king laughed that it was a cheap request, but by the time he reached the sixty-fourth square, even emptying every granary in the country was not enough. It is a story that numbers which somehow look small become staggeringly large once you keep stacking doubles.

words.defJa: 困難なことをうまく切り抜ける

cards.ja: 幕末の日本が欧米列強に植民地にされなかったのは、運がよかったからだけではありません。開国を迫られた幕府と藩は、対立を乗り越えて、短い期間のうちに軍事と制度を作り替えました。薩英戦争や下関戦争の敗北を経て、攘夷が現実的でないと身をもって知ったことも大きかったのです。侵略の危機を、滅びる理由ではなく変わるための材料として使えたことが、他国との分かれ目になりました。
cards.en: Late-Edo Japan was not kept from becoming a colony of the Western powers merely by luck. The shogunate and the domains, pressed to open the country, overcame their conflicts and remade their military and institutions within a short period. Having learned firsthand, through defeats in the Anglo-Satsuma War and the Shimonoseki campaigns, that expelling the foreigners was unrealistic also counted for a lot. Being able to use the danger of invasion not as a reason to perish but as material for change was the dividing line from other countries.

words.defJa: 人間の文化や社会を研究する学問

cards.ja: インドのカースト制をめぐる人類学の研究は、二十世紀を通じて見方を大きく変えてきた。かつては固定的な身分制度として描かれがちだったが、現地に長く滞在した研究者たちは、日々の食事や結婚、仕事の分担を通じて序列が絶えず交渉されている様子を記録した。近年は、全国的な統計に表れる区分と、暮らしの中の実態とのずれも指摘されている。こうした研究が示すのは、制度の名前だけでは社会は読めないという事実だ。
cards.en: Anthropological research on India's caste system has greatly changed its view over the twentieth century. Once it tended to be depicted as a fixed status system, but researchers who stayed long in the field recorded how the ranking is constantly negotiated through daily meals, marriage and the division of work. In recent years, gaps between the categories shown in nationwide statistics and the reality of life have also been pointed out. What such research shows is the fact that a society cannot be read from the names of its institutions alone.

words.defJa: 物事が進む速さ

cards.ja: 日本語のニュースは早口に聞こえる、と感じる学習者は少なくありません。実際、フランスの研究チームが複数の言語を比べたところ、日本語は一秒あたりの音の数が多い言語に入りました。ただし、一音が運ぶ情報は少ないため、話すスピードが速くても、伝わる情報の量は他の言語とほとんど変わらなかったのです。耳が慣れないうちは、速さそのものより、音のかたまりを捉える練習が先でしょう。
cards.en: Not a few learners feel that Japanese news sounds fast-talking. In fact, when a French research team compared several languages, Japanese fell among the languages with many sounds per second. However, because each sound carries little information, even at a fast speaking speed the amount of information conveyed was hardly different from other languages. While your ear is not yet used to it, practice at catching chunks of sound probably comes before speed itself.

words.defJa: 金額のすべて

cards.ja: 生成AIの新興企業が集めた資金は、驚くほどの速さで消えていきます。最大の支出は人件費ではなく計算資源で、調達した資金の全額が半導体の購入やクラウドの利用料に消えることもあるといいます。投資家はそれを承知のうえで、巨額の損失を許容している一方で、成果が出なければ資金は一気に引き上げられます。この分野の競争は、アイデアの勝負であると同時に、資金の体力勝負でもあるのです。
cards.en: The money raised by generative AI startups disappears at astonishing speed. The biggest expense is not personnel but computing resources, and it is said that the full amount of funds raised can vanish into buying semiconductors and cloud usage fees. Investors tolerate huge losses knowing this, while on the other hand, if no results appear, the money is pulled out all at once. Competition in this field is a contest of ideas and, at the same time, a contest of financial stamina.

cards.ja: インド鉄道は毎日二千万人を超える乗客を運ぶ、世界有数の大規模な交通網である。かつて乗車券を買うには、窓口に長い列ができ、係員との交渉に半日を費やすことも珍しくなかった。近年はオンライン予約が急速に広がり、列に並ぶ人の姿は減りつつある。とはいえ、スマートフォンを持たない高齢者や遠隔地の住民にとって、窓口は今も全国的に欠かせない入口である。対面の窓口が担う役割は、画面の向こうにはまだ置き換えきれない。
cards.en: Indian Railways is one of the world's largest transport networks, carrying over twenty million passengers every day. In the past, buying a ticket meant long lines at the counter, and spending half a day negotiating with the clerk was not unusual. In recent years online booking has spread rapidly, and the sight of people standing in line is decreasing. Even so, for the elderly without smartphones and for residents of remote areas, the counter remains an indispensable entrance across the nation. The role played by the face-to-face counter cannot yet be replaced by what lies behind a screen.

words.defJa: 多くが同時にそろって行うさま

cards.ja: ガンジス河畔のヴァーラーナシーでは、夕暮れに鐘が鳴ると、岸に集まった人々が一斉に小さな灯りを水へ流す。その灯りは、祈りというより、ひとつの呼吸のように川面を渡っていく。眺めていると、人々を動かしているのは個々の願いではなく、場そのものだという気がしてくる。個がほどけて全体に溶ける感覚は、インド思想が長く問い続けてきた主題と無縁ではない。各地の集会や祭りに共通するのも、この溶け合いの力である。
cards.en: At Varanasi on the banks of the Ganges, when the bell rings at dusk, the people gathered on the bank all at once set small lamps afloat on the water. Those lights move across the river's surface less like prayers than like a single breath. Watching, you begin to feel that what moves the people is not each individual's wish but the place itself. The sensation of the individual loosening and dissolving into the whole is not unrelated to the theme Indian thought has long kept asking about. What gatherings and festivals everywhere share is also this power of merging.

words.defJa: 数や量がほんの少しであるさま

cards.ja: リンカーンのゲティスバーグ演説は、わずか二分ほどで終わったと伝えられている。当日の主役は別の弁士で、二時間に及ぶ長い話のあとに、紙一枚にも満たないこの短い言葉が続いたのである。ところが、聴衆の記憶に残ったのは、むしろ短いほうだった。話し方を本気で磨くなら、削りながらも芯を失わない姿勢にこそ学ぶべきものがある。短さは、聞き手の集中を逃さないという意味で、大きな長所にもなる。
cards.en: Lincoln's Gettysburg Address is said to have ended in a mere two minutes or so. The star of the day was another speaker, and these short words, less than a single sheet of paper, followed a long talk that ran two hours. Yet it was rather the short one that stayed in the audience's memory. If you want to seriously polish your speaking, there is much to learn from the stance of cutting while never losing the core. Brevity can be a great strength too, in the sense that it does not let the listener's attention slip away.

words.defJa: 国全体に広がるさま

cards.ja: 一九三〇年、ガンディーは弟子たちとともに、約三百八十キロの道のりを歩いて海へ向かい、塩の専売に抗議した。それだけの行動が、各地で集会を呼び、やがて全国的な不服従運動へと広がったのである。武器を持たないただの行進が、なぜ巨大な帝国を揺さぶり得たのか。塩という誰もが毎日口にする物を選んだことに、その答えの一端があるように思われる。暮らしに直結する象徴は、思想より速く人の足を動かす。
cards.en: In 1930, Gandhi, together with his followers, walked some three hundred eighty kilometers to the sea and protested the salt monopoly. That one act drew gatherings in many places and spread, in time, into a nationwide movement of civil disobedience. How could a mere unarmed march shake a vast empire? Part of the answer seems to lie in his choosing salt, something everyone eats every day. A symbol tied directly to daily life moves people's feet faster than ideas do.

words.defJa: 危険がある度合い

cards.ja: 一八五四年、ロンドンのソーホーでコレラが急速に広がった。医師のジョン・スノーは患者の住所に基づいて地図を作り、ブロード街の共用井戸の周辺に症例が集中していることを突き止めた。当時は空気中の毒気が原因だという説が有力で、一見透明で澄んだ水の危険性を訴える彼の主張は、すぐには受け入れられなかった。それでも、井戸のポンプの取っ手が外されると、流行は収まっていったとされる。データを可視化する発想は、疫学の出発点の一つとなっている。
cards.en: In 1854, cholera spread rapidly in Soho, London. The physician John Snow made a map based on patients' addresses and established that cases clustered around the shared well on Broad Street. At the time the theory that foul air was the cause was dominant, and his claim about the danger of water that looked transparent and clear was not readily accepted. Even so, when the well pump's handle was removed, the outbreak is said to have subsided. The idea of visualizing data is one of the starting points of epidemiology.

words.defJa: 医学に関わる人々の世界

cards.ja: 十九世紀半ば、ウィーンの医師センメルワイスは、医師が手を洗うだけで産褥熱による死亡が大きく減ると訴えた。しかし当時の医学界は、その主張を受け入れなかった。不潔な手の危険性という考えはまだ広まっておらず、医師が患者を死なせているという指摘は、職業の誇りを傷つけるものでもあったからだ。正しいからといって受け入れられるとは限らない。真実が通るかどうかは、聞き手の自尊心との相性にも左右される。
cards.en: In the mid-nineteenth century, the Viennese physician Semmelweis argued that doctors merely washing their hands would greatly reduce deaths from childbed fever. The medical world of the time, however, did not accept his claim. The idea of the danger of unclean hands had not yet spread, and the charge that doctors were killing patients also wounded professional pride. Being right does not guarantee being accepted. Whether the truth gets through also depends on how well it fits the listener's self-regard.

words.defJa: 意思や情報を伝え合うこと

cards.ja: 遣唐使は、現地の人とどのようにコミュニケーションをとったのだろうか。通訳が同行していたが、知識人どうしのやりとりでは筆談も大きな役割を果たしたとされる。漢字を共有していたからこそ、海を隔てた隣国の相手とも、発音が通じなくても意味は伝わったのである。この話は、会話力と読み書きの力を別々に鍛えられることを教えてくれる。まず読む力を土台にしてから、話す練習を足していくという順序にも、十分に筋が通っている。
cards.en: How did the Japanese envoys to Tang China communicate with the people there? Interpreters accompanied them, but written conversation is said to have played a large part in exchanges between scholars. Precisely because they shared Chinese characters, meaning got across even to counterparts in a neighboring country across the sea, though pronunciation did not. This story teaches us that conversational ability and reading and writing can be trained separately. The order of building on reading first and then adding speaking practice is also perfectly reasonable.

words.defJa: 毎日勉強ばかりしている状態

cards.ja: 中国の科挙の受験生は、幼いころから四書五経を暗唱する、勉強漬けの日々を送った。合格できるのはごくわずかで、毎年多くの受験生が涙をのみ、白髪になってもなお受験を続ける者さえいたと伝えられる。合格すれば役人として家の名誉も高まるため、一族の期待も重くのしかかった。この制度は努力が報われるという信念を支えた反面、全員が一つの試験に人生を賭ける社会は、才能の使い道を狭めてもいたのではないか。皮肉な話である。
cards.en: Candidates for China's imperial examinations spent days steeped in study, reciting the Four Books and Five Classics from early childhood. Only a very few could pass, and many candidates swallowed their tears each year; it is said some kept sitting the exam even after their hair had turned white. Passing raised the family's honor as an official, so the expectations of the whole clan weighed heavily as well. While this system upheld the belief that effort is rewarded, a society in which everyone staked their life on a single exam may also have narrowed the uses of talent. It is an ironic tale.
