cards.enTarget: It has been reported that, because of the declining birthrate, more than half of all private universities now enroll fewer students than their capacity.

words.defJa: 品物につけられている、前もって決まった値段。

cards.ja: 日本では、新刊の書籍や雑誌はどの書店で買っても原則として定価で売られている。出版社が小売価格を決められる再販売価格維持制度があるためだ。この仕組みは、小さな書店や専門書の出版を守る役割を果たしてきたとされる。ただ、電子書籍には適用されず、割引販売が当たり前になっている。
cards.en: In Japan, new books and magazines are, as a rule, sold at the list price no matter which bookstore you buy them from. This is because of the resale price maintenance system, which allows publishers to set retail prices. The system is said to have helped protect small bookstores and the publishing of specialized books. However, it does not apply to e-books, where discounted sales have become the norm.

words.defJa: 程度や位置、力などが下がること。

cards.ja: 睡眠不足が続くと、集中力や判断力が目に見えて低下することが多くの研究で示されている。ある実験では、六時間睡眠を二週間続けた人の成績が、一晩徹夜した人とほぼ同じ水準まで落ちた。厄介なのは、本人はそれほど眠気を感じていないことが多い点だ。自覚のないまま能力が下がっているのである。
cards.en: Many studies have shown that when sleep deprivation continues, concentration and judgment decline noticeably. In one experiment, the performance of people who slept six hours a night for two weeks fell to almost the same level as that of people who had stayed up all night once. The tricky part is that the people themselves often do not feel very sleepy. Their abilities are falling without their being aware of it.

words.defJa: 決まった区間を、決まった期間、何度でも乗れる乗車券。

cards.ja: テレワークが定着したことで、通勤定期券を買うのをやめる会社員が増えている。週に二、三日しか出社しないなら、その都度運賃を払ったほうが安く済む場合が多いからだ。企業の側でも、交通費を定期代ではなく実費で支給する制度に切り替える動きが広がっている。鉄道会社は、利用日数に応じた新しい割引を模索している。
cards.en: With remote work now established, more and more office workers are giving up buying commuter passes. That is because if they only go into the office two or three days a week, paying each fare as they go often works out cheaper. Companies, too, are increasingly switching to systems that reimburse actual travel costs instead of paying for a commuter pass. Railway companies are exploring new discounts based on the number of days of use.

cards.enTarget: With remote work now established, more and more office workers are giving up buying commuter passes.

words.meaning: regular closing day (of a shop or business)
words.defJa: 店や会社などが、毎週や毎月、決まって休む日。

cards.ja: この町の商店街では、昔から水曜日を定休日にしている店が多い。理由をたずねると、かつて卸売市場が水曜日に休みで、仕入れができなかった名残だという。最近は観光客の増加を受けて、水曜日も店を開けるところが出てきた。訪れる前に店の案内を確認しておけば、無駄足を踏まずに済む。
cards.en: In this town's shopping street, many shops have long made Wednesday their regular closing day. When asked why, people say it is a holdover from the days when the wholesale market was closed on Wednesdays and shops could not stock up. Recently, in response to the rise in tourists, some shops have started opening on Wednesdays as well. If you check a shop's information before visiting, you can avoid a wasted trip.

cards.enTarget: In this town's shopping street, many shops have long made Wednesday their regular closing day.

words.defJa: 動いていたものや続いていたことを、途中で止めること。

cards.ja: ある自治体が進めていた自動運転バスの実証実験で、運行が一時停止された。走行中にセンサーが路上の落ち葉を障害物と誤って認識し、急ブレーキをかける事例が相次いだためだ。運営側は人工知能の判定基準を見直し、安全が確認され次第、運行を再開するとしている。技術の実用化には、こうした試行錯誤が欠かせない。
cards.en: In a trial of self-driving buses run by a local government, service has been temporarily suspended. This was because there were repeated cases of the sensors mistaking fallen leaves on the road for obstacles and slamming on the brakes while the bus was moving. The operators say they will review the artificial intelligence's decision criteria and resume service as soon as safety has been confirmed. This kind of trial and error is indispensable for putting technology into practical use.

words.meaning: coming and going (of people), comings and goings
words.defJa: 人や物が、ある場所に入ったり出たりすること。

cards.ja: 祖父母の家は商店街の角にあり、子どものころから人の出入りが絶えなかった。近所の人がふらりと立ち寄っては、お茶を飲みながら町の出来事を話していく。鍵をかけるのは夜だけで、昼間は玄関が開けっ放しだった。今振り返ると、あの家は地域の小さな集会所のような役割を果たしていたのだと思う。
cards.en: My grandparents' house stood on a corner of the shopping street, and ever since I was a child there was a constant coming and going of people. Neighbors would drop by on a whim and chat about what was happening in town over a cup of tea. The door was locked only at night; during the day the front entrance was left wide open. Looking back, I think that house served as a kind of small meeting hall for the neighborhood.

words.defJa: 建物や駅などで、人が出たり入ったりするところ。

cards.ja: 地下鉄の駅には複数の出入口があり、それぞれに番号が振られている。目的地に最も近い出入口を事前に調べておけば、地上に出てから道に迷うことが少ない。大きな駅では出入口が二十か所を超えることもあり、初めて訪れる観光客には分かりにくい。最近は案内板に多言語の表示や周辺の地図を加える駅が増えている。
cards.en: Subway stations have several entrances and exits, each assigned a number. If you check in advance which exit is closest to your destination, you are less likely to get lost once you reach street level. Large stations can have more than twenty of them, which is confusing for tourists visiting for the first time. Recently more stations have been adding multilingual signs and maps of the surrounding area to their information boards.

cards.enTarget: Subway stations have several entrances and exits, each assigned a number.

words.defJa: 人や動物が出たり入ったりするための口。

cards.ja: ミツバチの巣の出入り口には、門番の役割を担う働きバチが常に待機している。彼らは巣の仲間に特有のにおいを嗅ぎ分け、別の巣から来たハチや外敵を見つけると追い払う。花の蜜が少なくなる時期には、蜜を盗みに来るよその巣のハチが増えるため、門番の数も多くなることが知られている。小さな昆虫の社会にも、状況に応じた見事な分業がある。
cards.en: At the entrance of a honeybee hive, worker bees acting as gatekeepers are always on standby. They pick out the scent peculiar to their nestmates, and when they find bees from another hive or other enemies, they drive them away. It is known that when flowers yield less nectar, more bees from other hives come to steal honey, so the number of guards rises as well. Even in the society of a small insect, there is a remarkable division of labor that adapts to circumstances.

words.defJa: よい状態を保つために、世話をしたり直したりすること。

cards.ja: かつて里山の雑木林は、薪や炭をとるために定期的に木が切られるなど、絶えず手入れされてきた。燃料が石油やガスに変わると、林は放置され、竹やササが地面を覆うようになった。光が届かなくなった林では、春に咲く野草や、それを頼りに暮らす昆虫が姿を消しつつある。各地で市民による下草刈りや竹の伐採が始まっているのは、こうした変化への危機感からだ。
cards.en: The mixed woodlands around rural villages were once constantly tended, with trees cut regularly for firewood and charcoal. When fuel shifted to oil and gas, the woods were left untended, and bamboo and dwarf bamboo came to cover the ground. In woods where light no longer reaches, the wildflowers that bloom in spring, and the insects that depend on them, are disappearing. The undergrowth clearing and bamboo cutting by local residents that have begun in many places stem from a sense of alarm at these changes.

words.meaning: the finished result, how something turns out; completion
words.defJa: 作っていたものが完成すること。また、完成した状態や具合。

cards.ja: 陶芸の難しさは、窯から出すまで出来上がりが分からない点にある。同じ材料を使っても、窯の中の温度や炎の当たり方によって色合いは大きく変わる。何十年も土に向き合ってきた職人でさえ、思いどおりの器が焼けるのはごく一部にすぎないという。だからこそ、偶然が生んだ美しさを大切にする文化が育ったのだろう。
cards.en: The difficulty of pottery lies in the fact that you cannot know how a piece will turn out until you take it out of the kiln. Even with the same materials, the colors change greatly depending on the temperature inside the kiln and how the flames strike the piece. Even craftspeople who have worked with clay for decades are said to fire the vessel they intended only a small fraction of the time. Perhaps that is exactly why a culture grew up that treasures beauty born of chance.

words.meaning: to be completed, to be finished; to be ready
words.defJa: 作っていたものが、すっかり完成する。

cards.ja: 自家製の味噌づくりが静かなブームになっている。ゆでた大豆をつぶし、こうじと塩を混ぜて容器に詰めたら、あとは涼しく暗い場所で寝かせるだけだ。半年から一年ほどたつと、まろやかな香りの味噌が出来上がる。手間はかかるが、季節ごとに味が変わっていく過程を楽しめるのが魅力だという。
cards.en: Making miso at home has become a quiet boom. You mash boiled soybeans, mix in koji and salt, pack the mixture into a container, and then all that remains is to let it rest in a cool, dark place. After six months to a year, miso with a mellow aroma is ready. It takes effort, but people say the appeal lies in enjoying the process as the flavor changes with each season.

words.defJa: その場に適していて、確実で間違いがないようす。

cards.ja: 改正された法律は、事業者に対し、利用者からの苦情を適確に処理するための体制を整えるよう求めている。担当部署を定めるだけでなく、対応の記録を残し、再発の防止に生かすことが必要だ。監督する官庁は、体制が不十分な事業者に改善を命じることができる。違反が続けば、事業の停止を命じられることもある。
cards.en: The revised law requires businesses to put in place a system for handling complaints from users accurately and appropriately. Beyond simply designating a department in charge, they must keep records of how they responded and use them to prevent recurrence. The supervising ministry can order businesses with inadequate systems to make improvements. If violations continue, a business may even be ordered to suspend operations.

words.defJa: 腕と手のひらをつなぐ、細くなっている部分。

cards.ja: パソコンやスマートフォンを長時間使う人の間で、手首の痛みを訴える例が増えている。キーボードを打つときに手首を反らせた姿勢が続くと、内部の神経が圧迫されやすいためだ。専門医は、一時間に一度は手を休め、指や手首をゆっくり伸ばすよう勧めている。机の高さを見直すだけでも、負担はかなり軽くなるという。
cards.en: Among people who use computers and smartphones for long hours, complaints of wrist pain are on the rise. This is because keeping the wrist bent back while typing tends to put pressure on the nerves inside. Specialists recommend resting your hands once an hour and slowly stretching your fingers and wrists. Simply adjusting the height of your desk is said to reduce the strain considerably.

words.defJa: 表面が平らでなく、高いところと低いところがあること。

cards.ja: ある自治体では、ごみ収集車にスマートフォンを取り付け、道路の凸凹を自動で見つける取り組みを始めた。走行中の揺れをセンサーで記録し、AIが路面の傷みが激しい場所を地図上に示す仕組みだ。これまで職員が目で見て行っていた点検に比べ、はるかに広い範囲を短時間で調べられる。補修の優先順位を決める材料としても役立っている。
cards.en: One municipality has started mounting smartphones on its garbage trucks to automatically detect bumps and dips in the roads. Sensors record the shaking while the trucks are driving, and AI marks on a map the places where the road surface is badly damaged. Compared with the inspections staff used to carry out by eye, a far wider area can be surveyed in a short time. The data also helps in deciding the order in which repairs are made.

words.defJa: 値段や大きさなどが、自分に合っていてちょうどよいようす。

cards.ja: 物価の上昇が続くなか、手ごろな価格で食事ができる店に客が集まっている。ある定食チェーンでは、ご飯の量を選べるようにしたり、仕入れを見直したりして、値上げの幅を最小限に抑えた。利用者からは、毎日通える値段がありがたいという声が多い。外食業界では、価格と品質のバランスをめぐる競争が一段と激しくなっている。
cards.en: As prices keep rising, customers are flocking to restaurants where they can eat at reasonable prices. One set-meal chain kept its price increases to a minimum by letting customers choose how much rice they want and by reviewing its purchasing. Many customers say they are grateful for prices that let them come every day. In the restaurant industry, competition over the balance between price and quality is growing ever fiercer.

words.defJa: 先生や師匠について、技術や教えを学ぶ人。

cards.ja: 落語の世界では、入門を許された弟子は師匠の家に通い、掃除や着物の着付けなど身の回りの世話から修業を始める。すぐに舞台に上がれるわけではなく、師匠や先輩の話を何度も聞いて、少しずつ演目を覚えていく。こうした期間を経て一人前と認められるまでには、十年以上かかることも珍しくない。近年は大学を卒業してから弟子入りする若者も増えている。
cards.en: In the world of rakugo storytelling, an apprentice who has been accepted goes to the master's house and begins training by tending to the master's personal needs, such as cleaning and helping with kimono. They cannot go on stage right away; instead they listen again and again to the stories of their master and senior apprentices, gradually memorizing the repertoire. It is not unusual for it to take more than ten years of this before they are recognized as full-fledged performers. In recent years, more young people have been becoming apprentices after graduating from university.

words.defJa: 予定や大事なことを書いておく、持ち歩き用の小さな帳面。

cards.ja: スマートフォンで予定を管理する人が増えた今も、年末になると書店の手帳売り場はにぎわう。紙の手帳には、一週間の予定を一目で見渡せ、思いついたことをすぐ書き込めるという良さがある。ある文具メーカーの調査では、仕事の予定はアプリ、個人的な目標は手帳と使い分ける人が多かった。書くという行為そのものが、頭を整理する助けになっているのかもしれない。
cards.en: Even now that more people manage their schedules on smartphones, the planner sections of bookstores are busy at the end of the year. Paper planners have the advantage of letting you take in a week's schedule at a glance and jot down ideas the moment they occur to you. In a survey by one stationery maker, many people split their use, keeping work appointments in an app and personal goals in a planner. Perhaps the very act of writing helps people put their thoughts in order.

words.defJa: 物事を正式に行うために、決められた順序で進めるやり方。

cards.ja: 引っ越しをすると、役所での住所変更をはじめ、電気やガス、銀行など、さまざまな手続きが必要になる。以前は窓口ごとに書類を書き、平日に何度も足を運ばなければならなかった。最近はオンラインで済ませられるものが増え、一度の入力で複数の届け出をまとめて行える仕組みも整いつつある。それでも高齢者の中には、操作に不安を感じる人が少なくない。
cards.en: When you move house, you have to go through all sorts of procedures, starting with a change of address at the municipal office and extending to electricity, gas, banks and more. In the past, you had to fill out forms at each counter and make repeated trips on weekdays. Recently more of these can be completed online, and systems that let you file several notifications at once with a single entry are being put in place. Even so, quite a few elderly people feel uneasy about using them.

words.defJa: 火薬の力で弾を飛ばす、筒の形をした武器。

cards.ja: 十六世紀の半ば、九州の南の島に流れ着いた船に乗っていたポルトガル人が、日本に初めて鉄砲を伝えたとされる。島の領主はその威力に驚き、高い値で二丁を買い取って、職人に同じものを作らせた。製法はまたたく間に各地へ広がり、やがて戦国大名の戦い方を大きく変えていく。わずか数十年で、日本は世界有数の鉄砲の生産地になったといわれる。
cards.en: In the middle of the sixteenth century, Portuguese aboard a ship that drifted ashore on an island south of Kyushu are said to have brought firearms to Japan for the first time. The lord of the island, astonished by their power, bought two at a high price and had craftsmen make copies. The method of making them spread rapidly across the country and eventually transformed the way the warlords of the Warring States period fought. Within just a few decades, Japan is said to have become one of the world's leading producers of guns.

words.defJa: 汗や手をふくのに使う、薄い木綿の細長い布。

cards.ja: 手ぬぐいは一枚の綿の布にすぎないが、使い道は驚くほど広い。汗をふくのはもちろん、頭に巻いたり、食器をふいたり、物を包んだりすることもできる。薄いので乾きやすく、両端を縫っていないのも、水切れをよくして早く乾かすための工夫だという。最近は季節の柄や現代的なデザインのものが増え、壁に飾って楽しむ人もいる。
cards.en: A tenugui is nothing more than a single piece of cotton cloth, yet its uses are surprisingly wide. Besides wiping away sweat, of course, you can wrap it around your head, dry dishes with it, or wrap things in it. It is thin, so it dries easily, and leaving both ends unhemmed is said to be a deliberate touch that lets water drain off so it dries faster. Recently more of them come in seasonal patterns or modern designs, and some people enjoy hanging them on the wall as decoration.

words.defJa: ある物や場所より、自分に近い側。

cards.ja: 道を尋ねられたとき、目印を一つ添えるだけで説明はぐっと分かりやすくなる。たとえば、郵便局の手前の角を右に曲がると言えば、相手は郵便局が見えた時点で曲がる場所に気づける。反対に、二つ目の信号といった数え方は、途中で数え間違えると迷いやすい。地図アプリが普及した今でも、言葉で道を伝える工夫は役に立つ。
cards.en: When someone asks you for directions, adding just one landmark makes your explanation much easier to follow. For example, if you say to turn right at the corner just before the post office, the person will know where to turn as soon as the post office comes into view. Counting methods like the second traffic light, by contrast, easily lead people astray if they miscount along the way. Even now that map apps are widespread, these tricks for giving directions in words remain useful.

words.meaning: meeting someone on arrival, welcome, reception
words.defJa: 到着する人を、その場所まで行って待ち、むかえること。

cards.ja: 世界大会で初めて金メダルを獲得した代表チームが帰国し、空港で大勢のファンの出迎えを受けた。到着ロビーには早朝から人が集まり、選手が姿を見せると大きな拍手と歓声が上がった。主将はメダルを掲げながら、皆さんの応援がずっと力になっていたと感謝を述べた。来週には都内で記念のパレードが行われる予定だ。
cards.en: The national team, which won its first-ever gold medal at the world championships, returned home and was greeted at the airport by a large crowd of fans. People had gathered in the arrivals lobby since early morning, and when the players appeared, loud applause and cheers went up. Holding up the medal, the captain thanked the fans, saying their support had been a source of strength all along. A celebratory parade is scheduled to be held in Tokyo next week.

words.meaning: to go out to meet, to greet (an arriving person)
words.defJa: 訪ねてくる人や帰ってくる人を、外まで出てむかえる。

cards.ja: 山あいの小さな旅館では、車の音が聞こえると、おかみが玄関の外まで出て客を出迎える。部屋に案内される前に、温かいお茶と地元の和菓子でひと息つくのがこの宿の習慣だ。夕食には近くの畑でとれた野菜や川魚が並び、素朴ながら手の込んだ料理が続く。何度も訪れる常連客が多いのは、こうした細やかなもてなしのためだろう。
cards.en: At a small inn in the mountains, as soon as the sound of a car is heard, the proprietress steps out past the front entrance to greet the guests. It is the custom at this inn to take a breather with hot tea and local Japanese sweets before being shown to your room. Dinner features vegetables from nearby fields and river fish, a succession of simple yet carefully prepared dishes. The many regulars who come back again and again are probably drawn by this kind of attentive hospitality.

words.meaning: to shine on, to illuminate; to check against (a standard)
words.defJa: 光を当てて明るくする。

cards.ja: 幕が上がると、真っ暗な舞台の中央に立つ一人の俳優を、細いスポットライトが照らした。観客は息をのみ、劇場全体が静まり返る。照明を担当するスタッフによれば、光を当てる角度や色を少し変えるだけで、同じ場面でも人物の孤独や希望が違って見えるという。芝居において、光はせりふと同じくらい多くを語るのだ。
cards.en: When the curtain rose, a narrow spotlight shone on a lone actor standing in the middle of the pitch-dark stage. The audience held its breath, and the whole theater fell silent. According to the lighting staff, just slightly changing the angle or color of the light can make a character's loneliness or hope look different, even in the same scene. In theater, light says as much as the dialogue does.

words.meaning: to shine (of the sun or moon)
words.defJa: 太陽や月が光を出して、あたりを明るくする。

cards.ja: 梅雨が明けて連日かんかんと日が照るようになると、熱中症で救急搬送される人が一気に増える。特に危ないのは、体がまだ暑さに慣れていない梅雨明け直後の時期だという。専門家は、外出の際には帽子や日傘を使い、のどが渇く前にこまめに水分をとるよう呼びかけている。室内でも、風通しが悪ければ油断はできない。
cards.en: Once the rainy season ends and the sun blazes down day after day, the number of people rushed to hospital with heatstroke jumps sharply. The most dangerous time is said to be right after the rainy season ends, when the body is not yet used to the heat. Experts urge people to use hats or parasols when going out and to drink water frequently, before they feel thirsty. Even indoors, you cannot let your guard down if the ventilation is poor.

words.meaning: development, turn of events (in a story or situation); rollout, expansion (of a business)
words.defJa: 物事や話が次々と進み、広がっていくこと。

cards.ja: 連続ドラマの最終回が放送されると、予想を裏切る展開にSNSは大いに盛り上がった。主人公を支えてきた親友こそが事件の真犯人だったという結末に、多くの視聴者が衝撃を受けたようだ。一方で、手がかりは序盤からきちんと示されていたと評価する声も目立つ。脚本家のよく練られた構成が、改めて注目を集めている。
cards.en: When the final episode of the drama series aired, social media lit up over the unexpected turn the story took. Many viewers seem to have been shocked by the ending, in which the best friend who had supported the protagonist turned out to be the real culprit. At the same time, many people praised the fact that the clues had been laid out properly from the early episodes. The screenwriter's carefully crafted structure is drawing renewed attention.

words.defJa: 電気を通すと光る、ガラスでできた明かりの部品。

cards.ja: 長年使ってきた白熱電球をLEDに替えたところ、電気代が目に見えて下がった。LEDは消費電力が少ないうえに寿命も長く、一度取り付ければ十年近く交換しなくて済むものもある。最近は、白っぽい光から、電球色と呼ばれる温かみのあるオレンジ色の光まで、色を選べる製品も多い。くつろぎたい寝室には、その電球色を選ぶ人が多いようだ。
cards.en: When I replaced the incandescent light bulbs I had used for years with LEDs, my electricity bill dropped noticeably. LEDs use little power and last a long time, and some of them need no replacing for nearly ten years once installed. Recently many products also let you choose the color of the light, from a whitish glow to the warm orange known as "light-bulb color." For the bedroom, where people want to relax, many seem to choose that warm light-bulb color.

words.defJa: 試験や試合などの成績を、数で表したもの。

cards.ja: テストの点数だけで子どもの力を測ることには、以前から疑問の声がある。ある中学校では、定期試験に加えて、調べ学習の発表やグループでの話し合いへの参加も評価に取り入れた。担任によると、点数が伸び悩んでいた生徒が発表で活躍し、自信をつけた例もあるという。数字には表れない成長をどう捉えるかが問われている。
cards.en: Doubts have long been raised about measuring children's abilities by test scores alone. One junior high school has begun including presentations on research projects and participation in group discussions in its assessments, in addition to regular exams. According to one homeroom teacher, there have been cases where students whose scores had stalled shone in their presentations and gained confidence. The question now is how to recognize growth that does not show up in numbers.

words.meaning: contagion, infection; spreading (of a mood or habit)
words.defJa: 病気や気分などが、人から人へうつって広がること。

cards.ja: 誰かがあくびをすると、つられて自分もあくびをしてしまう。こうした現象はあくびの伝染と呼ばれ、親しい相手ほど起こりやすいことが知られている。研究者の中には、他人の気持ちを感じ取る共感の働きと関係があると考える人もいる。笑いや不安が周りに伝染するのも、同じ仕組みによるのかもしれない。
cards.en: When someone yawns, you find yourself yawning too, as if pulled along. This phenomenon is called contagious yawning, and it is known to happen more readily the closer you are to the other person. Some researchers think it is linked to empathy, the capacity to sense other people's feelings. Perhaps laughter and anxiety spread to those around us through the same mechanism.

words.defJa: 化学の反応などを利用して、電気をためたり生み出したりする装置。

cards.ja: 電気自動車の普及に向けて、全固体電池の開発競争が世界中で激しくなっている。現在主流のリチウムイオン電池は内部に燃えやすい液体を使っているが、全固体電池ではこれを固体の材料に置き換える。そのため安全性が高く、短い時間で充電できる可能性がある。ただし、大量生産の技術やコストには、まだ多くの課題が残されている。
cards.en: With electric vehicles expected to spread, competition to develop all-solid-state batteries is heating up around the world. The lithium-ion batteries in mainstream use today contain a flammable liquid, but all-solid-state batteries replace it with a solid material. As a result, they are safer and could potentially be charged in a short time. However, many challenges still remain in mass-production technology and cost.

words.defJa: 電線や電話線を支えるために、道ばたに立てられた柱。

cards.ja: 日本の街並みを特徴づけるものの一つに、道路沿いに立ち並ぶ電柱がある。地震や台風で倒れると、道をふさいで救助や避難の妨げになるおそれがある。そのため国や自治体は電線を地中に埋める無電柱化を進めているが、工事費の高さから思うように進んでいない。欧米の主要都市と比べると、日本の取り組みはまだ遅れているのが現状だ。
cards.en: One of the things that characterize Japanese streetscapes is the utility poles lining the roads. If they topple in an earthquake or typhoon, they can block the roads and get in the way of rescue and evacuation. For this reason, the national and local governments are promoting the burial of power lines underground to remove the poles, but high construction costs mean progress has been slower than hoped. Compared with major cities in Europe and North America, Japan's efforts are still lagging behind.

words.meaning: here and there, dotted about; in drops
words.defJa: あちこちに、ぽつりぽつりと散らばっているようす。

cards.ja: 冬の朝、雪が積もった公園を歩いていると、小さな足跡が点々と続いているのに気づいた。たどっていくと植え込みの陰で途切れており、どうやらタヌキが餌を探して歩き回ったらしい。普段は人目を避けて暮らす動物たちも、雪の上にはその行動の跡がはっきりと残る。研究者にとって、冬は野生動物の暮らしをのぞく絶好の季節なのだ。
cards.en: Walking through a snow-covered park one winter morning, I noticed a line of small footprints dotted across the snow. When I followed them, they broke off in the shadow of some shrubs; apparently a raccoon dog had wandered around looking for food. Animals that usually live out of people's sight leave clear traces of their movements in the snow. For researchers, winter is the perfect season to peek into the lives of wild animals.

words.meaning: moving from place to place, drifting from one to another
words.defJa: 住む所や仕事などを、次々に移り変わっていくようす。

cards.ja: かつては一つの会社に定年まで勤めるのが当たり前で、職を転々とする人は根気がないと見られがちだった。しかし今では、経験を積むために数年ごとに職場を変えることを前向きに捉える企業も増えている。ある人材会社の担当者は、異なる業界で身につけた視点がむしろ強みになると話す。働き方をめぐる価値観は、この二十年で大きく変わった。
cards.en: It used to be taken for granted that you would work at one company until retirement, and people who drifted from job to job tended to be seen as lacking perseverance. Now, however, a growing number of companies view changing workplaces every few years to gain experience in a positive light. A representative of one recruitment firm says that perspectives gained in different industries can actually become a strength. Attitudes toward work have changed greatly over the past twenty years.

words.defJa: 日本国憲法で、日本国と日本国民統合の象徴と定められている地位。また、その地位にある人。

cards.ja: 日本国憲法では、天皇は日本国と日本国民統合の象徴と定められ、国の政治に関わる権限を持たない。国会の召集や法律の公布といった国事行為も、内閣の助言と承認に基づいて行われる。戦前の憲法で主権者とされていた立場とは、根本的に異なる位置づけだ。この象徴としてのあり方は、戦後の長い時間をかけて国民の間に定着してきた。
cards.en: Under the Constitution of Japan, the Emperor is defined as the symbol of the State and of the unity of the Japanese people, and has no powers related to government. Even acts in matters of state, such as convening the Diet and promulgating laws, are carried out on the advice and with the approval of the Cabinet. This is a fundamentally different position from that under the prewar constitution, in which the Emperor was the sovereign. This role as a symbol has taken root among the public over the long postwar decades.

words.defJa: 電気と磁気の波のうち、波長が比較的長く、通信や放送などに使われるもの。

cards.ja: 山奥のキャンプ場や地下の店で、スマートフォンの電波が届かず困った経験のある人は多いだろう。携帯電話会社は基地局を増やしてきたが、山間部や海の上まで地上の設備だけで覆うのは難しい。そこで注目されているのが、人工衛星から直接スマートフォンに電波を送る技術だ。実用化が進めば、災害で地上の設備が壊れたときにも連絡手段を確保できる。
cards.en: Many people have probably been stuck without a phone signal at a campsite deep in the mountains or in an underground shop. Mobile carriers have kept adding base stations, but covering mountain areas and the open sea with ground facilities alone is difficult. That is why a technology that sends radio signals directly from satellites to smartphones is attracting attention. If it comes into practical use, people will still have a way to communicate even when ground facilities are knocked out by a disaster.

words.defJa: 電気が導線などの中を流れること。また、その流れ。

cards.ja: 電気ウナギは獲物を見つけると、体内の発電器官から水中に強い電流を流し、相手をしびれさせる。その電圧は数百ボルトに達し、小さな魚なら一瞬で動けなくなる。一方、濁った水の中では弱い電気を出し続け、周りの様子を探っていることも知られている。こうした発電の仕組みをまねて、柔らかい電池をつくろうという研究も行われている。
cards.en: When an electric eel finds prey, it sends a strong electric current through the water from the electricity-generating organs in its body, stunning its target. The voltage reaches several hundred volts, enough to immobilize a small fish in an instant. In murky water, on the other hand, it is also known to keep giving off weak electric signals to sense its surroundings. Researchers are also working on soft batteries modeled on this power-generating mechanism.

words.meaning: electric power; electricity (as a supplied utility)
words.defJa: 電流が単位時間にする仕事の量。また、家庭や工場などに送られて使われる電気。

cards.ja: 猛暑の夏、電力の需給が最も厳しくなるのは、実は昼間よりも夕方だという。太陽光発電の出力が落ちていく時間帯に、帰宅した人々が一斉に冷房をつけるからだ。各地の電力会社は、需給がひっ迫しそうな日には家庭にも節電への協力を呼びかけている。蓄電池を備えた住宅が増えれば、この夕方の山を少しはならせるかもしれない。
cards.en: During a sweltering summer, electricity supply is said to be tightest not at midday but in the evening. That is because people coming home switch on their air conditioners all at once, just as solar output is falling off. On days when supply looks likely to run short, power companies around the country ask households to cooperate by saving electricity. If more homes had storage batteries, that evening peak might be smoothed out somewhat.

words.defJa: わからないことや確かめたいことを、相手に聞いて確認すること。

cards.ja: 新商品の発売初日、コールセンターでは朝から問い合わせの電話が鳴りやまなかった。多くは注文した品がいつ届くのかという内容で、担当者は昼食をとる暇もなかったという。会社は翌週、よくある質問をまとめたページをサイトに設け、チャットでの問い合わせも受け付けるようにした。その結果、電話の件数は半分ほどに減った。
cards.en: On the day a new product went on sale, the phones at the call center rang nonstop from the morning with inquiries. Most were about when ordered items would arrive, and the staff reportedly had no time even to eat lunch. The following week the company added a page of frequently asked questions to its website and began taking inquiries by chat as well. As a result, the number of calls fell by about half.

words.defJa: 赤みをおびた色の金属。電気や熱をよく伝え、電線などに使われる。

cards.ja: 電気をよく通す銅は、電線やモーターに欠かせない金属だ。電気自動車一台には、ガソリン車の数倍の銅が使われるといわれる。脱炭素の流れで需要が伸びる一方、新しい鉱山の開発には十年以上かかることも多い。そのため国際価格は高止まりし、使い終わった電線を回収して再利用する動きが広がっている。
cards.en: Copper, which conducts electricity well, is an indispensable metal for power lines and motors. A single electric vehicle is said to use several times as much copper as a gasoline car. While demand is growing with the shift toward decarbonization, developing a new mine often takes more than ten years. As a result, international prices have stayed high, and efforts to collect and reuse old wiring are spreading.

words.meaning: the same ~; the said ~ (referring back to something just mentioned)
words.defJa: 名詞の前につけて、「等しい」「変わらない」の意味を表す語。また、すでに話に出たものを指して、「その」「前に述べた」の意味を表す。

cards.ja: 大手家電メーカーは昨日、来年春に国内の二つの工場を閉鎖すると発表した。同社によると、生産は海外の拠点に移し、従業員は配置転換などで雇用を維持するという。工場の一つがある市の市長は、地域経済への影響が大きいと述べ、同社に詳しい説明を求める考えを示した。同社は昨年度まで二期連続で赤字を計上していた。
cards.en: A major home-appliance maker announced yesterday that it will close two of its domestic factories next spring. According to the company, production will be moved to overseas sites, and employees will keep their jobs through reassignments and other measures. The mayor of a city where one of the factories is located said the impact on the regional economy would be significant and indicated plans to ask the company for a detailed explanation. The company had posted losses for two consecutive fiscal years through last year.

words.defJa: ばらばらだったものを、一つにまとめること。また、そろえること。

cards.ja: 県内の市町村では、これまでごみの分別ルールがそれぞれ異なっていた。隣の町に引っ越しただけでプラスチックの出し方が変わり、戸惑う住民も少なくなかった。そこで県と全市町村が協議を重ね、来年度から分別の区分と収集袋の色を県全体で統一することを決めた。収集にかかる費用の削減にもつながると期待されている。
cards.en: Until now, the municipalities in the prefecture each had their own rules for sorting garbage. Simply moving to the next town changed how plastics had to be put out, and quite a few residents were confused. So the prefecture and all of its municipalities held a series of talks and decided that, from next fiscal year, the sorting categories and the colors of collection bags will be standardized across the whole prefecture. It is also expected to help reduce collection costs.

cards.ja: 二つの会社が合併するにあたり、新会社では両社の出身者を同格に扱うことが条件とされた。役員の数も半々とし、本社の機能も二つの都市に分けて置くという。どちらかが吸収されたという印象を与えないための配慮だ。ただ、こうした体制は意思決定が遅れやすいとの指摘もある。
cards.en: As the two companies merged, it was made a condition that people from both firms be treated as equals in the new company. The number of executives will also be split half and half, and headquarters functions will be divided between two cities. This is meant to avoid any impression that one side was absorbed by the other. However, some point out that such an arrangement tends to slow down decision-making.

words.defJa: 山道を登りつめて、そこから下りになる所。また、物事の勢いがいちばん盛んな時期。

cards.ja: かつて旅人たちは、この峠を越えて二つの地方を行き来した。標高およそ千メートルの峠の上には今も茶屋の跡が残り、昔の人はここで足を休めて一息ついたという。現在は山の下をトンネルが通り、車ならわずか数分で向こう側へ抜けられる。それでも週末になると、古い街道をたどって峠まで登るハイカーの姿が絶えない。
cards.en: In the past, travelers crossed this pass to go back and forth between the two regions. The remains of a teahouse still stand at the top of the pass, about 1,000 meters above sea level, where people of old are said to have rested their feet and caught their breath. Today a tunnel runs beneath the mountain, and by car you can get through to the other side in just a few minutes. Even so, on weekends there is a steady stream of hikers following the old highway up to the pass.

words.defJa: 体を動かすこと。また、機械が決められたとおりに動くこと。

cards.ja: 介護の現場では、立ち上がるときの一連の動作を細かく観察することが大切だとされる。椅子から立つには、足を手前に引いて前かがみになり、重心をお尻から足の裏へ移していく必要がある。この順序のどこかでつまずいている人は、手すりの位置を少し変えるだけで自力で立てるようになることもある。介助する側が力任せに引き上げると、かえって本人が自分の力を使う機会を奪ってしまう。
cards.en: In caregiving, it is considered important to closely observe the sequence of movements a person makes when standing up. To rise from a chair, you need to draw your feet back, lean forward, and shift your center of gravity from your buttocks to the soles of your feet. People who get stuck at some point in this sequence can sometimes stand on their own just by having a handrail moved slightly. If the caregiver simply hauls them up by force, it actually robs them of the chance to use their own strength.

words.meaning: east and west; East and West (cultures)
words.defJa: 東と西。また、東洋と西洋。

cards.ja: 洋の東西を問わず、人は昔から星空に物語を見いだしてきた。古代ギリシャでは星座に神話の英雄が重ねられ、中国では天の川をはさんで離ればなれになった男女の伝説が生まれた。地域も時代も異なるのに、夜空を眺めて想像をふくらませる心の動きはよく似ている。街の明かりで星が見えにくくなった今、こうした物語に触れる機会は減りつつある。
cards.en: In East and West alike, people have long found stories in the starry sky. In ancient Greece, mythical heroes were overlaid onto the constellations, while in China a legend arose of a man and a woman separated on either side of the Milky Way. Although the regions and eras differ, the urge to gaze at the night sky and let the imagination roam is strikingly similar. Now that city lights make the stars hard to see, chances to encounter such stories are dwindling.

cards.enTarget: In East and West alike, people have long found stories in the starry sky.

words.meaning: the day (of an event), the very day
words.defJa: 何かが行われる、その日。

cards.ja: 市民マラソンの当日は、朝から冷たい雨が降り続いた。それでも約五千人のランナーがスタート地点に集まり、沿道では家族や友人が傘を差して声援を送った。大会の事務局は、体が冷えた参加者のために、ゴール付近に温かい飲み物と毛布を用意した。中止を求める声もあったが、大きな事故もなく大会は無事に終わった。
cards.en: On the day of the city marathon, a cold rain fell steadily from the morning. Even so, some 5,000 runners gathered at the start, and along the route family and friends cheered them on under umbrellas. The organizers set out hot drinks and blankets near the finish line for participants who had gotten chilled. There had been calls to cancel, but the event ended safely without any serious accidents.

words.defJa: 岬や島に建てられ、夜に光を出して船に位置や危険を知らせる塔。

cards.ja: 岬の先端に立つ白い灯台は、明治時代に建てられたものだという。今では船の位置は人工衛星で正確にわかるようになり、灯台の役割はかつてほど大きくない。それでも、嵐の夜にこの光を頼りに港へ戻った経験を持つ漁師は多い。最近は内部が一般に公開され、らせん階段を上って海を見渡す観光客でにぎわっている。
cards.en: The white lighthouse at the tip of the cape is said to have been built in the Meiji era. Now that a ship's position can be pinpointed by satellite, the lighthouse's role is not as large as it once was. Even so, many fishermen have made it back to port on a stormy night guided by its light. Recently the interior has been opened to the public, and it bustles with tourists who climb the spiral staircase to look out over the sea.

cards.en: There has been a string of bicycle thefts at the bicycle parking area in front of the station. According to the police, in most cases the bikes had either not been locked or had only a thin cable lock. The city is adding security cameras and urging users to lock their bikes with two locks. If a bike is registered, it is easier to return it to its owner when it is found.

words.meaning: turn of duty; person on duty
words.defJa: 順番に受け持つ仕事。また、その仕事をする番に当たっている人。

cards.ja: 日本の小学校では、子どもたちが交代で給食当番を務める。白いエプロンと帽子を身につけ、給食室から大きな容器を教室まで運んで、おかずやご飯をクラス全員に配る。量を均等に分けるのは意外に難しく、最初はこぼしたり足りなくなったりすることも多い。海外の教育関係者からは、責任感や協調性を育てる仕組みとして注目されている。
cards.en: At Japanese elementary schools, children take turns on lunch duty. Wearing white aprons and caps, they carry large containers from the school kitchen to the classroom and serve side dishes and rice to the whole class. Dividing portions evenly is surprisingly hard, and at first they often spill food or run short. Educators abroad have taken notice of it as a system that fosters a sense of responsibility and cooperation.

words.defJa: 同じ量や大きさになるように分けること。

cards.ja: 丸いケーキを五人で分けるとき、きれいに等分するのは案外難しい。四つや八つなら半分に、さらに半分にと切っていけば済むが、五つとなると勘に頼るしかない。最近は、上にのせるだけで切る位置がわかる透明なガイドが製菓用品の店で売られている。子どもの誕生日会で取り合いにならないと、親たちに好評だという。
cards.en: When five people share a round cake, dividing it into equal pieces is surprisingly hard. With four or eight pieces you can just cut it in half and then in half again, but with five you have to rely on guesswork. These days, baking-supply shops sell transparent guides that show where to cut just by laying them on top. They are reportedly popular with parents because they prevent squabbles at children's birthday parties.

words.defJa: 石油からつくられる燃料の一つ。ストーブなどの暖房に使う。

cards.ja: 雪の多い地方では、冬になると灯油ストーブが暮らしに欠かせない。週に一度、移動販売の車が音楽を流しながら住宅街を回ってくると、住民たちはポリタンクを手に家から出てきて灯油を入れてもらう。ここ数年は原油高や円安の影響で価格が上がり、家計への負担を訴える声も多い。暖房費の一部を補助する自治体も出てきている。
cards.en: In snowy regions, kerosene heaters become indispensable to daily life once winter arrives. Once a week, when a mobile sales truck comes around the residential streets playing music, residents come out of their houses with plastic tanks to have them filled with kerosene. In recent years prices have risen because of high crude oil prices and the weak yen, and many people complain about the strain on household budgets. Some local governments have begun subsidizing part of residents' heating costs.

words.defJa: 子どものために書かれた、夢のある物語。

cards.ja: 世界中で読み継がれている童話の中には、もともと子ども向けではなかった話も少なくない。各地に伝わる昔話を集めた編者たちは、版を重ねるたびに表現を書き改め、家庭で読み聞かせやすい形にしていった。初版と後の版を読み比べると、実の母親が継母に変えられているなど、意外な違いが見つかる。子どものころに親しんだ物語の、思いがけない素顔が見えてくる。
cards.en: Among the fairy tales still read around the world, quite a few were not originally meant for children. The editors who collected folktales handed down in various regions revised the wording with each new edition, turning them into stories that were easier to read aloud at home. Compare a first edition with a later one, and you find surprising differences, such as a birth mother rewritten as a stepmother. The unexpected true face of tales we loved as children comes into view.

cards.en: One evening recently, an elderly man was crouched over on the riverside promenade. Two high school students who happened to be passing by called out to him and immediately called an ambulance. The man was on the verge of heatstroke, but because the two responded quickly, moving him into the shade and giving him water, his life was not in danger. The fire department later presented the two with certificates of appreciation.

cards.en: With homemade chocolate sweets, the step where things most often go wrong is actually the first one. Heating a chocolate bar directly in a pan over the flame makes it scorch or separate, so the basic method is to chop it finely and melt it slowly in a hot-water bath. The water should be around 50 degrees, and even a single drop of water getting in will ruin its smoothness.

words.meaning: to come to a point, to be pointed
words.defJa: 物の先が細くなって、するどくなる。

cards.ja: 寒い地域に生える針葉樹には、葉が細く先がとがっているものが多い。葉の表面積を小さくすることで、乾いた冷たい風に水分を奪われるのを防いでいるのだ。また、枝が下向きに傾いた円すい形の樹形は、積もった雪が滑り落ちやすい。厳しい環境に適応した結果、こうした独特の姿が生まれたと考えられている。
cards.en: Many conifers that grow in cold regions have narrow needles with pointed tips. By keeping the leaf surface small, they prevent the dry, cold wind from robbing them of moisture. In addition, a conical shape with branches angled downward makes it easy for accumulated snow to slide off. These distinctive forms are thought to have arisen through adaptation to a harsh environment.

cards.ja: 正月に食べる雑煮ほど、地域ごとの特色がはっきり表れる料理は珍しい。東日本では焼いた角餅をすまし汁に入れるのが一般的だが、西日本では丸餅が主流で、関西には煮た丸餅を白みそ仕立ての汁で食べる家庭も多い。中には、あんこ入りの餅を使う地方まであるという。転勤や結婚で別の土地の雑煮に出会い、その違いに驚く人は少なくない。
cards.en: Few dishes show regional character as clearly as zoni, the soup eaten at New Year. In eastern Japan it is common to put grilled square rice cakes into a clear broth, while in western Japan round rice cakes are the norm, and in the Kansai region many households simmer them and serve them in a white-miso broth. There is even said to be a region that uses rice cakes filled with sweet bean paste. Quite a few people are surprised by the difference when they first encounter another area's zoni after a job transfer or marriage.

Experts recommend checking the background carefully before posting and turning off location recording.

cards.ja: 都会から山あいの村に移り住んだ家族は、最初の一年、地域にどう溶け込むかに悩んだという。そこで、草刈りや祭りの準備といった共同作業には欠かさず顔を出すようにした。顔なじみが増えるにつれて、野菜のおすそ分けが届いたり、子どもに声をかけてもらったりすることが多くなった。今では村の行事の運営を任されるまでになっている。
cards.en: A family who moved from the city to a mountain village say that in their first year they struggled with how to fit into the community. So they made a point of always turning up for communal work such as cutting grass and preparing for festivals. As they got to know more people, neighbors increasingly dropped off shared vegetables or stopped to talk with their children. Now they have even been entrusted with running village events.

cards.en: For the big year-end cleaning, I make a point of moving the sofa and bookshelves, which normally stay put, out of the way and cleaning behind them. Not only has a year's worth of dust built up, but sometimes earrings I thought I had lost or the children's toys turn up. Moving heavy furniture alone can hurt your back, so it is best to get family members to help. Another trick is to lay a cloth under the legs and slide the furniture so the floor does not get scratched.

The autumn leaves dotted among trees that are still green look as if paint had been scattered across the hills. According to the meteorological observatory, because the summer heat lingered this year, the colors are running about a week behind the usual. The best viewing looks likely to come at the end of the month.

On the other hand, quite a few companies that value face-to-face meetings are moving into new buildings in the city center close to stations. The diversification of work styles is changing the very shape of the city.

In response, a growing number of companies are setting policies for dealing with abusive customers and putting systems in place to protect employees.

cards.en: In internal company documents, it used to be standard to add the honorific dono after a job title, as in 'Personnel Manager-dono'. cards.en: The Great Meireki Fire, which broke out in Edo in 1657, burned most of the city over three days. Fanned by a strong northwesterly wind, the flames spread from one area to the next, and people could do nothing but flee in confusion. The death toll is said to have reached tens of thousands, and the shogunate used the disaster as an opportunity to build a less flammable city, widening roads and creating firebreaks.

cards.ja: 「パンはパンでも食べられないパンは何か」。答えはフライパンだが、こうしたなぞなぞは、子どもが言葉の仕組みに気づく絶好の機会になる。同じ音の言葉が別の意味を持つことや、一つの言葉がいくつかの部分に分けられることを、遊びながら自然に学べるからだ。言語発達の研究者は、親子で問題を出し合うことを勧めている。
cards.en: 'What kind of pan (bread) can't you eat?' The answer is a frying pan, and riddles like this give children a perfect chance to notice how words work. That is because, through play, they naturally learn that words with the same sound can have different meanings and that a single word can be broken into several parts. Researchers in language development recommend that parents and children take turns posing riddles to each other.

cards.en: In front of the main hall of some old temples stands a wooden statue known as a 'stroking Buddha'. That is because of a tradition that if you stroke the part of the statue matching the ailing part of your own body, the illness will be cured. Touched by countless worshippers over the years, such statues have faces and knees worn smooth and shiny, so worn down that their original expression can hardly be made out.

That is because subjects that tend to look flat from the front gain a sense of three-dimensionality when shot at an angle. Professional photographers reportedly begin by walking around the subject to find the angle at which the light falls most beautifully.

cards.en: In workplaces where a culture of seniority runs deep, young employees who speak their minds frankly in meetings are sometimes seen as cheeky. One company says that after it began regularly holding sessions where anyone could speak regardless of rank, a new product came out of a young employee's proposal.

On weekends the sidewalks bustle with people who come to take photos, and the cafés facing the street fill up too. At the same time, the huge amount of fallen leaves is slippery and can cause falls on rainy days, so people from the shopping street keep sweeping every morning, brooms in hand.

cards.en: Inside Antarctica's thick ice, air from hundreds of thousands of years ago is trapped in tiny bubbles. Research teams have drilled down through the ice to depths of several thousand meters and analyzed the recovered columns of ice to study past temperatures and carbon dioxide levels. These records serve as important clues showing just how rapidly today's global warming is progressing.

cards.ja: 虹は、空気中の水滴に入った太陽の光が、中で屈折や反射をしながら色ごとに分かれることで生まれる。光は入ってきた側へはね返されるため、虹が見えるのは通常、太陽を背にしたときだ。夕立が上がった直後の夕方、東の空に大きな虹がかかりやすいのもこのためである。運がよければ、その外側に色の並びが逆になった薄い虹がもう一本見えることもある。
cards.en: A rainbow forms when sunlight entering water droplets in the air is refracted and reflected inside them and split into its colors. Because the light is bounced back toward the side it came from, you normally see a rainbow with the sun at your back. This is also why, in the evening just after a summer shower ends, a large rainbow so often appears in the eastern sky. If you are lucky, you may see a second, fainter rainbow outside it, with its colors in reverse order.

cards.en: It is not unusual for emails to go back and forth many times just to settle the date and time of a single meeting. So these days more and more workplaces use services that, once each person enters the times they are free, automatically suggest slots everyone can attend.

cards.ja: 以前参加したツアーの日程表には、朝から晩まで見どころがぎっしりと詰め込まれていた。一日に五か所も回ると、一つひとつをゆっくり味わう余裕はない。そこで今回は個人で旅をすることにし、日程の中にあえて何も予定を入れない半日を設けた。結果的に、旅でいちばん印象に残ったのはその半日だった。
cards.en: The itinerary of a tour I once joined was packed with sights from morning till night. When you visit as many as five places a day, there is no time to savor any of them properly. So this time I decided to travel on my own and deliberately set aside half a day in the schedule with nothing planned at all. As it turned out, that half day was what stayed with me most from the whole trip.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.enTarget: The itinerary of a tour I once joined was packed with sights from morning till night.

words.defJa: 刃物の切れ味が悪い。また、反応がおそい。

cards.ja: 長年使っている包丁の切れ味が鈍くなると、トマトの皮に刃が入らず、実がつぶれてしまう。料理人に言わせれば、切れない包丁は余計な力が要るぶん、かえってけがをしやすいそうだ。月に一度でも砥石で研いでおけば、切れ味は驚くほど戻る。研ぎ終えた包丁でトマトを切ると、皮に刃がすっと吸い込まれていく。
cards.en: When a kitchen knife you have used for years grows dull, the blade won't cut into a tomato's skin and the flesh gets crushed. According to chefs, a blunt knife needs extra force, so it is actually more likely to cause injuries. If you sharpen it on a whetstone even once a month, the edge comes back surprisingly well. Slice a tomato with a freshly sharpened knife, and the blade sinks smoothly through the skin.

cards.enTarget: When a kitchen knife you have used for years grows dull, the blade won't cut into a tomato's skin and the flesh gets crushed.

words.defJa: 会社に社員として入ること。

cards.ja: この会社では、入社してから最初の三か月間、新入社員がすべての部署を順番に回る。営業や経理だけでなく、地方の工場で生産ラインに立つこともある。会社全体の仕事の流れを肌で知ってもらうのが目的だ。正式な配属先が決まるのは、この研修を終えてからになる。
cards.en: At this company, for the first three months after joining, new employees rotate through every department in turn. Besides sales and accounting, they may even work on the production line at a regional factory. The aim is to have them experience firsthand how work flows through the whole company. Their official assignments are decided only after they finish this training.

cards.enTarget: At this company, for the first three months after joining, new employees rotate through every department in turn.

words.defJa: 自分の妻のことを、親しみをこめて言う言葉。

cards.ja: 定年退職した日、家に帰ると女房が赤飯を炊いて待っていた。四十年近く、朝早く出て夜遅く帰る暮らしで、家のことはほとんど任せきりだった。これからは料理くらい覚えようと台所に立ってみたものの、包丁の持ち方から笑われる始末だ。それでも、二人で並んで台所に立つ時間は悪くない。
cards.en: On the day I retired, I came home to find my wife waiting with festive red rice she had made. For nearly forty years I left early and came home late, leaving almost everything at home to her. I decided I would at least learn to cook from now on and stepped into the kitchen, only to be laughed at for the way I hold a knife. Still, the time the two of us spend standing side by side in the kitchen isn't bad at all.

words.defJa: 物事が急に起こるようす。突然。

cards.ja: 午後三時を過ぎたころ、晴れていた空がにわかに暗くなった。まもなく大粒の雨が降り出し、遠くで鳴っていた雷の音もみるみる近づいてきた。夏の山では、こうした急な天候の変化が珍しくない。登山の際は、午後の早い時間までに山小屋へ着くよう計画を立てるのが基本だ。
cards.en: Shortly after three in the afternoon, the clear sky suddenly darkened. Before long, large drops of rain began to fall, and the thunder that had been rumbling in the distance drew rapidly closer. Such abrupt changes in the weather are not unusual in the mountains in summer. When climbing, the basic rule is to plan so that you reach the mountain hut by early afternoon.

words.defJa: 針と糸で、布などをつなぎ合わせる。

cards.ja: 家庭科の授業で、子どもたちが初めてミシンを使ってエプロンを縫った。まっすぐ縫うだけでも思った以上に難しく、布がずれて縫い目が曲がってしまう子も多かった。先生は一人ひとりの机を回り、布の押さえ方を手を添えて教えていた。最後に完成したエプロンを身につけると、どの子も誇らしげな顔をしていた。
cards.en: In home economics class, the children used a sewing machine for the first time to sew aprons. Just sewing in a straight line was harder than they expected, and many of them saw the fabric slip and their seams go crooked. The teacher went around to each desk, guiding their hands to show them how to hold the fabric down. When they finally put on their finished aprons, every one of them looked proud.

words.defJa: 細長いものや体の一部を、回すようにしてひねる。

cards.ja: デスクワークで同じ姿勢が続くと、背中や腰の筋肉がこわばってくる。そんなときは椅子に座ったまま、上半身をゆっくり左右にねじってみるとよい。息を止めずに、吐きながら十秒ほどかけて回すのがこつだ。一時間に一度でも続ければ、夕方の疲れ方がかなり違ってくる。
cards.en: When you hold the same posture at a desk for a long time, the muscles in your back and lower back stiffen up. At times like that, it helps to stay seated and slowly twist your upper body to the left and right. The trick is to keep breathing and to turn over about ten seconds as you exhale. If you keep it up even once an hour, you will feel noticeably less tired by evening.

words.defJa: 火などで温度を上げる。あつくする。

cards.ja: 鉄道のレールは、夏の強い日差しで熱せられると、わずかに伸びる。そのため、レールの継ぎ目には数ミリのすき間が空けてある。列車が「ガタンゴトン」と音を立てるのは、車輪がこのすき間を通るときだ。最近は継ぎ目の少ない長いレールを使う区間が増え、あの音を聞く機会も減っている。
cards.en: Railway rails expand slightly when they are heated by strong summer sunlight. For that reason, a gap of a few millimeters is left at each joint between rails. The 'clackety-clack' a train makes is the sound of its wheels passing over these gaps. These days, more and more sections use long rails with few joints, so there are fewer chances to hear that sound.

words.defJa: 夜、寝るときに着る服。

cards.ja: 日本の旅館やホテルでは、部屋に浴衣が寝間着として用意されていることが多い。ただ、慣れない人が着て寝ると、朝には帯がほどけて前がすっかりはだけてしまいがちだ。最近は外国人客の増加を受けて、上下に分かれたパジャマを置く宿も増えてきた。浴衣で館内を歩くのは楽しいが、眠るときは別というわけだ。
cards.en: At Japanese inns and hotels, a yukata is often provided in the room to wear as nightclothes. But when people who aren't used to it sleep in one, by morning the sash has often come undone and the front has fallen completely open. Recently, with the rise in foreign guests, more places have started providing two-piece pajamas. Strolling around the inn in a yukata is fun, but sleeping in one is another matter.

words.defJa: 眠るときに身につける衣服。

cards.ja: 睡眠の専門家によれば、寝る前には部屋着のままでいるより、寝巻きに着替えたほうがよいという。着替えるという動作が、体と頭に「これから眠る」という合図を送るからだ。素材は汗をよく吸う綿やガーゼがすすめられる。締めつけの少ない形を選ぶことも、深い眠りにつくための大切な条件だ。
cards.en: According to sleep experts, before bed it is better to change into nightclothes than to stay in your loungewear. That is because the act of changing sends your body and mind the signal that it is time to sleep. Cotton or gauze, which absorb sweat well, are the recommended fabrics. Choosing a loose-fitting cut is also an important condition for falling into a deep sleep.

words.defJa: 目当てのものを決めて、それに向かって攻撃したり、手に入れようとしたりする。

cards.ja: 高齢者を狙った詐欺の手口が、年々巧妙になっている。最近は役所の職員を名乗って「医療費の払い戻しがある」と電話をかけ、ATMへ誘導するケースが目立つ。警察は、ATMの操作でお金が戻ってくることは絶対にないとして、少しでも怪しいと感じたらすぐに家族や警察に相談するよう呼びかけている。
cards.en: The methods used in scams targeting elderly people are growing more sophisticated year by year. Recently, a common pattern has been to phone while posing as a city-office employee, say 'You're due a refund of medical expenses,' and steer the victim to an ATM. Stressing that money is never refunded by operating an ATM, the police urge anyone who feels even slightly suspicious to consult their family or the police right away.

cards.enTarget: The methods used in scams targeting elderly people are growing more sophisticated year by year.

words.defJa: 仕事や会計の区切りとして決めた一年の期間。日本では四月から翌年の三月までが多い。

cards.ja: 日本では、役所や学校の多くが四月に始まり翌年三月に終わる「年度」で動いている。そのため三月は、予算の締めくくりや人事異動、引っ越しが重なり、一年でいちばん慌ただしい時期になる。年度末に道路工事が増えるのは、残った予算を使い切るためだと言われることもある。
cards.en: In Japan, most government offices and schools run on a fiscal year that begins in April and ends the following March. As a result, March, when the closing of budgets, personnel transfers and house moves all coincide, becomes the busiest time of the year. It is sometimes said that road works increase at the end of the fiscal year because offices are using up their leftover budgets.

cards.enTarget: In Japan, most government offices and schools run on a fiscal year that begins in April and ends the following March.

words.defJa: 住民の多くが農業をして暮らしている村や地域。

cards.ja: 若い世代の都市への流出が続き、多くの農村で耕す人のいない田畑が増えている。一方で、都会から移り住んで農業を始める人も少しずつ現れてきた。自治体の中には、空き家や農地を格安で貸し出し、移住者を呼び込もうとするところもある。地域の祭りや行事が、若い移住者の手で復活した例も珍しくない。
cards.en: As the younger generation continues to leave for the cities, fields with no one to till them are increasing in many farming villages. At the same time, people who move from the cities and take up farming have gradually begun to appear. Some local governments rent out vacant houses and farmland cheaply to try to attract newcomers. It is not unusual for local festivals and events to be revived by young people who have moved in.

cards.enTarget: As the younger generation continues to leave for the cities, fields with no one to till them are increasing in many farming villages.

words.defJa: 作物を虫や病気、雑草から守るために使う薬。

cards.ja: 農薬を使わずに野菜を育てるのは、思っている以上に手間がかかる。夏場は毎朝のように畑に出て、葉の裏についた虫を一匹ずつ手で取り除かなければならない。それでも収穫量は、一般的な栽培方法の半分ほどにとどまることもある。無農薬の野菜の値段が高めなのは、こうした労力が上乗せされているからだ。
cards.en: Growing vegetables without pesticides takes more work than you might think. In summer you have to go out to the field nearly every morning and pick the insects off the undersides of the leaves one by one by hand. Even so, the harvest sometimes comes to only about half that of conventional growing methods. Pesticide-free vegetables cost more because all this labor is added to the price.

words.meaning: efficiency (of work done in a given time)
words.defJa: 決まった時間の中で、どれだけ仕事や作業を進められるかの度合い。

cards.ja: 試験前になると夜遅くまで机に向かう学生は多いが、疲れた頭では能率が上がらない。睡眠不足のまま長時間勉強するより、早めに寝て朝の時間を使うほうが、覚えた内容も定着しやすいという研究もある。大切なのは、机に向かった時間の長さではなく、その中身だ。
cards.en: Many students sit at their desks until late at night before exams, but a tired brain does not work efficiently. Some research even suggests that going to bed early and using the morning hours helps what you have learned stick better than studying for long hours on too little sleep. What matters is not how long you spend at your desk but what you do with that time.

cards.enTarget: Many students sit at their desks until late at night before exams, but a tired brain does not work efficiently.

words.defJa: ひとつも欠けることなく、すべて。

cards.ja: 学生のころ、ある作家に夢中になり、図書館にあるその人の作品を一冊残らず読んだ。初期の短編から晩年の随筆まで読み進めるうちに、文体が少しずつ変わっていくのがわかった。若いころの華やかな言い回しは影をひそめ、晩年はごく平易な言葉で深いことを書いている。一人の作家を通して読むと、人間の成熟をたどるような面白さがある。
cards.en: As a student I became captivated by a certain writer and read every single one of their books in the library. As I read on from the early short stories to the essays of their final years, I could see the style gradually changing. The ornate phrasing of their youth faded away, and in later years they wrote about profound things in very plain words. Reading one writer all the way through has the fascination of tracing a person's growth toward maturity.

words.meaning: inbound (toward Tokyo or the city); ascent, uphill
words.defJa: 高い方へ進むこと。また、鉄道や道路で、東京や路線の起点に向かう方向。

cards.ja: お盆休みの最終日を迎えた今日、首都圏へ向かう高速道路の上り線では、帰省先から戻る車による渋滞が朝から続いている。渋滞は最も長いところで四十キロを超え、サービスエリアの駐車場も昼前には満車になった。道路会社は、混雑は夜遅くまで続く見込みだとして、出発の時間をずらすなどしてピークを避けるよう呼びかけている。
cards.en: Today, the last day of the Obon holidays, traffic has been backed up since morning on the inbound lanes of expressways heading into the Tokyo area, as cars return from hometown visits. At its longest the jam stretches more than forty kilometers, and service-area parking lots were full before noon. Expecting the congestion to last until late at night, the expressway companies are urging drivers to avoid the peak, for example by shifting their departure times.

words.defJa: 紙などをはりつけるのに使う、ねばりのあるもの。

cards.ja: 年末の大掃除で、久しぶりに障子を張り替えた。古い紙をはがした桟に、はけで薄くのりを塗り、新しい紙がたるまないように張っていく。のりが乾くと紙がぴんと張り、部屋がひときわ明るくなった。昔は米を煮て作ったのりを使ったそうだが、今はホームセンターで専用のものが手に入る。
cards.en: During the year-end cleaning, I re-papered the shoji screens for the first time in a while. On the frames stripped of their old paper, I brushed on a thin layer of paste and applied the new paper so that it would not sag. Once the paste dried, the paper pulled taut and the room became noticeably brighter. Apparently people used to use paste made by boiling rice, but now you can buy a purpose-made one at a home improvement store.

words.defJa: 途中で別の電車やバスに移って乗ること。

cards.ja: 初めての街で電車に乗るとき、スマートフォンの乗換案内アプリが欠かせないという人は多い。出発駅と到着駅を入力すれば、どの駅で乗り換えればよいかはもちろん、所要時間や運賃まで数秒で表示される。最近は混雑の予測や、何号車に乗れば階段に近いかまで教えてくれるものもある。かつて駅の路線図を見上げて悩んだ時間は、確実に短くなった。
cards.en: Many people say a transfer-and-route app on their smartphone is indispensable when taking trains in an unfamiliar city. Enter your departure and arrival stations, and within seconds it shows not only where to change trains but also the travel time and the fare. Some now go as far as predicting crowding and telling you which car to board to end up closest to the stairs. The time once spent puzzling up at the route maps in stations has certainly grown shorter.

words.meaning: transfer, change (of trains, buses, etc.); switching (to another product or service)
words.defJa: 途中で降りて、別の電車やバスなどに移ること。また、別のものに切り替えること。

cards.ja: 大きなターミナル駅では、乗り換えに十五分近くかかることも珍しくない。地下深くを走る路線から別の会社の路線へ移るには、長い通路を歩き、何度もエスカレーターを上り下りしなければならないからだ。大きな荷物を持った観光客が案内板の前で立ち止まる姿もよく見かける。駅の側も、多言語の表示や床の色分けで迷いにくくする工夫を重ねている。
cards.en: At large terminal stations, it is not unusual for a transfer to take close to fifteen minutes. That is because moving from a line that runs deep underground to one operated by a different company means walking down long passageways and riding escalators up and down again and again. It is also common to see tourists with large bags stopping in front of the information boards. Stations, for their part, keep coming up with ways to make them easier to navigate, such as multilingual signs and color-coded floors.

words.meaning: riding past one's station; travelling beyond the section one's ticket covers
words.defJa: 買った切符の区間より先の駅まで乗ること。

cards.ja: 紙の切符で電車に乗り、予定より先の駅まで行くことになっても、途中で切符を買い直す必要はない。降りた駅の改札の手前にある精算機に切符を入れれば乗り越しの運賃が表示されるので、その分を払うだけで済む。交通系のICカードなら改札を通るだけで自動的に精算されるため、精算機の前に列ができる光景は昔に比べてずいぶん減った。ただし、残高が足りないと改札で止められてしまうので、チャージは早めにしておきたい。
cards.en: If you board a train with a paper ticket and end up going beyond the station you planned, there is no need to buy a new ticket along the way. At the station where you get off, insert your ticket into the fare-adjustment machine just before the gates and it shows the fare for the extra distance, so you only have to pay that amount. With a transit IC card the fare is settled automatically as you pass through the gate, so lines in front of fare-adjustment machines are far less common than they used to be. If your balance runs short, however, the gate will stop you, so it is best to top up ahead of time.

words.defJa: 細かいことを気にせず、あまり心配しないようす。

cards.ja: 周りから「のんきだね」と言われる人は、締め切りが迫っても慌てず、失敗してもあまり引きずらない。せっかちな人から見ると危なっかしく映るが、こうした性格には意外な強みもあるらしい。ストレスをため込みにくい傾向があるともいわれる。もっとも、度を越すと大事な約束を忘れたり、準備不足で周囲に迷惑をかけたりするので、ほどほどが肝心だ。
cards.en: People whom others call "so easygoing" don't panic even when a deadline looms, and they don't dwell much on their mistakes. To impatient people they can look like an accident waiting to happen, but this kind of temperament apparently has some surprising strengths. Such people are also said to be less prone to letting stress build up. That said, taken too far it can mean forgetting important appointments or causing trouble for those around them by being underprepared, so moderation is key.

cards.enTarget: People whom others call "so easygoing" don't panic even when a deadline looms, and they don't dwell much on their mistakes.

words.defJa: 白と黒の間の、燃えたあとの灰のような色。

cards.ja: 江戸時代の後半、幕府はたびたびぜいたくを禁じ、庶民が派手な色の着物を着ることを制限した。そこで人々は、許された茶色や灰色の中に微妙な違いを見つけ、それぞれに粋な名前をつけて楽しんだ。灰色の仲間だけで百種類近くの呼び名があったともいわれる。地味に見える色に美しさを見いだす感覚は、今の和の配色にも受け継がれている。
cards.en: In the late Edo period, the shogunate repeatedly banned luxury and restricted commoners from wearing brightly colored kimono. So people found subtle differences within the browns and greys that were still permitted, gave each one a stylish name, and enjoyed them. It is said there were nearly a hundred names for shades of grey alone. That sensibility of finding beauty in seemingly plain colors lives on in traditional Japanese color schemes today.

words.defJa: 五・七・五の十七音で作る、季語を入れた日本の短い詩。

cards.ja: 五・七・五のわずか十七音で季節や心の動きを表す俳句は、世界で最も短い詩の一つとされる。近年はテレビ番組で芸能人の作品を専門家が添削する企画が人気を集め、若い世代にも関心が広がっている。SNSに日々の一句を投稿する人も珍しくない。英語やフランス語で作る愛好家も多く、海外の学校の授業で取り上げられることもある。
cards.en: Haiku, which expresses the seasons or stirrings of the heart in just seventeen morae (sound units) arranged five-seven-five, is considered one of the shortest forms of poetry in the world. In recent years, TV segments in which experts correct poems by celebrities have become popular, and interest has spread to younger generations as well. It is not unusual for people to post a daily verse on social media. There are also many enthusiasts who write haiku in English or French, and the form is sometimes taken up in school lessons abroad.

words.defJa: 駅や病院、球場などの中にある、小さな店。

cards.ja: プロ野球の球場では、試合そのものと同じくらい売店めぐりを楽しみにしているファンが多い。各球団は地元の名物を使った弁当や、選手がプロデュースしたメニューを競うように売り出している。試合前や攻守の交代の時間には、どの店の前にも長い列ができる。最近はスマートフォンで注文し、席まで届けてもらえる仕組みを取り入れた球場も増えてきた。
cards.en: At professional baseball stadiums, many fans look forward to making the rounds of the food stands as much as to the game itself. Each team competes to launch bento boxes made with local specialties and menu items developed by its players. Before the game and between innings, long lines form in front of every stand. Recently, more stadiums have adopted systems that let fans order on their smartphones and have food delivered to their seats.

words.meaning: buying and selling, trade (esp. of property or shares)
words.defJa: 物を売ったり買ったりすること。

cards.ja: 空き家が増える地方では、古い住宅の売買を手助けする自治体の取り組みが広がっている。持ち主が手放したい物件の情報を集め、ウェブサイトで紹介する「空き家バンク」はその代表例だ。都会から移り住みたい人にとっては、格安で家を手に入れる機会にもなる。ただ、建物の傷みが激しく、修理に思わぬ費用がかかるケースもあるため、契約前の確認が欠かせない。
cards.en: In rural areas where vacant houses are increasing, municipal efforts to help with the buying and selling of old homes are spreading. A typical example is the "vacant house bank," which gathers information on properties their owners want to part with and presents them on a website. For people who want to move from the city, it can also be a chance to get a house cheaply. However, because some buildings are badly deteriorated and repairs can cost unexpectedly large sums, checking carefully before signing a contract is essential.

words.meaning: to crawl, to creep (on hands and knees or on the belly)
words.defJa: 手足や腹を地面につけて、ゆっくり進む。

cards.ja: 夏の夜、ウミガメの産卵地として知られる砂浜では、ふ化したばかりの子ガメが一斉に砂の中から姿を現す。手のひらに乗るほどの小さな体で、子ガメたちは月明かりに照らされた海のほうへ懸命に這っていく。ところが、近くの道路や建物の明かりに引き寄せられ、反対の方向に進んでしまうこともある。そのため一部の地域では、この時期に海岸沿いの照明を控えるよう呼びかけている。
cards.en: On summer nights, at beaches known as sea turtle nesting sites, freshly hatched baby turtles emerge from the sand all at once. With bodies small enough to sit in the palm of a hand, the hatchlings crawl with all their might toward the moonlit sea. However, they are sometimes drawn by the lights of nearby roads and buildings and head off in the opposite direction. For that reason, some areas ask people to refrain from using coastal lighting during this season.

words.meaning: to peel off, to tear off, to strip
words.defJa: 表面にくっついているものを、引っぱって取る。

cards.ja: 賃貸の部屋でも模様替えを楽しみたいという人に、貼って剥がせる壁紙が人気だ。裏面の粘着力が弱めに作られているため、引っ越しのときにはきれいに剥がして元の状態に戻せる。ただし、古い壁や湿気の多い場所では、剥がすときに下の壁紙ごと破れてしまうことがある。目立たない場所で試してから全面に貼るのが、失敗しないこつだという。
cards.en: Peel-and-stick wallpaper is popular with people who want to enjoy redecorating even in a rented apartment. Because the adhesive on the back is made fairly weak, you can peel it off cleanly when you move out and restore the room to its original state. However, on old walls or in damp places, the wallpaper underneath can tear along with it when you peel it off. The trick to avoiding failure, apparently, is to test it in an inconspicuous spot before covering the whole wall.

cards.en: Many municipalities ask residents to remove the label and cap when putting out PET bottles as recyclables. This is because they are made of a different material from the bottle itself, and leaving them mixed in lowers the quality of the recycled material. Yet quite a few people find peeling off the labels a hassle. So recently more drinks have been sold in bottles without labels, with the product name and other details stamped directly onto the container.

words.defJa: 物の重さを量るための道具。

cards.ja: 小学三年生の算数では、重さの単位とともに、はかりの使い方を学ぶ。子どもたちは教室にある身の回りの物を台に載せ、針が指す目盛りを読んで記録していく。見た目が大きい物ほど重いと思い込んでいた子が、結果を見て首をかしげる場面もある。実際に手で持ち比べた感覚と数字を結びつけることが、この単元の大きな狙いだという。
cards.en: In third-grade math at elementary school, children learn how to use scales along with units of weight. They place everyday objects from the classroom on the platform, read the mark the needle points to, and record it. Sometimes a child who assumed that bigger-looking things are always heavier tilts their head in puzzlement at the result. A major aim of the unit, apparently, is to connect the feel of comparing objects in one's hands with the numbers.

words.defJa: 胃がむかむかして、もどしそうになる感じ。

cards.ja: 夏場に気をつけたいのが、熱中症の初期症状を見逃さないことだ。めまいや立ちくらみに加えて、頭痛や吐き気を感じたら、体の中の水分や塩分がかなり失われているサインだといわれる。すぐに涼しい場所へ移り、首やわきの下を冷やしながら水分をとることが大切だ。自分で飲めないほど具合が悪いときは、迷わず救急車を呼ぶよう医師は呼びかけている。
cards.en: In summer, it is important not to overlook the early symptoms of heatstroke. In addition to dizziness and lightheadedness on standing up, a headache or nausea is said to be a sign that your body has lost a considerable amount of water and salt. It is important to move to a cool place right away and drink fluids while cooling your neck and armpits. Doctors urge people to call an ambulance without hesitation when they feel too sick to drink on their own.

words.defJa: 周りにぎざぎざの歯がついた輪で、かみ合わせて回転を伝えるもの。

cards.ja: 江戸時代のからくり人形の一つ、茶運び人形は、盆に茶碗を載せると客に向かって進み、客が茶碗を取ると止まる。飲み終えた茶碗を盆に戻すと、くるりと向きを変えて元の場所へ帰っていく。その動きを生み出しているのは、木で作られた歯車とクジラのひげを使ったぜんまいだ。電気を動力として使わずに、職人たちは工夫を重ねてこうした複雑な仕組みを実現した。
cards.en: The tea-serving doll, one of the karakuri automata of the Edo period, moves toward a guest when a teacup is placed on its tray and stops when the guest picks the cup up. When the empty cup is put back on the tray, it turns around and returns to where it started. What produces this movement are gears made of wood and a spring made from whale baleen. Without using electricity as a power source, craftsmen achieved such complex mechanisms through sheer ingenuity.

cards.en: On escalators in stations and shopping facilities, accidents in which children's shoes or trouser hems get caught in the gap between the steps and the side keep happening. Sandals made of soft material in particular are easily pulled in and can lead to injuries. The Consumer Affairs Agency urges people to stand inside the yellow lines and for parents to hold their children's hands while riding. Recently, more models are being equipped with mechanisms that stop automatically when they detect a foreign object.

cards.en: The origin of the sandwich is said to go back to eighteenth-century England. The story goes that it began when a nobleman engrossed in a card game had meat brought to him between slices of bread so he could eat without dirtying his hands. It reached Japan in the Meiji era, and today convenience stores stock sandwiches filled with all kinds of things, from egg and cutlets to fruit. The fruit sandwich, which pairs whipped cream with fruit, is a uniquely Japanese item that surprises even overseas travelers.

words.meaning: ladder; (fig.) going from one place to the next, as in bar-hopping
words.defJa: 高い所に上り下りするための道具で、二本の長い棒の間に足をかける横木を並べたもの。

cards.ja: 建設現場や工場で起きる労働災害のうち、大きな割合を占めるのが高い所からの転落だ。中でも、はしごや脚立を使った作業中の事故は、高さが二メートルに満たなくても大けがにつながることがある。ある会社では、はしごの使用前に足元の固定や角度を二人で確認するルールを設けた。小さな手間を惜しまないことが、命を守る最も確実な方法だという。
cards.en: Among the occupational accidents that occur at construction sites and factories, falls from heights account for a large share. Accidents during work on ladders or stepladders in particular can lead to serious injuries even when the height is less than two meters. One company introduced a rule requiring two people to check the footing and angle of a ladder before it is used. Not begrudging small efforts like these, it says, is the surest way to protect lives.

words.defJa: 物事がスタートしたばかりのところで。最初の部分で。

cards.ja: ニュース番組の始めに、その日の主な項目を短くまとめて伝える形は、多くの局で定着している。視聴者が最初の数十秒で、見続けるかどうかを決めてしまうからだ。動画配信サイトでも同じ傾向があり、冒頭で内容の見どころを示す作品ほど最後まで見られやすいという。限られた時間で関心をつかむ工夫は、作り手にとって避けて通れない課題になっている。
cards.en: The format of briefly summarizing the day's main stories at the start of a news program has become standard at many stations. This is because viewers decide within the first few dozen seconds whether to keep watching. The same tendency is seen on video-streaming sites, where videos that show their highlights at the outset are reportedly more likely to be watched to the end. Finding ways to capture interest in limited time has become an unavoidable challenge for creators.

cards.ja: 報告書やメールを書くとき、初めに結論を述べるよう指導する会社は多い。読み手は忙しく、要点がどこにあるのか分からない文章は最後まで読んでもらえないからだ。結論の後に理由や根拠を示し、最後にもう一度要点をまとめれば、伝わりやすさは大きく変わる。一方、日本語の手紙や挨拶では、本題の前に季節の言葉を置く習慣が今も大切にされている。
cards.en: Many companies instruct employees to state their conclusion first when writing reports or emails. This is because readers are busy, and a text in which they can't tell where the main point lies won't be read to the end. If you give your reasons and evidence after the conclusion and then summarize the key point once more at the end, it makes a big difference in how well the message gets across. On the other hand, in Japanese letters and greetings, the custom of placing seasonal phrases before the main subject is still valued today.

cards.ja: 我が家の斜向かいに、小さなパン屋ができた。夫婦二人で切り盛りしている店で、毎朝六時前から焼きたての香りが通りに漂ってくる。開店からまだ半年ほどだが、昼前には人気の食パンが売り切れてしまう日も多い。最近は近所の人たちが店先で立ち話をする姿も見かけるようになり、静かだった通りが少しにぎやかになった。

It has been open for only about half a year, but on many days their popular loaf of white bread sells out before noon. Lately I've also begun to see neighbors chatting in front of the shop, and the once-quiet street has become a little livelier.

words.meaning: underwear, undergarment worn next to the skin
words.defJa: 肌にじかに触れるように着る衣類。下着。

cards.ja: 冬に人気の「着るだけで温かい」肌着には、汗などの水分を吸うと熱を出す繊維が使われている。体から出る水蒸気が繊維に吸い込まれる際、水分子が繊維と結びつくことでエネルギーが熱として放出される仕組みだ。ただし、吸える水分の量には限りがあるため、大量に汗をかくとかえって体が冷えることもある。運動するときは、汗をすばやく外に逃がす素材を選ぶのがよいとされる。
cards.en: Winter's popular "warm just by wearing it" underwear uses fibers that give off heat when they absorb moisture such as sweat. The mechanism is that when water vapor from the body is absorbed into the fibers, water molecules bind to the fibers and energy is released as heat. However, because there is a limit to how much moisture the fibers can absorb, sweating heavily can actually leave the body chilled. When exercising, it is considered better to choose materials that quickly wick sweat away.

words.meaning: really, actually (in doubtful questions); sure enough
words.defJa: 疑問の文で「本当に」「いったい」という気持ちを表す言葉。

cards.ja: 朝食に何を食べるか、どの道を通って駅へ向かうか、私たちは毎日自分の意志で選んでいると感じている。だが、脳の活動を調べた実験の中には、本人が決めたと自覚する少し前に、脳がすでに準備を始めていることを示したものもある。そうだとすれば、人間に果たして自由な意志があると言えるのだろうか。哲学者や科学者の間で、この問いをめぐる議論は今も続いている。
cards.en: What to eat for breakfast, which route to take to the station: we feel that we choose these things every day of our own free will. Yet some experiments examining brain activity have shown that the brain has already begun preparing slightly before the person becomes aware of having decided. If that is so, can we really say that humans have free will? Among philosophers and scientists, the debate over this question still continues.

cards.ja: 政府は物価高への対策として、家庭の電気代やガス代を補助する制度を延長すると発表した。冬場の負担が和らぐことを歓迎する声がある一方で、効果は一時的で、根本的な解決にはならないという指摘も根強い。補助を続けるために必要な財源は、数兆円規模に上る。果たしてこの支出に見合う成果が得られるのか、国会でも厳しい議論が予想される。

While some welcome the easing of the burden in winter, there are also persistent criticisms that the effect is temporary and will not provide a fundamental solution. The funds needed to keep the subsidies going run to several trillion yen. A heated debate is expected in the Diet as well over whether the spending will really yield results to justify it.

cards.ja: 東京発の夜行バスは、今も学生や若い旅行者を中心に根強い人気がある。夜に出発して翌朝には目的地に着くため、宿代を一泊分浮かせられるのが最大の魅力だ。最近は座席の間をカーテンで仕切り、横になれるほど背もたれが倒れる車両も登場した。新幹線より時間はかかるが、料金の安さと快適さを両立させる工夫が利用者を引きつけている。
cards.en: Overnight buses departing from Tokyo remain firmly popular, especially among students and young travelers. Because they leave at night and arrive at their destination the next morning, their biggest attraction is that you can save the cost of a night's lodging. Recently, vehicles have appeared that separate seats with curtains and have backrests that recline far enough to lie down. They take longer than the shinkansen, but the efforts to combine low fares with comfort are drawing riders.

words.defJa: 新しい考えを思いつくこと。また、その考え方。

cards.ja: 新しい商品を生み出すには、これまでの常識にとらわれない発想が欠かせない。ある文具メーカーでは、商品企画の会議に営業や工場の担当者だけでなく、入社したばかりの若手も必ず参加させている。経験の浅い社員の素朴な疑問が、思いがけないヒットにつながったことが何度もあるからだ。発想の転換を促すには、多様な視点が自由に交わる場づくりが大切だという。
cards.en: Creating new products requires ideas that aren't bound by conventional wisdom. At one stationery maker, newly hired young employees are always included in product-planning meetings, not just staff from sales and the factory. That is because naive questions from inexperienced employees have led to unexpected hits on several occasions. To encourage a shift in thinking, the company says, it is important to create a space where diverse perspectives can mix freely.

words.defJa: 電気をつくり出すこと。

cards.ja: インドでは近年、太陽光による発電が急速に広がっている。日差しの強い西部の砂漠地帯には、見渡す限りパネルが並ぶ世界有数の規模の施設が建設された。人口の増加と経済成長で電力の需要は今後も伸び続けると見込まれており、政府は石炭への依存を減らす目標を掲げている。一方で、天候に左右されやすい電力をどう安定して届けるかが大きな課題だ。
cards.en: In India, solar power generation has been spreading rapidly in recent years. In the sun-drenched desert region of the west, one of the world's largest facilities has been built, with panels lined up as far as the eye can see. Demand for electricity is expected to keep growing with population increase and economic growth, and the government has set targets to reduce dependence on coal. At the same time, a major challenge is how to deliver power that is easily affected by the weather in a stable way.

words.defJa: 関係する人どうしが、意見を出して相談すること。

cards.ja: 隣の家の騒音や庭木の枝の越境など、近所どうしのもめごとに関する相談が各地の自治体に寄せられている。ある市が作った手引きでは、まず当事者間の「話合い」による解決を勧めている。直接話すことが難しい場合は、市の相談窓口や裁判所の調停を利用する方法も紹介されている。いきなり訴訟に踏み切るより、時間も費用も抑えられることが多いという。
cards.en: Municipalities around the country are receiving consultations about disputes between neighbors, such as noise from the house next door or tree branches crossing the property line. A guide produced by one city recommends first trying to resolve the matter through "discussion" between the parties involved. For cases where talking directly is difficult, it also introduces options such as the city's consultation desk and court mediation. This often keeps both time and costs down compared with jumping straight into a lawsuit, it says.

words.defJa: お互いに意見を出し合って、相談すること。

cards.ja: 年老いた親の介護をどうするかは、多くの家族にとって避けて通れない問題だ。誰がどれだけ担うのか、費用をどう分けるのかを曖昧にしたままだと、後から兄弟の間に深い溝が生まれかねない。専門家は、親が元気なうちに家族で話し合いの場を持ち、本人の希望も聞いておくよう勧めている。早めに話しておくことが、結果的に家族の関係を守ることにつながるという。
cards.en: How to handle the care of aging parents is an unavoidable issue for many families. If it remains unclear who will take on how much and how costs will be divided, deep rifts can later open up between siblings. Experts recommend that families sit down for a discussion while their parents are still healthy, and that they also hear what the parents themselves want. Talking things over early, they say, ultimately helps protect family relationships.

cards.ja: 一人暮らしの高齢者の間で、話しかけると答えてくれるAIスピーカーやロボットを使う人が増えている。天気や薬の時間を尋ねるだけでなく、昔の思い出を話して相づちを打ってもらうのが楽しみだという人もいる。離れて暮らす家族にとっても、会話の記録から親の様子を知る手がかりになる。ただ、機械との会話が人とのつながりの代わりになるのかについては、慎重な見方もある。
cards.en: Among elderly people living alone, more and more are using AI speakers and robots that answer when spoken to. Some say they enjoy not only asking about the weather or when to take their medicine but also talking about old memories and having the device chime in with responses. For family members living far away, the conversation logs also offer clues to how their parents are doing. However, some take a cautious view of whether conversations with machines can substitute for connections with people.

cards.ja: 体調を崩して近所の診療所に電話をかけたのに、何度かけても話し中でつながらない。そんな経験から、受診をあきらめてしまう人も少なくないという。特に冬の感染症が流行する時期は、朝の受付開始と同時に電話が殺到する。こうした状況を受け、ウェブやアプリで予約や問診ができる仕組みを導入する医療機関が増えている。
cards.en: You feel unwell and call the local clinic, but no matter how many times you try, the line is busy and you can't get through. Reportedly, quite a few people give up on seeing a doctor after experiences like that. Especially during the winter season when infectious diseases are spreading, calls flood in the moment morning reception opens. In response, more medical institutions are introducing systems that allow appointments and preliminary questionnaires to be completed on the web or through an app.

cards.ja: 夏の夜空を彩る花火大会は、江戸時代から続く日本の風物詩である。近年は打ち上げの費用や警備の負担が増え、開催を見送る地域も出てきた。それでも、有料の観覧席を設けたり、企業から協賛金を募ったりして、伝統を守ろうとする動きが広がっている。地元の人々にとって、花火は夏そのものなのだ。
cards.en: Fireworks festivals that color the summer night sky are a seasonal tradition in Japan dating back to the Edo period. In recent years, the cost of the launches and the burden of security have grown, and some areas have begun to forgo holding them. Even so, efforts to preserve the tradition are spreading, such as setting up paid viewing seats and seeking sponsorship money from companies. For local people, fireworks are summer itself.

words.defJa: 結婚式を挙げる女性。また、結婚したばかりの女性。

cards.ja: 式場の扉が開くと、白いドレス姿の花嫁が父親と腕を組んでゆっくりと入ってきた。最近は披露宴を省き、家族だけで食事会を開く夫婦も増えている。それでも、この入場の場面だけは残したいという声は根強い。式場の担当者は「多くの方がここで涙ぐまれます」と話す。
cards.en: When the doors of the wedding hall opened, the bride in a white dress walked slowly in, arm in arm with her father. These days, more couples are skipping the reception and holding just a dinner with family. Even so, many still want to keep at least this entrance scene. A staff member at the venue says, "Many people are moved to tears at this moment."

words.meaning: to jump, to leap; to splash, to spatter
words.defJa: 地面や水面などから、勢いよく飛び上がる。

cards.ja: 川や湖で、魚が水面から勢いよく跳ねる姿を見かけることがある。なぜ跳ねるのかについては、体についた寄生虫を落とすため、天敵から逃げるためなど、いくつもの説がある。ある研究チームは定点カメラで水面の撮影を続け、水温や時間帯によって跳ねる回数が変わることを突き止めた。身近な光景にも、まだ解明されていない謎が残っている。
cards.en: In rivers and lakes, you sometimes see fish leaping vigorously out of the water. As for why they jump, there are several theories, such as to shake off parasites clinging to their bodies or to escape predators. One research team kept filming the water's surface with fixed cameras and found that the number of jumps changes with the water temperature and the time of day. Even familiar sights still hold mysteries that have yet to be solved.

cards.ja: 食後すぐの歯磨きは歯を傷めるという話を聞いたことがある人も多いだろう。酸性の飲み物を飲んだ直後は歯の表面が柔らかくなっているため、強くこするとすり減るおそれがあるからだ。ただし歯科医の団体は、ふだんの食事のあとであれば、すぐに磨いて問題ないとしている。大切なのは時間よりも、毎日丁寧に続けることだという。
cards.en: Many people have probably heard the claim that brushing your teeth right after eating damages them. The reasoning is that right after you drink something acidic, the surface of the teeth is softened, so scrubbing hard could wear it down. However, an association of dentists says that after an ordinary meal, there is no problem with brushing right away. What matters, it says, is not the timing but keeping it up carefully every day.

words.defJa: 話すのがとても速いこと。また、そのような話し方。

cards.ja: ニュースを読むアナウンサーは、一分間におよそ三百字のペースで話すよう訓練される。これより速いと早口に聞こえ、内容が頭に入りにくくなるからだ。ところが最近は動画を倍速で見る習慣が広がり、若い世代ほど速い話し方に慣れているとの調査もある。聞き取りやすい速さの基準も、時代とともに変わっていくのかもしれない。
cards.en: Announcers who read the news are trained to speak at a pace of about three hundred characters a minute. That is because anything faster sounds rushed, and the content becomes harder to take in. Recently, however, the habit of watching videos at double speed has spread, and one survey even suggests that the younger the generation, the more used it is to fast speech. The standard for an easy-to-follow speed may also change with the times.
