cards.en: In the cold season, a long, slow soak in a bath that is not too hot is said to be good for you. Bathing for about ten minutes in water of around 40 degrees warms the body to the core and also helps you fall asleep. Water that is too hot, on the other hand, raises blood pressure sharply, so older people in particular need to be careful. Drinking a glass of water before and after bathing is also recommended.

This record has become a valuable source for understanding the starting point of modern medicine in Japan.

Only now do I realize that this casual greeting was a signal by which we confirmed each other was safe and well.

cards.ja: お気に入りのウールのセーターを洗濯機で洗ったら、子ども服のように縮んでしまった。これは、羊毛の表面に細かいうろこ状の組織があり、水と摩擦によって繊維どうしが絡み合うためだ。洗う際は水温を低めに保ち、手で軽く押し洗いするのがよい。最近は、洗濯機で丸洗いできる加工を施した製品も増えている。
cards.en: I washed my favorite wool sweater in the washing machine, and it shrank to the size of a child's. This happens because wool fibers have tiny scale-like structures on their surface, and water and friction make the fibers tangle together. When washing wool, it is best to keep the water cool and gently press-wash by hand. Recently, more products have been treated so they can go straight into the washing machine.

cards.ja: 昭和の面影を残すその喫茶店では、白いエプロン姿のウエートレスが、今も銀の盆でコーヒーを運んでくる。常連客の好みをすべて覚えていて、注文を聞く前に角砂糖を好みの数だけ用意してくれるという。最近の飲食店では、性別を問わないホールスタッフという呼び方が一般的になった。それだけに、この店の光景はどこか懐かしく映る。
cards.en: At that coffee shop, which keeps the feel of the Showa era, waitresses in white aprons still bring coffee on silver trays. They reportedly remember every regular's preferences and even have the right number of sugar cubes ready before taking the order. At restaurants these days, the gender-neutral term floor staff has become common. That makes the scene at this shop feel all the more nostalgic.

words.meaning: to appear (in a photo), to be photographed; to show through
words.defJa: 写真などに、姿や形がとらえられて現れる。また、裏や下にあるものが透けて見える。

cards.ja: 実家の押し入れを片づけていたら、色あせた家族写真が一枚出てきた。そこには、まだ若い両親と、母に抱かれた赤ん坊の私が写っていた。裏には撮影した日付と、近所の写真館の名前が鉛筆で記されている。何千枚でも気軽に撮れる今とは違い、一枚の写真が特別な重みを持っていた時代だ。
cards.en: While tidying a closet at my parents' house, I came across a faded family photo. In it were my parents, still young, and me as a baby in my mother's arms. On the back, the date it was taken and the name of a local photo studio are written in pencil. Unlike today, when you can casually take thousands of pictures, it was an era when a single photograph carried special weight.

words.defJa: 小麦粉をこねて、太く長く切った白いめん。

cards.ja: 香川県では、うどんは単なる食事ではなく、暮らしに根づいた文化そのものだ。県内には人口の割に驚くほど多くの店があり、朝食代わりに一杯すする人も珍しくない。セルフ式の店では、客が自分で麺を湯に通し、好みの天ぷらやねぎをのせる。一杯数百円という手軽さも、県外から訪れる観光客をひきつけている。
cards.en: In Kagawa Prefecture, udon is not just a meal but a culture rooted in daily life. The prefecture has a surprisingly large number of shops for its population, and it is not unusual for people to slurp down a bowl in place of breakfast. At self-service shops, customers warm the noodles in hot water themselves and top them with their choice of tempura and green onions. The ease of a bowl costing just a few hundred yen also draws tourists from outside the prefecture.

words.meaning: to nod (in agreement or to show one is listening)
words.defJa: 相手の話に同意したり、聞いていることを示したりするために、首を縦に軽く振る。

cards.ja: 人の話を聞くとき、適度にうなずくだけで相手の話しやすさは大きく変わる。ある心理学の実験では、聞き手がうなずきを控えると、話し手の発言量が目に見えて減ったという。ただし、何にでも機械的に首を縦に振っていると、かえって話を聞いていない印象を与えかねない。大切なのは、内容に合わせて自然に反応することだ。
cards.en: When you listen to someone, simply nodding at the right moments makes a big difference in how easy it is for them to talk. In one psychology experiment, when listeners held back their nods, the amount the speakers said dropped noticeably. On the other hand, nodding mechanically at everything can actually give the impression that you are not listening. What matters is reacting naturally to what is being said.

words.meaning: presence or absence; whether or not something exists
words.defJa: あるかないかということ。

cards.ja: 介護業界は人手不足が深刻で、多くの施設が経験の有無を問わずに職員を募集している。採用担当者によると、重視するのは資格よりも、人と接することへの意欲や体力だという。入社後は先輩について現場を回り、半年ほどで一通りの仕事をこなせるようになる人が多い。未経験から挑戦する転職者にとって、門戸の広い業界といえる。
cards.en: The nursing-care industry faces a serious labor shortage, and many facilities recruit staff regardless of whether they have experience. According to hiring managers, what they value more than qualifications is a willingness to work with people, along with physical stamina. After joining, many new hires shadow senior staff on the floor and can handle the full range of tasks within about six months. For career changers starting without experience, it is an industry with its doors wide open.

cards.ja: 山の天気は変わりやすく、ふもとが晴れていても山頂付近では急に気温が下がることがある。一般に、標高が100メートル上がるごとに気温はおよそ0.6度下がるとされる。真夏の登山でも、薄手の上着を一枚リュックに入れておくと安心だ。風が強い日は体感温度がさらに下がるので、風を通しにくいものを選びたい。
cards.en: Mountain weather changes easily, and even when it is sunny at the foot of a mountain, the temperature near the summit can drop suddenly. It is generally said that the temperature falls by about 0.6 degrees for every 100 meters of elevation gained. Even on a midsummer hike, it is reassuring to keep a light jacket in your backpack. On windy days the temperature you feel drops even further, so it is best to choose one that blocks the wind.

words.meaning: a lot, very much, a great deal
words.defJa: 量や程度がとても大きいようす。たくさん。

cards.ja: 高校時代の野球部の監督は、「うんと食べて、うんと寝ろ」が口癖だった。当時は根性論のように聞こえたが、今では成長期の体づくりに十分な栄養と睡眠が欠かせないことがよく知られている。練習量だけを増やしても、体が回復しなければ力はつかない。監督の言葉は、案外理にかなっていたのだ。
cards.en: My high school baseball coach always used to say, "Eat plenty and sleep plenty." Back then it sounded like mere tough-guy talk, but it is now well known that ample nutrition and sleep are essential for building the body during the growth years. Simply increasing the amount of practice will not make you stronger if your body cannot recover. The coach's words made more sense than they seemed.

words.meaning: um, er, let me see (hesitation filler)
words.defJa: 言葉に詰まったときや、次に言うことを考えているときに口にする言葉。

cards.ja: 話の途中で「ええと」や「あのー」と言ってしまうのを、悪い癖だと考える人は多い。しかし言語学では、こうした言葉はフィラーと呼ばれ、話し手が次の言葉を探していることを相手に伝える役割があるとされる。実際、まったく言いよどまない話し方は、かえって原稿を読んでいるような印象を与えることもある。大切なのは、使いすぎないことだ。
cards.en: Many people regard saying "um" or "er" in the middle of speaking as a bad habit. In linguistics, however, such words are called fillers and are thought to signal to the listener that the speaker is searching for the next word. In fact, speaking without any hesitation at all can instead give the impression that you are reading from a script. What matters is not to overuse them.

cards.en: When the season for infectious diseases arrives, posters at stations and hospitals urge people to follow "cough etiquette." It means wearing a mask when you cough or sneeze, or covering your mouth and nose with a tissue or your sleeve. If you cover them with your hand, the virus may spread through the straps and doorknobs you then touch. It is a small courtesy, but it helps protect the people around you.

cards.en: Once a month, a cooking class for elementary school children is held at the local community center. The children put on aprons they have brought from home, tie back their hair and head to the cooking stations. That day's menu was miso soup and rice balls, and the instructor carefully taught everything, starting with how to hold a kitchen knife. As the children ate the food they had made themselves, they looked quietly proud.

cards.en: At an orchestra concert, there is a moment before the performance when all the players sound the same note at once. This is called tuning, and in most cases everyone matches the A played by the oboe. That is because the oboe's tone carries well and its pitch is stable. It is a ritual lasting only a few dozen seconds, but it is also the moment when the atmosphere in the hall grows taut.

cards.en: On car factory assembly lines, robots have long handled much of the welding and painting. While this advance of automation has raised productivity, it has also reduced jobs for people doing simple, repetitive work. Recently, the wave of automation has spread to logistics and agriculture, which suffer from labor shortages. The question of which jobs will be left for people is being asked anew.

cards.en: Scientists sometimes try to grasp the overall picture of a problem through rough estimates, without fussing over precise figures. For example, even a question like "How many piano tuners are there in the country?" can be answered to the right order of magnitude by making assumptions about the number of households, how common pianos are and how often they are tuned. Estimates like this are sometimes even posed in company job interviews. The point is not the exact answer but showing the line of reasoning.

words.meaning: thanks to you; fortunately (polite reply about one's health or circumstances)
words.defJa: 相手や周りの人の助けに感謝しながら、無事であることやうまくいったことを伝えるあいさつ。

cards.ja: 「お元気ですか」と聞かれて「おかげさまで」と答えるのは、日本語の典型的なあいさつの一つだ。相手が直接何かをしてくれたわけではなくても、周りの人々の支えに対する感謝を込めて使われる。もともと「おかげ」は神や仏の助けを指す言葉で、それが人の助け全般へと広がったとされる。短い一言の中に、人とのつながりを大切にする感覚が息づいている。
cards.en: Answering "Thanks to you, I'm fine" when asked "How are you?" is one of the most typical exchanges in Japanese. It expresses gratitude for the support of the people around you, even if the listener has not directly done anything for you. The underlying word originally referred to the help of gods and buddhas, and is said to have broadened to mean help from people in general. Within this short phrase lives a sense of valuing one's ties with others.

words.defJa: ご飯といっしょに食べる料理。肉や魚、野菜などを使ったもの。

cards.ja: 日本の弁当は、限られた箱の中にいくつものおかずを詰める工夫に特徴がある。卵焼きや焼き魚、煮物などを彩りよく並べ、ご飯との量のバランスも考える。最近では、前の晩に多めに作った料理を冷凍しておき、朝はそれを詰めるだけという人も多い。手間を減らしながら品数を保つ知恵といえる。
cards.en: Japanese bento are known for the ingenuity of packing several dishes into a small box. Rolled omelet, grilled fish, simmered vegetables and the like are arranged for color, with the balance against the amount of rice also considered. These days, many people make extra food the night before, freeze it, and simply pack it in the morning. It is a clever way to keep up the variety of dishes while cutting down on work.

words.meaning: please don't go to any trouble (for me)
words.defJa: 自分のために特別な気づかいやもてなしをしなくてよい、と相手に伝える言葉。

cards.ja: 友人の家を訪ねると、彼女は慌ててお茶やお菓子を用意し始めた。「すぐ帰るから、どうぞおかまいなく」と声をかけたが、結局テーブルにはたくさんの皿が並んだ。日本では、客がこう言って遠慮するのも、それでも招いた側がもてなすのも、どちらも礼儀の一部である。そのやり取り自体が、一種の決まった会話になっているのだ。
cards.en: When I visited a friend's home, she hurriedly began preparing tea and sweets. I told her, "I'm leaving soon, so please don't go to any trouble," but in the end the table filled up with plates. In Japan, the guest holding back with these words and the host offering hospitality anyway are both part of good manners. The exchange itself has become a kind of set conversation.

At work it is normal to use the polite full form, but among family and friends the short version is enough. A greeting is also a small act of care toward the people close to you.

words.defJa: 「待ってください」をていねいに言う言葉。

cards.ja: 企業のコールセンターに電話をかけると、「このまましばらくお待ちください」という音声が延々と続くことがある。こうした待ち時間を減らすため、AIが用件を聞き取り、よくある質問にはその場で答える仕組みを導入する企業が増えている。複雑な相談だけを人間の担当者に回すことで、オペレーターの負担も軽くなる。ただ、機械相手では話しにくいと感じる利用者もまだ少なくない。
cards.en: When you call a company's call center, the recording "Please hold for a moment" can go on and on. To cut such waiting times, more and more companies are introducing systems in which AI listens to the caller's request and answers common questions on the spot. Routing only complicated inquiries to human staff also lightens the operators' load. Still, quite a few users feel it is hard to talk to a machine.

words.meaning: sorry to have kept you waiting (casual, homely)
words.defJa: 待たせた相手に、親しみを込めて言うあいさつ。食べ物を出すときなどに使う。

cards.ja: 昔ながらのそば屋では、店主が丼を運んでくるとき「はい、おまちどおさま」と声をかけることが多い。チェーン店の決まり文句と比べると、どこか温かく、下町らしい響きがある。出前が盛んだった時代には、配達先の玄関でもよく聞かれた言葉だ。最近の若い店員が使うことは少なくなったが、この一言に店の人柄を感じる客もいる。
cards.en: At old-fashioned soba shops, the owner often says "Here you are, sorry for the wait" when bringing a bowl to the table. Compared with the stock phrases of chain restaurants, it has a warm, old-neighborhood ring to it. In the days when food delivery was common, it was also often heard at customers' front doors. Young staff rarely use it these days, but some customers sense the character of the shop in this one phrase.

words.defJa: 祝うのにふさわしいようす。喜ばしい。

cards.ja: 日本では、結婚式や長寿の祝いなど、おめでたい席に鯛が出されることが多い。鯛の赤い色が縁起のよい色とされるうえ、名前が「めでたい」に通じるからだ。同じように、紅白のまんじゅうや赤飯も祝い事に欠かせない。食べ物に願いを込める習慣は、今も多くの家庭や地域に受け継がれている。
cards.en: In Japan, sea bream is often served on happy occasions such as weddings and celebrations of long life. That is because its red color is considered lucky, and its name, tai, echoes medetai, meaning joyous. Likewise, red-and-white buns and red bean rice are essential at celebrations. The custom of putting wishes into food is still handed down in many homes and communities.

words.defJa: 食事と食事の間に食べる軽い食べ物。特に午後に食べるお菓子など。

cards.ja: 「おやつ」という言葉は、江戸時代の時刻の呼び方に由来する。当時は今の午後2時から4時ごろを「八つ」と呼び、この時間に軽い食事をとる習慣があった。一日二食が一般的だった時代には、この間食が働く人々の大切な栄養補給だったという。やがて「お八つ」という言い方が定着し、今では時間に関係なく間食全般を指すようになった。
cards.en: The word oyatsu comes from the way time was reckoned in the Edo period. Back then, roughly 2 to 4 p.m. by today's clock was called the hour of "yatsu" (eight), and people had the custom of eating a light meal at that time. In an era when two meals a day were the norm, this snack is said to have been an important source of nourishment for working people. Eventually the polite form o-yatsu took hold, and today it refers to snacks in general, whatever the time.

words.defJa: 鍵盤を押し、空気でリードやパイプを鳴らして音を出す楽器。

cards.ja: 明治時代に西洋式の音楽教育が始まると、全国の小学校に足踏み式のオルガンが置かれるようになった。ピアノに比べて安く、調律の手間も少なかったためだ。昭和の頃まで、音楽の授業では先生がオルガンを弾き、子どもたちがそれに合わせて歌うのがおなじみの光景だった。今でも古い校舎の一角に、当時のオルガンが大切に残されていることがある。
cards.en: When Western-style music education began in the Meiji era, pedal-operated organs came to be placed in elementary schools across the country. That was because they were cheaper than pianos and needed less tuning. Until around the Showa era, a teacher playing the organ while the children sang along was a familiar scene in music class. Even today, organs from those days are sometimes carefully kept in a corner of old school buildings.

cards.ja: 就職活動の面接では、志望する会社のことを「御社」と呼ぶのが一般的だ。一方、履歴書やメールなどの書き言葉では「貴社」を使うのが慣例になっている。話し言葉で「きしゃ」と言うと、「記者」や「汽車」と聞き間違えられやすいためだといわれる。細かな使い分けだが、面接官は意外とよく見ている。
cards.en: In job interviews, it is standard to refer to the company you are applying to as onsha. In written documents such as resumes and emails, on the other hand, the convention is to use kisha. This is said to be because, spoken aloud, kisha is easily misheard as the words for reporter or steam train. It is a subtle distinction, but interviewers notice it more than you might think.

words.defJa: 夏に多い小さな虫で、雌が人や動物の血を吸う。かゆみや病気の原因になる。

cards.ja: 世界で最も多くの人の命を奪っている生き物は、サメでもヘビでもなく、蚊だといわれる。マラリアやデング熱などの感染症を媒介し、毎年数十万人が亡くなっているからだ。日本でも2014年、都内の公園で刺された人を中心に、デング熱の国内感染が相次いだ。夏場の屋外では、虫よけや長袖で肌を守ることが勧められている。
cards.en: The creature said to kill more people than any other is not the shark or the snake but the mosquito. That is because it spreads infectious diseases such as malaria and dengue fever, which kill hundreds of thousands of people every year. In Japan, too, a string of locally acquired dengue cases occurred in 2014, centered on people bitten in a park in Tokyo. When outdoors in summer, people are advised to protect their skin with insect repellent and long sleeves.

cards.ja: 海沿いの道を走る路線バスは、岬に差しかかると急なカーブが続く。運転手はスピードを落とし、対向車に注意しながらゆっくりとハンドルを切っていく。窓の外には、曲がるたびに違う角度から海が見えてくる。乗り物に弱い人は、前寄りの席で進行方向を向いて座ると酔いにくいそうだ。
cards.en: The local bus that runs along the coastal road meets a series of sharp curves as it approaches the cape. The driver slows down and turns the wheel gently, watching for oncoming cars. Out the window, the sea comes into view from a different angle at every bend. People prone to motion sickness are said to feel less queasy if they sit near the front, facing the direction of travel.

cards.ja: 春の干潟は、潮が引くと、砂の中からアサリなどの貝を掘る潮干狩りの人々でにぎわう。こうした二枚貝は、海水を吸い込んでプランクトンをこし取り、水をきれいにする働きも担っている。しかし、埋め立てによって干潟が減り、貝の数も大きく減った。海の浄化役を守ることは、豊かな漁場を守ることにもつながる。
cards.en: In spring, when the tide goes out, tidal flats bustle with people digging short-necked clams and other shellfish out of the sand. Bivalves like these also help clean the water by drawing in seawater and filtering out plankton. However, land reclamation has shrunk the tidal flats, and shellfish numbers have fallen sharply. Protecting these natural cleaners of the sea also helps protect rich fishing grounds.

Many locations, mainly inland, recorded extremely hot days with highs of 35 degrees or more, and one person after another was taken to hospital with heatstroke. The Japan Meteorological Agency is urging people to drink water frequently and to use air conditioning sensibly. The heat is expected to continue tomorrow.

words.defJa: ある数を、もう一つの数の回数だけ足し合わせる計算。

cards.ja: 日本の小学生は、二年生になると九九を覚える。「ににんがし」「にさんがろく」とリズムに乗せて唱えるうちに、自然とかけ算の答えが口から出てくるようになる。この暗記法のおかげで、日本の子どもは計算が速いといわれることもある。一方で、意味を理解せずに丸暗記するだけでは応用がきかないとして、図を使って考える授業も増えている。
cards.en: Japanese children learn the multiplication table by heart in their second year of elementary school. As they chant "two twos are four, two threes are six" to a rhythm, the answers to multiplication problems start coming out of their mouths naturally. Thanks to this memorization method, Japanese children are sometimes said to calculate quickly. On the other hand, since rote memorization without understanding leaves pupils unable to apply it, more lessons now use diagrams to think problems through.

words.defJa: 見た目を美しくするために付けたり置いたりするもの。

cards.ja: 北欧の家具が日本で人気を集める理由の一つは、余計な飾りのないシンプルなデザインにある。木の質感を生かし、暮らしに静かになじむ形は、日本の伝統的な美意識とも通じるところがある。装飾をそぎ落とすほど、素材の良さや作り手の技術がはっきりと表れる。長く使うほど味わいが増すのも魅力だ。
cards.en: One reason Scandinavian furniture is popular in Japan is its simple design, free of unnecessary ornament. Its forms, which bring out the texture of the wood and blend quietly into daily life, have something in common with traditional Japanese aesthetics. The more decoration is stripped away, the more clearly the quality of the materials and the skill of the maker show through. Another appeal is that it gains character the longer it is used.

Her polite speech and efficiency made me feel I understood why guests have loved this inn for so long.

When winter comes they dig them up, deftly gnaw the hard shells until they split in two, and eat the kernels inside. Some of the walnuts that are buried and forgotten sprout in spring and eventually grow into new trees. In other words, a small animal's winter meals also play a part in spreading the forest.

They can't match digital streaming for sound quality, but many people are reportedly drawn to the design of the palm-sized cases, or even enjoy the bother of rewinding the tape. At one used-record shop in Tokyo, sales of related products far exceeded the previous year's after it set up a dedicated section.

words.meaning: katakana (the angular Japanese syllabary used mainly for loanwords)
words.defJa: 日本語の文字の一つ。主に外来語や擬音語を書くのに使う、角ばった形の文字。

cards.ja: 日本語では、外国から入ってきた言葉の多くをカタカナで書き表す。ところが最近は、ビジネスの場でカタカナ語が増えすぎて、かえって意味が伝わりにくいという声も多い。会議で「エビデンス」や「アジェンダ」と言われても、すぐには理解できない人もいるだろう。言い換えられる日本語があるなら、そちらを使うほうが親切だという意見もある。
cards.en: In Japanese, most words that have come in from abroad are written in katakana. Recently, however, many people complain that katakana words have multiplied so much in business settings that meaning actually becomes harder to get across. Some people probably can't immediately understand when they hear “evidence” or “agenda” in a meeting. There is also a view that if a Japanese word can say the same thing, using it is more considerate.

Thanks to boldly getting rid of things I don't use, it looks like I can start my new life unburdened. All that remains is the change-of-address paperwork at the city office.

words.meaning: (large hanging) bell, especially a temple bell
words.defJa: 寺などにつるし、太い棒でついて鳴らす大きな金属の器具。

cards.ja: 大みそかの夜、各地の寺で、鐘を百八回つく「除夜の鐘」が響き渡る。百八という数は人間の煩悩を表すとされ、一回つくごとに心の迷いを払うという意味が込められている。近年は「音がうるさい」という苦情を受け、昼間につく寺も出てきた。伝統と地域の暮らしをどう両立させるかが問われている。
cards.en: On New Year's Eve, the year-end bells ring out from temples across the country, each struck 108 times. The number 108 is said to represent human worldly desires, and each strike carries the meaning of dispelling one of the heart's delusions. In recent years, after complaints that the noise is too loud, some temples have started ringing the bell in the daytime. The question now is how to reconcile tradition with the life of the local community.

words.meaning: cover (e.g., a paper book cover or protective case); also, making up for a shortfall
words.defJa: 物を包んだり覆ったりして守るもの。本の表紙を包む紙など。

cards.ja: 日本の書店で文庫本を買うと、店員に「カバーをおかけしますか」と聞かれることが多い。紙のカバーをかけておけば、電車の中で何を読んでいるか周りに知られずに済む。この習慣は海外から来た旅行者の目には珍しく映るらしく、各店のデザインを集めて楽しむ人もいる。最近は環境への配慮から、希望した人にだけかける店も増えている。
cards.en: When you buy a paperback at a Japanese bookstore, the clerk will often ask, “Would you like a cover on it?” With a paper cover on, you can read on the train without the people around you knowing what you're reading. The custom apparently looks unusual to travelers from abroad, and some enjoy collecting the different shops' designs. Recently, out of concern for the environment, more shops have started putting covers only on the books of customers who ask for one.

words.defJa: 口の中でかんで味わい、飲み込まずに捨てる菓子。

cards.ja: 仕事中にガムをかむと集中力が高まるという研究結果がある。あごを繰り返し動かすことで脳への血流が増え、眠気が抑えられると考えられている。長距離トラックの運転手の中にも、眠くなりそうなときは必ずガムを口に入れるという人が少なくない。ただし、接客中や会議中にかむのは、日本ではまだ失礼だと受け取られやすい。
cards.en: There are research findings that chewing gum while working improves concentration. Repeatedly moving the jaw is thought to increase blood flow to the brain and keep drowsiness at bay. Quite a few long-haul truck drivers, too, say they always pop a piece of gum in their mouths when they feel sleepiness coming on. However, chewing it while serving customers or in meetings is still apt to be taken as rude in Japan.

cards.enTarget: There are research findings that chewing gum while working improves concentration.

words.meaning: song, ballad; popular song (mostly in compounds, for Showa-era Japanese pop)
words.defJa: 多くの人に親しまれ、広く歌われる歌。特に昭和の流行歌を指すことが多い。

cards.ja: 昭和の歌謡曲が、いま十代や二十代の間で人気を集めている。動画配信サイトで偶然耳にした曲をきっかけに、当時のレコードを買い求める若者も珍しくない。覚えやすいメロディーと、恋や別れをまっすぐに描いた歌詞が、かえって新鮮に感じられるのだろう。親や祖父母の世代と同じ歌を口ずさめることで、家族の会話が弾むこともあるようだ。
cards.en: Popular songs from the Showa era are now winning fans among people in their teens and twenties. It is not unusual for young people to go looking for records from that time after happening to hear a song on a video-sharing site. Perhaps the catchy melodies and lyrics that portray love and parting so directly feel all the fresher for being old. Being able to hum the same songs as their parents' and grandparents' generations also seems to get conversation flowing in some families.

words.meaning: shell, husk (of an egg, nut, shellfish, etc.)
words.defJa: 卵や貝、木の実などの外側を包んでいる硬いもの。

cards.ja: ゆで卵の殻がきれいにむけないと、白身がぼろぼろになってしまう。料理研究家によると、ゆで上がったらすぐに冷水につけるのがこつだという。急に冷やすことで中身がわずかに縮み、殻との間にすき間ができるためだ。新鮮すぎる卵はかえってむきにくいので、買ってから数日置いたものを使うとよいそうだ。
cards.en: If the shell of a boiled egg won't peel off cleanly, the white ends up in tatters. According to a cooking expert, the trick is to plunge the eggs into cold water as soon as they are done. Cooling them suddenly makes the inside shrink slightly, creating a gap between it and the shell. Very fresh eggs are actually harder to peel, so it is said to be best to use ones that have sat for a few days after purchase.

words.meaning: color (as in color TV or color printing); also, collar
words.defJa: 色。白黒ではなく、色がついていること。

cards.ja: 日本でテレビのカラー放送が始まったのは、1960年のことだ。当初は受像機が非常に高価だったため、多くの家庭ではしばらく白黒テレビが使われ続けた。1964年の東京五輪は、カラーテレビへの関心を高める大きなきっかけとなった。それでも、一般の家庭にまで広く行き渡ったのは、1970年代に入ってからである。
cards.en: Color television broadcasting began in Japan in 1960. At first the sets were extremely expensive, so many households went on using black-and-white televisions for some time. The 1964 Tokyo Olympics gave a major boost to interest in color TV. Even so, it was not until the 1970s that color sets spread widely into ordinary homes.

words.meaning: to tease, to make fun of
words.defJa: 冗談を言ったりして、相手を困らせたり笑いものにしたりする。

cards.ja: 小学生のころ、私は名前が珍しいという理由で、よく同級生にからかわれた。相手は軽い冗談のつもりだったのかもしれないが、言われる側にとっては毎日が苦痛だった。大人になった今は、子どもどうしの何気ないやり取りにも気を配るようにしている。冗談といじめの境目は、本人にしか分からないことが多いからだ。
cards.en: When I was in elementary school, my classmates often teased me because my name was unusual. They may have meant it as a light joke, but for me, on the receiving end, every day was painful. Now that I'm an adult, I make a point of paying attention even to children's casual exchanges with one another. That's because the line between a joke and bullying is often something only the person concerned can see.

words.meaning: karuta (traditional Japanese card game, esp. the poem-matching game)
words.defJa: 読み上げられた札に合う札を取り合う、日本の伝統的なカードの遊び。

cards.ja: 百人一首を使った競技かるたは、記憶力と瞬発力が求められる本格的な頭脳スポーツだ。選手は百首の歌をすべて暗記したうえで、読み手の声に反応して札を払い取る。上級者になると、最初の一音が聞こえた瞬間に手が動くという。漫画や映画の影響で、近年は学校の部活動として取り組む生徒も増えている。
cards.en: Competitive karuta, played with the Hundred Poets cards, is a full-fledged mind sport that demands memory and lightning reflexes. Players memorize all one hundred poems and then sweep the right card away in response to the reader's voice. Top players are said to move their hands the instant they hear the first syllable. Thanks to the influence of manga and films, more students have taken it up as a school club activity in recent years.

words.meaning: to dry (something), e.g. laundry or hair
words.defJa: ぬれている物から水分を取り除いて、水気をなくす。

cards.ja: 洗濯物を早く乾かすには、気温よりも湿度と風が重要だといわれる。空気が湿っていると、布に含まれた水分がなかなか蒸発しないからだ。部屋干しの場合は、扇風機で風を当てたり除湿機を使ったりすると、乾くまでの時間を大幅に短くできる。生乾きのにおいを防ぐためにも、できるだけ短い時間で乾かしきることが大切だ。
cards.en: To dry laundry quickly, humidity and air flow are said to matter more than temperature. That's because when the air is damp, the water held in the fabric is slow to evaporate. When hanging clothes indoors, blowing air on them with a fan or running a dehumidifier can greatly shorten the drying time. Getting them fully dry as quickly as possible also matters for preventing that musty, half-dried smell.

cards.ja: 通勤ラッシュの時間帯、都心の地下鉄はわずか二分ほどの間隔で運行している。一本の電車が少しでも遅れると、後ろを走る電車も次々に詰まってしまう。そのため鉄道会社は、駅での乗り降りにかかる時間を秒単位で分析し、ダイヤの乱れを最小限に抑えようとしている。
cards.en: During the commuter rush, subway trains in the city center run at intervals of only about two minutes. If a single train is delayed even slightly, the trains running behind it bunch up one after another. That is why railway companies analyze the time passengers take to get on and off at stations down to the second, trying to keep timetable disruptions to a minimum.

cards.ja: 確定申告の期限が近づくと、税務署の窓口には長い列ができる。期限を過ぎてから申告すると、本来の税額に加えて延滞税などを納めなければならない場合がある。最近はスマートフォンからも手続きができるようになり、窓口に足を運ぶ人は年々減っている。国税庁も、期限ぎりぎりではなく早めの申告を呼びかけている。
cards.en: As the deadline for filing tax returns approaches, long lines form at the counters of tax offices. If you file after the deadline, you may have to pay late-payment tax and other charges on top of the tax originally owed. Recently it has become possible to file from a smartphone, and the number of people who go to the counter is falling year by year. The National Tax Agency is also urging people to file early rather than at the last minute.

cards.ja: 禁酒法時代のアメリカを舞台にしたギャング映画は、今も根強い人気がある。密造酒で富を築いた組織の興亡が、華やかな衣装やジャズとともにドラマチックに描かれるからだ。ただ、現実の暴力の歴史を美化しているという批判も、新作が公開されるたびに繰り返されてきた。
cards.en: Gangster films set in Prohibition-era America remain enduringly popular. That is because they dramatize the rise and fall of criminal organizations that built fortunes on bootleg liquor, complete with glamorous costumes and jazz. Yet the criticism that they glamorize a real history of violence has been repeated every time a new one comes out.

cards.ja: 長時間働き続けるよりも、こまめに休息を取ったほうが仕事の効率は上がるという。五十分作業したら十分休むといったリズムを守ると、一日を通して集中力を保ちやすくなるとされる。休息中はスマートフォンを眺めるより、窓の外を見たり軽く歩いたりするほうが、頭がすっきりするそうだ。
cards.en: Taking frequent rests is said to raise work efficiency more than working for long stretches without a break. Keeping to a rhythm such as fifty minutes of work followed by ten minutes of rest is thought to make it easier to sustain concentration throughout the day. During a break, looking out the window or taking a short walk apparently clears the head better than staring at a smartphone.

words.defJa: 財産を個人ではなく社会全体のものにしようとする考え方。主に「主義」「党」などと組み合わせて使う。

cards.ja: 20世紀には、共産主義を掲げる国家が世界各地に誕生した。生産手段を社会全体で共有し、貧富の差をなくすという理想は、多くの人々を引きつけた。しかし計画経済の行き詰まりや言論統制への不満が積み重なり、1991年にはソビエト連邦が崩壊した。それでも、共産党が政権を握り続けている国は今も存在する。
cards.en: In the twentieth century, states proclaiming communism sprang up in many parts of the world. The ideal of sharing the means of production across society as a whole and erasing the gap between rich and poor attracted many people. But discontent over the dead end of the planned economy and over censorship built up, and in 1991 the Soviet Union collapsed. Even so, there are still countries today where a communist party continues to hold power.

cards.ja: 正月の商業施設などで流れる琴の音色は、多くの人に日本らしさを感じさせる。十三本の弦を、指にはめた爪ではじいて演奏し、弦の下に立てた小さな支えを動かして音の高さを調節する。かつては良家の娘のたしなみとされたが、近年はポップスを演奏して動画で発信する若い奏者も現れている。
cards.en: The sound of the koto drifting through shopping centers and the like at New Year gives many people a feeling of something distinctly Japanese. It is played by plucking thirteen strings with picks worn on the fingers, and the pitch is adjusted by moving small bridges set under the strings. It was once considered a proper accomplishment for daughters of good families, but in recent years young players have appeared who perform pop songs and share them in videos.

cards.en: With one scorching day following another, there is no end to elderly people suffering heatstroke indoors. This is because quite a few of them get through the day without turning on the air conditioner, worried about the electricity bill or disliking the chill. Experts are urging people to use air conditioning without hesitation once the room temperature passes 28 degrees, and to drink fluids frequently.

cards.ja: 明るい日差しを浴びた瞬間、急にくしゃみが出る人がいる。これは「光くしゃみ反射」と呼ばれる現象で、およそ四人に一人に見られるともいわれる。目に入った光の刺激が、鼻の感覚を伝える神経にも伝わってしまうためだと考えられているが、詳しい仕組みはまだ分かっていない。
cards.en: Some people suddenly sneeze the moment they step into bright sunlight. This is a phenomenon called the photic sneeze reflex, said to occur in roughly one person in four. words.meaning: to wrap up snugly, to envelop
words.defJa: 布などで全体をおおうように包みこむ。

cards.ja: 冬山で道に迷った登山者が見つかったとき、救助隊が真っ先に行うのは体温の低下を防ぐことだ。濡れた服を脱がせ、乾いた毛布や銀色の保温シートで全身をすっぽりとくるむ。熱は頭や首からも逃げやすいため、帽子やタオルで覆うことも欠かせない。急に体を温めすぎると心臓に負担がかかるので、ゆっくりと時間をかけるのが基本である。
cards.en: When a climber lost on a winter mountain is found, the first thing rescuers do is stop their body temperature from falling. They remove the wet clothes and wrap the whole body snugly in dry blankets or a silver thermal sheet. Because heat also escapes easily from the head and neck, covering them with a hat or towel is essential too. Warming the body too quickly strains the heart, so the basic rule is to do it slowly, taking time.

words.defJa: 都道府県の中で、いくつかの町や村をまとめた地域の区分。

cards.ja: 地方の住所には、県名と町村名の間に郡の名前が入っていることが多い。かつて郡には役所が置かれ、行政の単位として機能していたが、大正時代に郡役所が廃止されてからは、ほとんど地理上の区分にすぎなくなった。それでも選挙区の線引きや、郡単位の医師会、農協などに名残がある。市町村合併で町が市に変わると、その地域は郡から外れ、住所から郡名が消えることになる。
cards.en: In rural addresses, the name of a district often appears between the prefecture and the town or village. Districts once had their own government offices and functioned as administrative units, but after those offices were abolished in the Taisho era they became little more than geographic divisions. Even so, traces remain in how electoral districts are drawn and in district-level medical associations and agricultural cooperatives. When a town becomes a city through a municipal merger, the area leaves the district and the district name disappears from its addresses.

cards.ja: 来月の市長選挙は、三期目を目指す現市長と、元県議会議員の新人による一騎打ちとなる見通しだ。現市長は駅前の整備や子育て支援の実績を前面に出し、継続を訴えている。これに対し新人側は、財政赤字が膨らんだと批判し、事業の見直しを公約に掲げる。投票率が低かった前回の選挙を踏まえ、両陣営とも若い世代への働きかけを強めている。
cards.en: Next month's mayoral election looks set to be a two-way race between the incumbent mayor, who is seeking a third term, and a newcomer who is a former prefectural assembly member. The incumbent is putting forward a record of improving the area around the station and supporting families with children, and is appealing for continuity. The newcomer, by contrast, criticizes the growing budget deficit and pledges to review the city's projects. Mindful of the low turnout in the last election, both camps are stepping up their outreach to younger voters.

cards.ja: 碁の世界では、人工知能がトップ棋士を破ってから、打ち方そのものが大きく変わった。昔から悪い手とされてきた打ち方を人工知能が平然と選び、それが実は有効だとわかったからだ。いまでは若手の多くが人工知能を相手に研究を重ね、プロの対局にも新しい手が次々に現れている。一方で、碁の楽しみは勝ち負けだけではないとして、人と向き合って打つ時間を大切にする愛好家も少なくない。
cards.en: In the world of go, the way the game is played has changed dramatically since artificial intelligence defeated top professionals. That is because AI calmly chose moves long regarded as bad, and they turned out to be effective. Now many young players study by playing against AI, and new moves keep appearing even in professional games. On the other hand, quite a few enthusiasts, holding that the pleasure of go is not only about winning or losing, treasure the time spent sitting across from another person and playing.

cards.ja: 日本の電車に初めて乗った外国人旅行者の多くが、車内の静けさに驚くという。通話は控えるよう呼びかけられ、友人同士でも小声で話すのが当たり前になっているからだ。ただ、その静けさを冷たいと感じる人もいて、受け止め方は人によってさまざまである。こうしたマナーの背景には、限られた空間で他人に迷惑をかけないという考え方がある。
cards.en: Many foreign travelers riding a Japanese train for the first time are said to be surprised by how quiet it is inside the car. That is because passengers are asked to refrain from phone calls, and even friends routinely talk in low voices. Some, however, find that quiet cold, and reactions vary from person to person. Behind this etiquette lies the idea of not bothering others in a confined space.

cards.en: This year's city marathon will have a substantially changed course. The organizers have dropped the hilly road along the mountains used until now and switched to an out-and-back route on the flat road beside the river. According to them, the aim is to make it easier not only for runners chasing a record but also for first-timers to finish. They also plan to add more cheering points along the route and to liven up the event together with the local shopping street.

The music teacher who leads them says the goal is not so much singing well as sharing the joy of layering one's own voice over others' while listening to them. At the end of each year, it has become a custom to visit a local hospital and bring songs to the patients there.

words.defJa: 学校で授業などに使う建物。

cards.ja: 少子化で廃校となった小学校の校舎を、地域の拠点として生かす動きが各地で広がっている。ある山あいの町では、教室を改装して宿泊施設とカフェを開き、週末には都市部から多くの家族連れが訪れる。黒板や木の机をそのまま残したことで、懐かしさを味わえる場所として人気を集めた。卒業生にとっても、思い出の詰まった建物が残ることは大きな喜びだという。
cards.en: Across the country, a growing number of communities are putting the buildings of elementary schools closed by the falling birthrate to use as local hubs. In one mountain town, classrooms were renovated into lodgings and a cafe, and on weekends many families come from urban areas. Keeping the blackboards and wooden desks as they were made it popular as a place to enjoy a sense of nostalgia. For graduates, too, having a building full of memories survive is said to be a great joy.

Small and medium-sized merchants selling on the site have repeatedly complained that this makes fair competition impossible. The regulator plans to open an investigation soon and ask for an explanation of how the listings work. In an era when giant companies sway the very rules of the market, the question is how to protect fairness in trade.

words.defJa: 秋に葉が赤く色づくカエデの木。また、秋に木の葉が赤や黄色に変わること。

cards.ja: 秋が深まると、山のもみじが赤や黄色に染まり、各地の名所は大勢の観光客でにぎわう。葉の色が変わるのは、気温が下がって緑の色素が分解され、もともと含まれていた黄色の色素や、新しく作られた赤い色素が目立ってくるためだ。昼と夜の寒暖の差が大きく、空気が澄んだ年ほど、色づきは鮮やかになるといわれる。今年は夏の猛暑の影響で、見頃が例年より一週間ほど遅れる見込みである。
cards.en: As autumn deepens, the maples in the mountains turn red and yellow, and famous viewing spots across the country bustle with crowds of tourists. The leaves change color because, as temperatures drop, the green pigment breaks down and the yellow pigment that was there all along, along with newly produced red pigment, becomes prominent. The colors are said to be more vivid in years when the gap between day and night temperatures is large and the air is clear. This year, because of the intense summer heat, the best viewing period is expected to come about a week later than usual.

words.defJa: その人がどの国の国民であるかという身分。

cards.ja: 日本の法律では、成人した人が二つの国籍を持ち続けることは原則として認められていない。生まれながらに二つの国籍を持つ子どもは、一定の年齢までにどちらか一方を選ぶよう求められる。ただ、選ばなかった場合の扱いはあいまいで、実際には両方を持ち続けている人も少なくない。国際結婚が増えるなか、制度の見直しを求める声も上がっている。
cards.en: Under Japanese law, adults are in principle not allowed to keep holding two nationalities. Children who hold two nationalities from birth are required to choose one or the other by a certain age. However, what happens to those who do not choose is unclear, and in practice quite a few people go on holding both. As international marriages increase, calls for a review of the system are also growing.

words.meaning: to make, to prepare (often by hand)
words.defJa: 手間をかけて作り上げる。また、口実や話などを都合よく作る。

cards.ja: 祖母は、孫たちが泊まりに来る日になると、朝早くから台所に立って料理を何品もこしらえた。煮物も酢の物も、畑で採れた野菜を使った手作りで、市販の調味料にはほとんど頼らなかった。手順を書き残すことはなく、分量はいつも目分量だった。今になって同じ味を再現しようとしても、どうしてもあの味にはならない。
cards.en: Whenever her grandchildren were coming to stay, my grandmother would stand in the kitchen from early morning and make dish after dish. The simmered dishes and vinegared salads alike were homemade from vegetables grown in her field, and she hardly relied on store-bought seasonings. She never wrote down her methods, and she always measured by eye. Even when I try to recreate those dishes now, they never quite taste the same.

words.meaning: thank you for the meal (said after eating)
words.defJa: 食事を終えたときに、作ってくれた人や食べ物に感謝して言うあいさつ。

cards.ja: 食事を終えると、日本では手を合わせて「ごちそうさま」と言うのが一般的だ。漢字では「御馳走様」と書き、「馳走」はもともと客をもてなすために走り回ることを意味していた。つまり、食事を用意してくれた人の手間に対して感謝を表す言葉なのである。最近では、飲食店で会計を済ませて店を出る際に、店員にこの一言をかける客も多い。
cards.en: In Japan, it is customary to put your hands together and say "gochisosama" when you finish a meal. Written in kanji, the phrase contains the word "chiso," which originally meant running around to entertain a guest. In other words, it expresses gratitude for the trouble taken by the person who prepared the meal. These days, many customers also say it to the staff as they pay and leave a restaurant.

words.meaning: likewise; it is I who should say so (in reply to thanks or an apology)
words.defJa: 相手のお礼やおわびに対して、自分のほうも同じ気持ちだと返すことば。

cards.ja: 取引先との打ち合わせが終わり、相手が「本日はお時間をいただき、ありがとうございました」と頭を下げた。私もすぐに「こちらこそ、ありがとうございました」と返した。日本のビジネスの場では、礼を言われたときに、自分の側も同じ気持ちだと伝えるこの表現が欠かせない。相手を立てつつ対等な関係を示す、便利な言葉だといえる。
cards.en: When the meeting with the client ended, the other person bowed and said, "Thank you for your time today." I immediately replied, "Likewise, thank you very much." In Japanese business settings, this expression, which tells someone who has thanked you that you feel the same way, is indispensable. It is a handy phrase that shows respect for the other person while conveying that the relationship is one of equals.

words.meaning: cook, chef (esp. of Western food); tap, stopcock
words.defJa: レストランなどで料理を作ることを仕事にしている人。特に西洋料理の料理人。

cards.ja: 明治時代に西洋料理が日本に広まると、ホテルや客船で働くコックが新しい職業として注目を集めた。多くは外国人の料理人のもとで修業し、ソースの作り方や肉の焼き方を一から学んだ。やがて彼らが独立して町に洋食屋を開き、とんかつやオムライスといった日本独自の料理が生まれていく。いまでは家庭の定番となったこれらの料理も、そうした職人たちの工夫の産物なのである。
cards.en: When Western cuisine spread in Japan in the Meiji era, cooks working in hotels and on passenger ships drew attention as a new profession. Many trained under foreign chefs, learning from scratch how to make sauces and roast meat. Eventually they went independent and opened Western-style restaurants in town, giving rise to distinctly Japanese dishes such as tonkatsu and omurice. These dishes, now staples of home cooking, are the fruit of those craftsmen's ingenuity.

words.defJa: 人に知られないように、静かに何かをするようす。

cards.ja: 父の定年退職の日に合わせて、家族で小さなパーティーを開くことにした。本人に気づかれないよう、母と兄弟でこっそり準備を進め、父の昔の同僚にも声をかけた。当日、何も知らずに帰宅した父は、部屋に集まった懐かしい顔ぶれを見て言葉を失った。照れくさそうに笑いながら目を赤くする姿を、私は初めて見た。

It was the first time I had seen him laugh sheepishly with reddened eyes.

cards.ja: タイヤや手袋に使われるゴムには、木の樹液から作る天然のものと、石油を原料とする合成のものがある。天然ゴムは東南アジアを中心に栽培されるゴムの木の幹に傷をつけ、にじみ出る白い液を集めて作られる。そのままでは暑さで柔らかくなりすぎるが、硫黄を加えて熱すると、伸び縮みする丈夫な素材に変わる。今でも大型の航空機のタイヤには、天然ゴムが欠かせないといわれる。
cards.en: The rubber used in tires and gloves comes in two kinds: natural rubber made from tree sap and synthetic rubber made from petroleum. Natural rubber is made by cutting into the trunks of rubber trees, grown mainly in Southeast Asia, and collecting the white liquid that oozes out. On its own it gets too soft in the heat, but when sulfur is added and it is heated, it turns into a tough material that stretches and springs back. Even today, natural rubber is said to be indispensable for the tires of large aircraft.

words.meaning: excuse me, is anyone home? (called out when visiting)

cards.ja: 昔の日本の家では、玄関の戸を開けて「ごめんください」と声をかけるのが訪問の作法だった。呼び鈴のない家が多く、家の人が奥から出てくるまで、客は玄関先で待つのが普通だったからだ。インターホンが普及した今では、この言葉を耳にする機会はめっきり減った。それでも地方の商店などでは、店に入るときのあいさつとして、まだ使われている。
cards.en: In old Japanese homes, the proper way to visit was to open the front door and call out "Gomen kudasai." Many houses had no doorbell, and visitors usually waited at the entrance until someone came out from the back of the house. Now that intercoms are widespread, the chances of hearing this phrase have dropped sharply. Even so, at shops in the countryside it is still used as a greeting on entering.

words.defJa: 音楽や絵画などの作品や演技の出来を競い合う会。

cards.ja: 若手音楽家の登竜門とされる国際ピアノコンクールで、日本の二十代のピアニストが二位に入賞した。審査は数週間にわたって行われ、予選の段階を重ねるごとに出場者が絞り込まれていく。本人は幼いころから地元のピアノ教室に通い、高校を卒業してからは海外の音楽院で学んできたという。入賞をきっかけに各地の楽団から共演の依頼が相次いでおり、本格的な演奏活動が始まろうとしている。
cards.en: At an international piano competition regarded as a gateway to success for young musicians, a Japanese pianist in their twenties won second prize. The judging runs over several weeks, and the field is narrowed down with each successive round. The pianist reportedly attended a local piano school from early childhood and, after finishing high school, has been studying at a conservatory abroad. Since the prize, invitations to perform with orchestras in many places have been pouring in, and a full-fledged performing career is about to begin.

words.defJa: セメントに砂や砂利、水を混ぜて固めた建築材料。

cards.ja: 高度経済成長期に一斉に造られた橋やトンネルの多くが、建設から五十年を超えようとしている。コンクリートは丈夫な素材だが、内部の鉄筋がさびると膨張してひびが入り、強度が落ちてしまう。こうした劣化を早く見つけるため、最近ではドローンで撮影した画像を人工知能で分析する点検方法も導入されている。限られた予算の中で、どの施設から補修するかを決めることが自治体の大きな課題となっている。
cards.en: Many of the bridges and tunnels built all at once during the era of rapid economic growth are nearing fifty years since construction. Concrete is a durable material, but when the steel reinforcing bars inside rust, they expand and cause cracks, and the structure loses strength. To catch this kind of deterioration early, inspection methods that use artificial intelligence to analyze images taken by drones have recently been introduced. Deciding which facilities to repair first on a limited budget has become a major challenge for local governments.

cards.en: On shinkansen trains and in airport waiting areas, more and more seats come with a power outlet beside them each year. Now that charging smartphones and computers has become essential, whether a power source is available has become a major factor in where people choose to go. Some cafes deliberately do not install outlets so that customers will not linger. On the other hand, some shops have begun actively courting customers who come to charge their devices.

cards.ja: 夜のニュース番組は、アナウンサーの「こんばんは」という一言で始まることが多い。何気ないあいさつだが、視聴者にとっては一日の終わりに社会の出来事を振り返る合図にもなっている。最近はインターネットの動画配信でも、配信者が同じ言葉で番組を始める姿がよく見られる。画面越しでも、あいさつが人と人との距離を縮める役割を果たしているのだろう。
cards.en: Evening news programs often open with the announcer saying "Good evening." It is an ordinary greeting, but for viewers it also serves as a cue to look back on the day's events at the end of the day. Lately, streamers on online video platforms can often be seen opening their shows with the same words. Even through a screen, it seems, a greeting helps close the distance between people.

words.meaning: club, circle (esp. an informal student club)
words.defJa: 同じ趣味や関心を持つ人たちが集まって活動する仲間の集まり。

cards.ja: 大学に入学すると、多くの学生がまず悩むのがどのサークルに入るかだ。運動系から音楽、ボランティアまで種類は数百に及び、春のキャンパスは勧誘の声であふれる。体育会の部活動ほど練習は厳しくなく、学部や学年を超えた友人ができるのが魅力だという。一方で、新入生を狙った悪質な勧誘もあり、大学側は注意を呼びかけている。
cards.en: When students start university, one of the first things many agonize over is which club to join. There are hundreds to choose from, from sports to music to volunteering, and in spring the campus is full of recruiting calls. Practice is not as tough as in the official athletic clubs, and the appeal is said to be making friends across faculties and years. On the other hand, there is also malicious recruiting aimed at new students, and universities are urging caution.

cards.en: Talks between the city and the local shopping street over redevelopment of the area in front of the station are still going on. The city has presented a plan to tear down aging buildings and put up high-rise condominiums and commercial facilities. In response, many independent shops that have been in business for years are pushing back, saying rising rents would force them to close. The debate centers on how to balance the town's convenience with its traditional streetscape.

cards.en: As competition to develop generative AI intensifies, securing the computing resources to run cutting-edge models has become a challenge for every company. Data centers packed with huge numbers of semiconductors consume enormous amounts of electricity and also need a great deal of water for cooling. As a result, more and more facilities are being built near power plants or in cold regions. How to weigh technological progress against the burden on the environment is once again being called into question.

cards.en: At two in the morning, an ambulance siren rang out through the residential neighborhood. When I opened the window, red lights were flashing in front of the apartment building across the street. Neighbors, too, leaned out of their windows, watching anxiously until the ambulance drove away. In this area, where many elderly people live alone, nighttime ambulance calls are reportedly rising year by year.

cards.ja: 魚の小骨がのどに刺さったとき、ご飯を丸のみして押し流そうとする人は多い。しかし耳鼻科の医師によると、この方法はかえって骨を奥へ押し込んでしまうおそれがあるという。軽いせきで取れない場合は、無理をせずに早めに受診したほうがよい。小さな骨でも、放っておくと炎症を起こすことがあるからだ。
cards.en: When a small fish bone gets stuck in their throat, many people try to wash it down by swallowing a mouthful of rice whole. According to ear, nose and throat doctors, however, this can actually push the bone in deeper. If a light cough does not dislodge it, it is better not to force things and to see a doctor early. Even a small bone can cause inflammation if left alone.

cards.en: More young employees now start packing up briskly the moment the end-of-day chime sounds. There used to be an atmosphere in which leaving before your boss felt awkward, but now going home once your work is done is becoming the norm. One section chief says it is far healthier to focus and finish quickly than to linger aimlessly.

words.defJa: 人と別れるときに言うあいさつの言葉。

cards.ja: 日本語の教科書では別れのあいさつとして必ず登場するが、大人が日常でさようならと口にする場面は意外に少ない。職場では「お疲れさまでした」、友人同士なら「じゃあね」や「またね」で済ませるのが普通だ。この言葉には、もう会えないかもしれないという響きがあるため、避けられがちだという指摘もある。一方、小学校では今も、帰りの会でみんなでさようならを言う光景が見られる。
cards.en: It always appears as the farewell greeting in Japanese textbooks, but adults actually say sayonara in daily life surprisingly rarely. At work people usually make do with "otsukaresama deshita," and among friends with "jaa ne" or "mata ne." Some point out that the word tends to be avoided because it carries a sense that you may never meet again. In elementary schools, on the other hand, you can still see children saying sayonara together at the end-of-day class meeting.

words.defJa: すがすがしくて、気持ちがよいようす。

cards.en: Mornings in the highlands are so refreshing that the muggy heat of the city seems unreal. Above 1,000 meters, morning temperatures stay around 20 degrees even in midsummer, and the air is crisp and dry. Walking in the breeze that slips through the trees clears even a sleep-deprived head. It is easy to see why the area has long been popular as a summer retreat.

cards.ja: 大気中の二酸化炭素が海に溶け込むと、海水は少しずつ酸性に近づいていく。この現象は海洋酸性化と呼ばれ、貝やサンゴが殻や骨格をつくりにくくなることが知られている。これまでの観測によると、産業革命以降、海の表面のpHはすでに約0.1下がった。数字は小さく見えるが、水素イオンの濃度に直すと三割ほど増えた計算になる。
cards.en: When carbon dioxide in the atmosphere dissolves into the sea, seawater gradually shifts toward acidity. This phenomenon is called ocean acidification, and it is known to make it harder for shellfish and corals to build their shells and skeletons. Observations so far show that the pH of the ocean surface has already fallen by about 0.1 since the Industrial Revolution. The number looks small, but converted into hydrogen ion concentration it amounts to an increase of roughly 30 percent.

cards.ja: シーツは週に一度は洗ったほうがいいと分かっていても、つい後回しにしてしまう人は多い。人は寝ている間にコップ一杯分ほどの汗をかくとされ、寝具の表面には皮脂やほこりがたまりやすい。それがダニのえさにもなるため、アレルギーのある人には特にこまめな洗濯が勧められている。天気のよい日に干したシーツの肌ざわりは、それだけで眠りを心地よくしてくれる。
cards.en: Many people know they ought to wash their sheets at least once a week but keep putting it off. People are said to sweat about a glassful during sleep, and sebum and dust easily build up on the surface of the bedding. Because this also feeds dust mites, people with allergies in particular are advised to wash their sheets often. The feel of sheets dried in the sun on a fine day is enough on its own to make sleep more pleasant.

words.meaning: square, four-cornered (as a noun: a square)
words.defJa: 四つの角があり、正方形や長方形のような形をしているようす。

cards.ja: 四角いスイカは、もともと冷蔵庫に収まりやすいようにと考え出されたものだという。実がまだ小さいうちに透明な箱に入れて育てると、成長するにつれて箱の形に合わせて膨らんでいく。ただ、食べ頃になる前に収穫するため、味よりも見た目を楽しむ観賞用として売られることが多い。一個一万円以上の値がつくこともあり、海外からの観光客にも人気がある。
cards.en: Square watermelons were reportedly first devised so that they would fit more easily in refrigerators. If the fruit is placed in a transparent box while still small, it swells to match the shape of the box as it grows. Because they are harvested before they are ripe, however, they are mostly sold as ornaments to be enjoyed for their looks rather than their taste. They can fetch more than ten thousand yen apiece and are popular with visitors from overseas too.

words.defJa: 春・夏・秋・冬の四つの季節。

cards.ja: 日本には四季があると誇らしげに語られることは多いが、季節の移り変わり自体は世界の多くの地域に見られる。それでも、日本の暮らしや文化が季節と深く結びついてきたのは確かだ。俳句で季語が重んじられることや、和菓子が季節ごとに姿を変えることは、その表れだろう。近年は温暖化で春と秋が短くなり、四季が二季になりつつあると嘆く声も聞かれる。
cards.en: People often say with pride that Japan has four seasons, but the changing of the seasons itself is found in many regions of the world. Even so, it is certainly true that Japanese life and culture have long been closely tied to the seasons. That seasonal words are valued in haiku, and that wagashi sweets change their appearance with each season, are signs of this. In recent years, as warming shortens spring and autumn, some lament that the four seasons are turning into two.

words.defJa: 空気や物の中に含まれている水分。しめりけ。

cards.ja: 梅雨に入ると、押し入れやクローゼットの湿気対策が欠かせなくなる。空気がこもりやすい場所では、衣類や布団にいつの間にかカビが生えていることも珍しくない。晴れた日には扉を開けて風を通し、除湿剤をこまめに取り替えるのが基本だ。布団や収納ケースを床にじかに置かず、下にすき間をつくるだけでも、効果はかなり違ってくる。
cards.en: Once the rainy season begins, guarding against dampness in closets and storage spaces becomes essential. In places where air tends to stagnate, it is not unusual to find that mold has quietly grown on clothes and bedding. The basics are to open the doors to let air through on sunny days and to replace moisture absorbers regularly. Even just keeping futons and storage cases off the bare floor, with a gap underneath, makes a big difference.

cards.ja: 冬場は室内の湿度が三十パーセントを下回ることも珍しくない。空気が乾燥すると、のどや鼻の粘膜の働きが弱まり、ウイルスに感染しやすくなるとされる。専門家は、加湿器などを使って湿度を四十から六十パーセントに保つよう勧めている。ただし、上げすぎると今度は窓の結露やカビの原因になるので注意が必要だ。
cards.en: In winter, it is not unusual for indoor humidity to fall below 30 percent. When the air is dry, the mucous membranes of the throat and nose are said to work less well, making people more susceptible to viral infections. Experts recommend using humidifiers and the like to keep humidity between 40 and 60 percent. Raising it too much, however, can in turn cause condensation on windows and mold, so care is needed.

words.defJa: 動物の体の後ろの端から細長く伸びている部分。

cards.ja: 犬がしっぽを振るのは、うれしいときだけとは限らない。動物行動学の研究によると、緊張や警戒を感じているときにも、しっぽを小刻みに振ることがあるという。大切なのは、耳の向きや体の構え、表情など全体の様子をあわせて見ることだ。しっぽの動きだけで気持ちを判断すると、思わぬかみつき事故につながりかねない。
cards.en: A dog wagging its tail is not always happy. According to research in animal behavior, dogs may also wag their tails in small, quick movements when they feel tense or wary. What matters is to look at the whole picture, including the direction of the ears, body posture and facial expression. Judging a dog's feelings by the movement of its tail alone could lead to an unexpected bite.

words.defJa: その人が実際に持っている能力や力。

cards.ja: 年功序列を見直し、実力に応じて給与を決める企業が増えている。若手でも成果を上げれば管理職に就ける一方、評価の基準があいまいだと不満も生まれやすい。ある人事担当者は、数字に表れにくい後輩の育成やチームへの貢献をどう評価するかが、今後の大きな課題だと話す。
cards.en: More companies are reviewing seniority-based systems and setting pay according to ability. While young employees can now become managers if they deliver results, vague evaluation criteria easily breed dissatisfaction. One HR officer says that a major challenge ahead is how to evaluate things that are hard to show in numbers, such as mentoring junior staff and contributing to the team.

words.meaning: Excuse me (said on leaving); I'm sorry (for my rudeness)
words.defJa: 目上の人の部屋を出るときや、相手に迷惑をかけたことをわびるときに言う言葉。

cards.ja: 中学校や高校では、職員室に入るときは「失礼します」、用事を済ませて出るときは「失礼しました」と言うよう指導されることが多い。ドアの前で軽く一礼してから出るのも、よく見られる作法だ。この言葉は、ちょっとした失敗をわびるときにも使われる。電話をかけ間違えたと気づいたら、「失礼しました」と一言添えてから切るのが礼儀である。
cards.en: In junior and senior high schools, students are often taught to say "shitsurei shimasu" when entering the staff room and "shitsurei shimashita" when leaving after finishing their business. Bowing lightly at the door before going out is also a common custom. The phrase is used to apologize for small slips as well. If you realize you have dialed the wrong number, it is polite to add a quick "shitsurei shimashita" before hanging up.

words.meaning: to go numb, to fall asleep (of a limb); to be thrilled
words.defJa: 体の一部の感覚がなくなり、じんじんして思うように動かなくなる。

cards.ja: 法事などで長い時間正座をしていると、足がしびれて立てなくなることがある。これは体重で足の血管や神経が圧迫され、血流が一時的に悪くなるために起こる。ときどき重心を左右に移したり、足の親指を重ねる向きを変えたりするだけでも、だいぶ楽になるという。立ち上がる前には、つま先を立ててしばらく待つと転びにくい。
cards.en: When you sit in seiza for a long time at a memorial service or similar occasion, your legs may go numb and you may be unable to stand. This happens because your body weight presses on the blood vessels and nerves of the legs, temporarily reducing blood flow. Reportedly, just shifting your weight from side to side now and then, or switching which big toe rests on top, makes it much easier. Before standing up, you are less likely to fall if you tuck your toes under and wait a moment.

words.meaning: to wither, to wilt; to deflate
words.defJa: ふくらんでいたものや開いていた花が、小さく縮んで元気がなくなる。

cards.ja: 朝顔の花は、夜明け前に開き、昼ごろにはしぼんでしまう。わずか半日の命だが、つぼみが次々と育つため、夏の間は毎朝新しい花を楽しむことができる。小学校で観察日記をつけた人なら、青い花がしぼむころには赤紫っぽく変わっているのに気づいたかもしれない。花びらの細胞の中の液が、アルカリ性から酸性寄りに変わるためだという。
cards.en: Morning glory flowers open before dawn and wither by around noon. Each bloom lives only half a day, but because buds keep developing one after another, you can enjoy new flowers every morning all summer. If you kept an observation diary of them in elementary school, you may have noticed that blue flowers turn a reddish purple by the time they wither. This is said to be because the fluid inside the petal cells shifts from alkaline toward acidic.

words.defJa: 水分を含んで、少しぬれた状態になる。

cards.ja: 気象台によると、あすは南から暖かく湿った空気が流れ込み、大気の状態が非常に不安定になる見込みだ。昼過ぎからは局地的に雷を伴った激しい雨が降るおそれがある。急に空が暗くなったり、冷たい風が吹いてきたりしたら、すぐに頑丈な建物の中に移動してほしい。
cards.en: According to the meteorological observatory, warm, moist air will flow in from the south tomorrow, making atmospheric conditions very unstable. From early afternoon, there is a risk of intense localized rain accompanied by thunder. If the sky suddenly darkens or a cold wind starts to blow, people should immediately move inside a sturdy building.

cards.ja: 紛争地で取材を続けるジャーナリストの多くは、大手メディアに属さないフリーランスだ。現地の声を伝えたいという思いから危険な地域に入るが、安全対策や保険の費用は自分で負担しなければならないことが多い。近年は、記者が拘束されたり命を落としたりする事件も後を絶たない。それでも彼らが伝える映像や記事がなければ、私たちは戦争の実態を知ることができない。
cards.en: Many of the journalists who keep reporting from conflict zones are freelancers who do not belong to major media outlets. They enter dangerous areas out of a desire to convey local voices, but they often have to pay for safety measures and insurance themselves. In recent years, incidents in which reporters are detained or killed have kept occurring. Even so, without the footage and articles they deliver, we would have no way of knowing the reality of war.

words.defJa: ひざを深く曲げて腰を落とし、低い姿勢になる。

cards.ja: 和式トイレを使えない子どもが増えていると話題になって久しい。家庭や学校でトイレの洋式化が進み、かかとを床につけたまましゃがむ姿勢に慣れていないためだという。足首が硬くてうまく腰を落とせず、後ろに転びそうになる子もいる。災害時の避難所では和式しか使えない場合もあり、普段から練習しておくよう呼びかける自治体もある。
cards.en: It has long been reported that more and more children cannot use Japanese-style squat toilets. This is said to be because, with toilets at home and at school switching to Western style, they are not used to squatting with their heels on the floor. Some children have such stiff ankles that they cannot get low enough and nearly fall backward. Since evacuation shelters may have only Japanese-style toilets in a disaster, some local governments urge people to practice in ordinary times.

cards.ja: しゃっくりは、横隔膜がけいれんを起こし、それと同時に声帯が急に閉じることで起こる。息を止める、冷たい水を飲むなど、昔からさまざまな止め方が伝えられてきたが、確かな効果が証明されたものは少ない。たいていは数分で自然に治まるので、あまり心配はいらない。ただ、二日以上続くような場合は、ほかの病気が関係していることもあるという。
cards.en: Hiccups occur when the diaphragm spasms and the vocal cords suddenly close at the same moment. Various ways of stopping them, such as holding your breath or drinking cold water, have long been handed down, but few have been proven to work. They usually settle down on their own within a few minutes, so there is little need to worry. However, if they last two days or more, another illness may be involved.

words.meaning: to suck on (a finger, candy, etc.)
words.defJa: 口の中に入れて、なめたり吸ったりする。

cards.ja: 赤ちゃんが指をしゃぶるのは、ごく自然な行動である。おなかの中にいるときからすでに見られ、気持ちを落ち着かせる役割があると考えられている。小児科医の多くは、三歳ごろまでは無理にやめさせる必要はないとしている。ただし、四歳を過ぎても続く場合は、歯並びへの影響を考えて、少しずつ減らしていくとよい。
cards.en: It is entirely natural for babies to suck their fingers. The behavior can already be seen while they are in the womb and is thought to help them calm down. Many pediatricians say there is no need to force children to stop before about age three. If it continues past age four, however, it is a good idea to wean them off it gradually, given the effect on how the teeth line up.

words.defJa: グー・チョキ・パーの三つの手の形を同時に出して、勝ち負けを決める遊び。

cards.ja: じゃんけんは、日本では子どもの遊びにとどまらず、物事を公平に決める手段として広く使われている。給食の余ったデザートを誰がもらうかから、テレビ番組の出演順まで、じゃんけん一つで決まることも珍しくない。似た遊びは世界各地にあるが、手の形や掛け声は国によって少しずつ異なる。近年は、勝率を上げる心理的な戦略を研究した論文まで発表されている。
cards.en: In Japan, rock-paper-scissors is not just a children's game but is widely used as a way to decide things fairly. From who gets the leftover dessert at school lunch to the order of appearance on a TV show, it is not unusual for things to be settled by a single round. Similar games exist around the world, but the hand shapes and chants differ slightly from country to country. In recent years, papers have even been published on psychological strategies for raising one's winning rate.

words.meaning: heavy-, serious- (as in heavy industry, heavy labor)
words.defJa: ほかの語の前について、おもい、または程度がはなはだしいという意味を表す。

cards.ja: 高度経済成長期の日本では、鉄鋼や造船、化学といった重化学工業が経済をけん引した。太平洋沿岸には大規模な工業地帯がつくられ、多くの若者が地方から働き口を求めて移り住んだ。一方で、工場から出る煙や排水は深刻な公害を引き起こし、各地で住民の健康が損なわれた。豊かさの裏で払われた代償は、今も環境政策の教訓として語り継がれている。
cards.en: In Japan's period of rapid economic growth, heavy and chemical industries such as steel, shipbuilding and chemicals drove the economy. Large industrial zones were built along the Pacific coast, and many young people moved from rural areas in search of work. At the same time, smoke and wastewater from factories caused serious pollution, damaging residents' health in many places. The price paid behind that prosperity is still handed down today as a lesson for environmental policy.

The man in his twenties riding the motorcycle was taken to hospital, but he struck his head hard and is reported to be unconscious and in critical condition. Police are questioning the car's driver in detail about what happened. The intersection has good visibility, and locals had long pointed out that accidents were frequent there.

cards.ja: 手織りのじゅうたんは、一枚を仕上げるのに数か月、大きなものでは数年かかることもある。職人は縦糸に色とりどりの毛糸を一つずつ結びつけ、少しずつ模様を織り上げていく。結び目の数が多いほど柄は細かくなり、価値も高くなる。親から子へと受け継がれ、何十年も使い続けられるのは、こうした手間の結晶だからだろう。
cards.en: A hand-woven carpet can take several months to finish, and a large one sometimes takes years. Artisans tie colorful strands of wool to the warp threads one by one, gradually weaving the pattern. The more knots there are, the finer the design and the higher the value. That such carpets are handed down from parent to child and used for decades is probably because they are the fruit of all this painstaking work.

cards.en: Many people are unsure what to talk about when they meet someone for the first time. Psychological research has found that asking slightly deeper questions, rather than sticking to safe topics like the weather, makes it easier for people to like each other. Simply asking what has made the other person happy recently, for example, can make a conversation flow much more easily.

words.defJa: ほかの語の前について、いろいろな、多くのという意味を表す。

cards.ja: 日本の食料自給率は、カロリーベースで四割にも満たず、諸外国と比べても低い水準にある。小麦や大豆、飼料用のトウモロコシなどの多くを輸入に頼っているためだ。国際情勢が不安定になれば、価格の高騰や輸入の停滞が一気に家計を直撃しかねない。政府は国内生産の拡大を掲げるが、農業の担い手不足という課題が重くのしかかっている。
cards.en: Japan's food self-sufficiency rate is below 40 percent on a calorie basis, a low level even compared with other countries. This is because it relies on imports for much of its wheat, soybeans and feed corn. If the international situation becomes unstable, soaring prices or stalled imports could hit household budgets all at once. The government has pledged to expand domestic production, but a shortage of people to carry on farming weighs heavily on that goal.

cards.en: The exam results are already out, so there is no point agonizing over them now. Even when I tell myself that, at night I end up thinking about nothing but my answer sheet. In psychology, going over an unchangeable past again and again is considered closely linked to low mood. At such times, turning one's attention to physical tasks such as walking or housework is said to help.

Small daily habits are said to determine what your skin will look like ten years from now.

Vinegar also helps keep food from spoiling, and it has long been used as an essential seasoning for sushi and vinegared side dishes. Recently, more people are also drinking it diluted with water or sparkling water, not just using it in cooking.

cards.en: My grandmother has run a small diner in front of the station single-handedly for nearly sixty years. "I've kept this same flavor all along, ever since the day I opened," she says with a laugh, stirring the pot of curry. The regulars have changed with the generations, and now the children and grandchildren of former regulars come in. For her, staying the same is probably her greatest source of pride.

words.defJa: 習い事や技術を教える民間の教室。

cards.ja: 定年を迎えた男性たちの間で、料理スクールに通う人が増えている。妻に任せきりだった台所仕事を、包丁の使い方から一つずつ学ぶのだという。講師によれば、受講生の多くは最初こそぎこちないが、三か月もすると手際よく一品を仕上げられるようになる。教室は、退職後の新しい仲間づくりの場にもなっている。
cards.en: More and more men who have reached retirement age are attending cooking schools. They learn the kitchen work they had left entirely to their wives step by step, starting with how to use a knife. According to the instructors, most students are clumsy at first, but within about three months they can deftly finish a dish. The classes have also become a place to make new friends after retirement.

cards.en: Women who looked after passengers on airplanes were once called stewardesses, and it was a job many young women dreamed of. From the 1990s on, however, the gender-neutral term "cabin crew" spread. Today the old name is hardly ever used, even in airlines' job ads. The shift in words reflects changing social attitudes toward work.

cards.en: Taking the move as an opportunity, I boldly got rid of clothes I no longer wore and books I wasn't going to read. With fewer things, the room became neat and uncluttered, and cleaning it now takes about half the time. Strangely, once my surroundings were in order, even my mood felt lighter. The benefits of tidying up may go beyond appearances.

The singer began with no accompaniment, and that voice reached every corner of the three thousand seats. Even after the last note faded, it is said, no one could bring themselves to applaud for a while. Those few minutes left a deep mark on many people's memories.

cards.en: As summers grow harsher, more companies are reviewing their workplace dress codes. One bank abolished its rule requiring female employees to wear stockings. The areas in front of station ticket gates overflowed with people waiting for service to resume, and people could be seen everywhere phoning their offices to say they would be late. The Meteorological Agency is urging caution, warning that more snow may accumulate through tomorrow. It seems best to avoid going out unless necessary.

cards.ja: 駅のホームでは、天井のスピーカーから発車の案内が絶えず流れている。ところが、音が反響しやすい構内では声がこもり、内容を聞き取れないという利用者の不満が多かった。そこである鉄道会社は、音が特定の方向にだけ届く新型の機器を導入した。試験的に設置した駅では、案内が聞きやすくなったと好評だという。
cards.en: On station platforms, departure announcements stream constantly from ceiling speakers. In echo-prone station buildings, however, the voice sounds muffled, and many passengers complained they couldn't make out what was said. So one railway company introduced a new type of device that sends sound in one specific direction only. At stations where it was installed on a trial basis, it has reportedly been well received for making announcements easier to hear.

cards.en: Even with the same clothes, the impression they make changes a lot depending on how you choose the size. A stylist says that if you pick a jacket that fits your shoulder width, you will look slim and smart regardless of your build. Conversely, clothes that are too big often end up making the body look heavier. Rather than buying expensive clothes, the shortcut to dressing well is apparently to first know your own measurements.

words.meaning: sorry; I apologize (plain, mostly male speech)
words.defJa: 相手に悪いことをしたと感じて、申し訳なく思う気持ちを表す言葉。

cards.ja: 定年退職の日、父は家族を前に、長いあいだ仕事ばかりで本当にすまないと思っていた、と静かに語った。単身赴任が続き、運動会にも卒業式にもほとんど顔を出せなかったからだ。母は笑って首を振ったが、その目は少し潤んでいた。不器用な父がそんな思いを言葉にしたのは、それが初めてだった。
cards.en: On the day he retired, my father quietly told the family that for a long time he had felt truly sorry for doing nothing but work. He had spent years posted away from home and had hardly ever made it to sports days or graduations. My mother laughed and shook her head, but her eyes were a little moist. It was the first time my awkward father had ever put such feelings into words.

cards.en: When presenting at a meeting, it is important not to cram too much text onto your slides. Listeners get caught up reading the screen and stop hearing what the speaker is saying. cards.en: To avoid the morning rush hour, ways of working that shift commuting times are spreading. One company introduced a system that lets employees choose a starting time between 7 and 10 a.m. Employees speak highly of it, saying the stress of packed trains has eased and they can spend mornings with their families. Railway companies are also asking for cooperation, since it helps relieve congestion.

cards.en: At the year-end market, stalls selling fish and vegetables for New Year dishes stand in long rows, bustling with crowds of shoppers from early morning. words.defJa: 家の中で履く、かかとの部分がない簡単な履き物。

cards.ja: 日本の家庭を訪れた外国人が戸惑うことの一つに、スリッパの使い分けがある。玄関で靴を脱いだ後は廊下でスリッパを履き、畳の部屋に入るときにはそれも脱ぐ。さらにトイレには専用のものが置かれていることが多く、うっかり履いたまま戻ってきて笑われることもある。清潔さを重んじる習慣が、こうした細かな決まりを生んだのだろう。
cards.en: One thing that puzzles foreigners visiting Japanese homes is the rules about slippers. After taking off your shoes at the entrance, you wear slippers in the hallway, and you take those off too when entering a tatami room. On top of that, there are often special ones for the toilet, and people sometimes get laughed at for absentmindedly walking back out still wearing them. A custom that values cleanliness probably gave rise to these detailed rules.

cards.en: At one time, families printing their own New Year's cards at the end of the year was a common sight. Making a plate on a small home printing device, applying the ink color by color and pressing out the cards one at a time was laborious work. Now cards can be made easily with a computer and printer, and fewer people send New Year's cards at all. The smell of ink that hung in the living room at year's end is becoming a fond memory.

words.defJa: その家族に共通する名前。名字。

cards.ja: 日本では、日本人同士が結婚すると夫婦が同じ姓を名乗ることが法律で定められている。実際には、九割以上の夫婦が夫の姓を選んでいるのが現状だ。仕事上の不便などを理由に、夫婦が別々の姓を名乗れる制度を求める声も根強い。国会でもたびたび議論されてきたテーマである。
cards.en: In Japan, the law requires that when two Japanese nationals marry, they use the same surname. In practice, more than 90 percent of couples choose the husband's surname. There are also persistent calls, citing inconveniences at work and other reasons, for a system that would let married couples use separate surnames. It is a topic that has been debated in the Diet time and again.

words.defJa: そのものがもともと持っている特徴や性格。

cards.ja: 水には、ほかの多くの物質とは異なる変わった性質がある。ふつう液体は冷えるほど縮んで密度が高くなるが、水は四度付近で最も密度が高くなり、それより冷えるとかえって膨らむのだ。そのため、冬に湖の表面が凍っても、底のほうには四度前後の水が残る。魚たちが厳しい寒さを生き延びられるのは、この性質のおかげである。
cards.en: Water has an unusual property that sets it apart from most other substances. Liquids normally shrink and become denser as they cool, but water is densest at around 4 degrees Celsius and actually expands when it cools further. That is why, even when the surface of a lake freezes in winter, water of around 4 degrees remains near the bottom. It is thanks to this property that fish can survive the harsh cold.

words.defJa: 草や木が育って大きくなること。

cards.en: Besides light and water, temperature has a major effect on plant growth. Rice, for example, does not fill out properly if temperatures are too high while the grains are ripening, and the grains turn chalky white. In response to recent extreme heat, research institutes around the country are developing heat-tolerant varieties. An era has come in which the crops themselves must change to keep pace with the changing climate.

Experts urge people to use long passwords made of meaningless combinations of characters, and a different one for each service.

words.defJa: どんなことがあっても。強く願ったり頼んだりするときに使う。

cards.en: The local chamber of commerce has launched a signature campaign to bring an international conference, to be held the year after next, to the area. At a press conference, its president said emphatically that they want to win the bid at all costs, as an opportunity to revive the local economy. If the conference is held there, thousands of participants will come from around the world, and a big economic boost is expected for hotels and restaurants as well.

cards.ja: 大学三年生になると、多くの学生が専門のゼミに所属する。少人数で文献を読み、毎週交代で発表を行い、教授や仲間から厳しい質問を受けるのだ。講義を聞くだけの授業とは違い、自分の頭で考えて意見を述べる力が鍛えられる。卒業後も、ゼミの仲間とのつながりが続くという人は多い。
cards.en: In their third year, many university students join a specialized seminar. In small groups they read the literature, take turns giving presentations every week, and face tough questions from the professor and their peers. Unlike classes where you just listen to lectures, this builds the ability to think for yourself and express your opinions. Many people say their ties with seminar mates continue even after graduation.

cards.ja: 後半に入ると、地元チームは前線の人数を増やし、果敢に相手ゴールを攻めた。しかし相手は最後まで守備を崩さず、何度も訪れた好機は得点に結びつかなかった。試合後、監督は、攻める姿勢は見せられたが決定力が足りなかったと悔しさをにじませた。次の試合までに、ゴール前での精度をどう高めるかが課題となる。
cards.en: In the second half, the home team pushed more players forward and boldly attacked the opponent's goal. But the opponents kept their defense intact to the end, and the many chances that came the team's way did not turn into goals. After the match, the coach, visibly frustrated, said they had shown an attacking attitude but lacked the finishing touch. The challenge before the next match will be how to sharpen accuracy in front of goal.

words.defJa: 石灰石などを焼いて粉にしたもので、水と混ぜると固まる建築の材料。

cards.ja: インドは中国に次ぐ世界第二位のセメント生産国である。都市部では高速道路や地下鉄、住宅の建設が相次ぎ、需要は今後も伸び続けると見られている。ただ、セメントの製造には大量の熱が必要で、原料の石灰石そのものからも二酸化炭素が出る。各社は廃棄物を燃料に使うなどして、排出を減らす工夫を急いでいる。
cards.en: India is the world's second-largest cement producer after China. In its cities, expressways, subways and housing are being built one after another, and demand is expected to keep growing. However, making cement requires a great deal of heat, and the raw material, limestone, itself releases carbon dioxide. Companies are hurrying to find ways to cut emissions, for example by using waste as fuel.

words.defJa: 衣類や食器などの汚れを落とすために使う薬剤。

cards.ja: 洗濯のたびに洗剤を多めに入れている人は少なくない。だが、表示より多く入れても汚れの落ち方はほとんど変わらず、かえってすすぎ残しの原因になるという。最近の製品は濃縮されていて、少量でも十分に汚れが落ちるよう作られている。決められた量を守ればすすぎも短くて済み、水の節約にもなるので、一度キャップの目盛りを確かめてみてはどうだろう。
cards.en: Quite a few people put in extra detergent every time they do the laundry. But using more than the label says hardly changes how well the dirt comes out, and it can actually leave residue after rinsing. Recent products are concentrated and made to get dirt out well even in small amounts. Sticking to the stated amount also keeps rinsing short and saves water, so why not check the markings on the cap once?

cards.ja: 水泳は全身の筋肉をバランスよく使うスポーツだとよく言われる。水の抵抗を受けながら腕で水をかき、脚で蹴るため、多くのエネルギーを消費する。しかも浮力によって膝や腰への負担が小さく、高齢者でも続けやすい。最近は、プールの中を歩くだけの教室も人気を集めている。
cards.en: Swimming is often said to be a sport that works the muscles of the whole body in a balanced way. Because you pull through the water with your arms and kick with your legs against its resistance, it burns a lot of energy. What is more, buoyancy keeps the strain on the knees and lower back small, so even older people find it easy to keep up. Recently, classes where people simply walk in the pool have also become popular.

cards.en: In areas on the Sea of Japan side, snow has been falling continuously since last night under the influence of a strong cold air mass. In some mountain towns, the snow had reached a depth of 80 centimeters by morning. According to the weather office, the snow is expected to continue until early tomorrow afternoon, and another 30 centimeters or so could pile up. People should take great care with icy roads and snow sliding off roofs.

cards.en: In a general election for the House of Representatives, 465 seats are contested across single-member districts and proportional representation combined. Because the result decides the shape of the government, each party throws its full strength behind its candidates at every election. In recent years, however, turnout has stayed low, and how to draw out the interest of younger voters in particular has become a challenge. A growing number of local governments are setting up early-voting stations at universities.

words.defJa: 音を立てないように、静かに気をつけて動くようす。

cards.ja: ようやく眠った赤ちゃんを、母はそうっと布団に下ろした。少しでも揺れると目を覚ましてしまうので、背中を支えていた手を抜くまでに一分近くかかる。息を殺して部屋を出ると、廊下で待っていた兄が小さく親指を立てた。家族にとって、夜のこの数分間がいちばん緊張する時間なのだ。
cards.en: Mother gently lowered the baby, who had finally fallen asleep, onto the futon. Since the slightest jolt would wake the baby, it took her almost a minute to slide out the hand that had been supporting its back. As she left the room holding her breath, the older brother waiting in the hallway gave a small thumbs-up. For the family, these few minutes each night are the tensest of all.

words.defJa: 話の中で述べた、その時期。当時。

cards.ja: 東京で初めてオリンピックが開かれたのは一九六四年のことだ。そのころ、日本は高度経済成長のただ中にあり、新幹線や首都高速道路が次々と開通した。一方で、工場の煙や排水による公害が各地で深刻になりつつあった。豊かさと引き換えに失ったものの大きさに社会が気づくのは、もう少し後のことである。
cards.en: It was in 1964 that the Olympics were first held in Tokyo. In those days Japan was in the midst of its period of rapid economic growth, and the Shinkansen and the Metropolitan Expressway opened one after another. Meanwhile, pollution from factory smoke and wastewater was growing serious in many places. It was only somewhat later that society realized how much it had lost in exchange for prosperity.

cards.ja: 渡り鳥の多くは、夜に長い距離を飛ぶ。昼間に比べて気温が低く、体の熱を逃がしやすいうえ、天敵に襲われる危険も少ないからだ。そのため、都市の明るい照明は鳥にとって大きな脅威になる。光に引き寄せられた鳥が高層ビルの窓にぶつかる事故は、毎年数多く報告されている。
cards.en: Many migratory birds fly long distances at night. Compared with daytime, temperatures are lower, which makes it easier to shed body heat, and there is also less danger of being attacked by predators. For that reason, bright city lights are a major threat to birds. Accidents in which birds drawn to the light crash into the windows of high-rise buildings are reported in large numbers every year.

words.defJa: タデ科の植物の実をひいた粉で作る、細長い麺。日本の伝統的な食べ物の一つ。

cards.ja: 日本には、大みそかに年越しそばを食べる習慣がある。細く長い麺にあやかって長生きを願うためとも、切れやすいことから一年の苦労を断ち切るためとも言われる。駅前のそば店には、毎年この日だけ長い行列ができる。最近は店に並ぶ代わりに、生麺を買って家でゆでる人も増えているそうだ。
cards.en: In Japan there is a custom of eating toshikoshi soba on New Year's Eve. Some say it is to wish for a long life, taking a cue from the thin, long noodles; others say it is to cut off the year's hardships, since the noodles break easily. At the soba shop in front of the station, a long line forms on this one day every year. These days, more people are said to buy fresh noodles and boil them at home instead of lining up at a shop.

cards.ja: 体はくたくたに疲れている。それなのに、布団に入ると頭が妙にさえて眠れない。こうした状態は、仕事の心配ごとや、寝る直前までスマートフォンを見る習慣と関係していることが多いという。専門家は、眠れないときは無理に目を閉じ続けず、いったん寝室を出て心を落ち着かせるよう勧めている。
cards.en: My body is utterly exhausted. And yet, when I get into bed my mind is strangely wide awake and I can't sleep. This kind of state is said to be often linked to worries about work or the habit of looking at a smartphone right up until bedtime. Experts advise that when you can't sleep, rather than forcing your eyes to stay shut, you leave the bedroom for a while and calm your mind.

words.defJa: 相手の言ったことや前のことを受けて、「もしそうであるなら」という意味でつなぐ言葉。

cards.ja: 会議が長すぎるという不満は、どの職場でもよく聞かれる。ある会社の部長は、社員から「準備の時間が取れない」と訴えられ、それなら会議そのものを減らそうと決めた。定例の報告はチャットに切り替え、集まるのは判断が必要なときだけにした。半年後、残業時間は一割ほど減ったという。
cards.en: Complaints that meetings run too long are heard in every workplace. When staff told one department head that they could not find time to prepare, he decided that in that case he would cut the meetings themselves. Routine reports were moved to chat, and people gathered only when a decision was needed. Six months later, overtime had reportedly fallen by about ten percent.

words.meaning: that's too bad; I'm sorry to hear that (polite sympathy)
words.defJa: 相手の体の具合が悪いことや困ったことを聞いて、心配や同情を伝える丁寧な言い方。

cards.ja: 日本語の教科書には、相手が風邪をひいたと聞いたときの返事として「それはいけませんね」がよく載っている。直訳すれば「それはよくない」だが、相手を責めているわけではなく、気の毒に思う気持ちを伝える表現だ。実際の会話では、このあとに「大丈夫ですか」や「お大事に」と続けることが多い。ただ、やや改まった響きがあるので、親しい友人どうしなら「それは大変だね」と言うほうが自然だろう。
cards.en: Japanese textbooks often give 'That's not good, is it?' as the reply when you hear that someone has caught a cold. Taken literally it means 'that is not good,' but it does not blame the other person; it is an expression that conveys sympathy. In real conversation it is often followed by 'Are you all right?' or 'Take care of yourself.' It has a somewhat formal ring, though, so between close friends saying 'That must be rough' would probably sound more natural.
